II 
 
The Liquefied Petroleum Gas (Regulation of Use in Motor Vehicles) Order, 2001  
 
 
The Liquefied Petroleum Gas (Regulation of Use in M otor Vehicles) Order, 2001 
(Annexure I ) has been framed under the power conferred by Sect ion 3 of the Essential 
Commodities Act, 1955 ( Annexure II). This Order allows Government Oil Companies 
and Rated Parallel Marketeers to import (including Auto LPG import substitution), 
storage, distribution and selling AutoLPG for Autom otive purpose through Auto LPG 
Dispensing Stations to registered vehicles fitted w ith permanently fitted Auto LPG tanks 
and approved LPG conversion kits as notified by the  Ministry of Road Transport and 
Highways.  
 
2. The Committee took up the Liquefied Petroleum Gas (Regulation of Use in Motor 
Vehicles) Order, 2001 for detailed examination and a questionnaire on the subject matter 
was forwarded to the Ministry of Petroleum and Natu ral Gas for their 
comments/clarifications on the 10 
th  January, 2002. The Ministry furnished their 
comments on 1 st  April, 2002 ( Annexure III) . The points raised by the Committee and the 
comments/ clarifications received from the Ministry are reproduced below: 
 
(I) Para 2(b) gives the definition of consumer as f ollows: 
“Consumer” means a registered owner of a motor vehicle or a person having in his 
possession a motor vehicle or vehicle fitted with a n auto LPG tank, and a 
conversion kit as notified by the Government of Ind ia in the Ministry of Surface 
Transport, and runs such motor vehicle or vehicle b y using auto LPG as 
automotive fuel alone or with some other petroleum fuel” 
 
The Committee felt that the words “some other petro leum fuel” used in the Order 
had not been defined/ explained and sought to know whether there was any objection in 
defining or explaining the term in the Order itself.  
 
The Ministry clarified that the words “some other p etroleum fuel’ has already 
been covered by the Ministry of Surface Transport &  Highways in the Central Motor 

Vehicles (3 rd  Amendment) Rules, 2001 as notified on 24.04.2001  (Annexure IV).   As 
per para 2(d) of the said notification, “Vehicle sh all be capable of bi-fuel operation such 
as LPG and Petrol”. Thus, other petroleum fuel is p etrol (Motor spirit) and Auto LPG 
stand permitted for gasoline vehicles capable of bi -fuel operation.  The Ministry was of 
the view that if considered necessary, the words ‘a s notified by Ministry of Surface 
Transport & Highways may be added after the words ‘ with some other petroleum fuel’ in 
Liquefied Petroleum Gas (Regulation of Use in Motor Vehicles) Order, 2001.  
 
The Committee noted the facts as enumerated by the Ministry and 
recommends that the words ‘as notified by Ministry of Road Transport & 
Highways’ be added after the words ‘with some other  petroleum fuel’ in Liquefied 
Petroleum Gas (Regulation of Use in Motor Vehicles) Order, 2001. 
 
(II) Para 2: definitions 
The Committee observed that in every statute the de finitions are always placed 
alphabetically but in the said Order the definition s had not been put in alphabetical order.  
The Committee, accordingly, wanted to know the reas ons for deviating from the 
established practice. 
 
The Ministry agreed that the definitions in the Ord er had not been put in 
alphabetical order, and explained that they were so  placed in order to maintain a link 
among various terms defined in the order.  
 
(III)  Para 5(4) 
 Procurement, storage and sale of auto LPG by the au to LPG 
dispensing station dealer states that 
 
“No auto LPG dispensing station dealer shall keep t he auto LPG dispensing 
station premises including the storage point closed  during working hours on any 
day without the prior written permission of the Gov ernment Oil Company or a 
parallel marketeer” 
 

The Committee enquired as to whether the Ministry h ad any objection to 
prescribing that the permission so obtained may be displayed in order to avoid hardship 
to the consumers likely to arise due to unauthorized closure of dispensing station. 
 
The Ministry submitted that there was no objection to prescribe that the 
permissions obtained by Auto LPG Dispensing Station s (ALDS) for keeping the 
premises, including the storage points, closed duri ng working hours to be displayed to 
avoid hardship to the consumers likely to arise due  to closure of dispensing stations as 
suggested by the Committee and that the said instru ctions may be issued by the Ministry 
of Road Transport & Highways by an Administrative O rder to the Government Oil 
Marketing Companies/ Parallel Marketeers, who in tu rn would instruct their ALDS, or 
the Order may be amended. 
 
The Committee, accordingly, recommends that the Liq uefied Petroleum Gas 
(Regulation of Use in Motor Vehicles) Order, 2001 b e amended to incorporate that 
the permissions obtained by Auto LPG Dispensing Sta tions (ALDS) for keeping the 
premises, including the storage points, closed duri ng working hours to be displayed 
well in advance to avoid hardship to the consumers likely to arise due to closure of 
dispensing stations. 
 
(IV)  Para 6(1)(a):Assessment and certification rating of parallel Marketeers:- 
“No parallel marketer shall commence any activity, such as, import (including 
Auto LPG Import Substitution), transport, marketing , distribution, sale or any 
activity incidental thereto, relating to the busine ss of auto LPG to be used as 
automotive fuel without obtaining a minimum of low risk rating certificate, on the 
basis of evaluation and rating for his capability, infrastructure network and 
readiness to carry out professed business and deliv ery of good and services 
promised by him by an agency specified in Schedule-I. 
 
Provided that a parallel marketer carrying on the b usiness of transportation, 
marketing, distribution or selling of auto LPG for automotive fuel, as an agent of 
another parallel marketer, who has obtained a minim um of low risk rating 
certificate, shall not be required to obtain a rating certificate.”  
 

The Committee sought to know the objectives sought to be achieved by proviso 
and explanation to para 6(1)(a) of the Order. 
 
The Committee was informed that the objective for p roviding explanation to Para 
6(1)(a) of the Order was to clarify that the dealer s/agents appointed by the Parallel 
Marketeers for undertaking activities under Paralle l Marketing System (PMS) shall not 
be required to obtain the 'rating certificate' prov ided their principal 'Parallel Marketeer' 
had obtained the minimum of low risk rating certifi cate and had appointed dealers/agents 
through a legal instrument. 
 
(V)  Para 6(1)(b) -- Issue of rating certificate:-
 
 
"The rating certificate shall be issued in the form at as specified in Schedule -II 
and as per the forwarding letter given in Schedule- IV". 
 
It was enquired whether the procedure for obtaining  the rating certificate and a 
time frame in that behalf had been prescribed anywh ere, may be in the principal 
legislation, and if not, whether Government had any  objection in prescribing the same in 
the Order itself. 
 
The Ministry replied that as defined in Para 6(1)(a ) that since no parallel 
marketeer shall commence any activities relating to  the business of Auto LPG to be used 
as automotive fuel without obtaining a minimum of 'low risk' rating certificate, there is no 
need to define the time frame for obtaining the rat ing certificate as the Parallel 
Marketeers cannot commence any activity without obt aining a minimum low risk rating 
certificate. The para is based on similar para as i s applicable for issue of rating certificate 
in LPG (Regulation of Supply & Distribution) Order,  2000.  Further, the Ministry 
informed that no representation had so far been rec eived regarding any objection of 
undue delay for obtaining rating certificate. 
 
(VI) Para 6(4) (i):  Assessment and certification r ating of parallel Marketeers :
 
 
" There shall be paid in respect of every application to a rating agency- 
 

(i)  for the rating certificate awarded to the para llel marketeer, a fee at the rate of 
0.05% of the project cost, subject to a minimum of rupees fifty thousand  and 
maximum of rupees ten lakhs” 
 
The Committee felt that there was no mention in the  para about the mode or 
payment of fee and wanted to know whether the same could be provided in the Order 
itself.  Also, the fee appears to be on higher side  and whether there was any scope of 
reducing it. 
 
The Ministry replied that no need was felt to defin e the mode of payment under 
para 6(4)(i) as the same was governed by norms laid  down by Reserve Bank of India/ 
Ministry of Finance, and mutual agreement with the parties. Further, the fees as defined 
in the above para was retained at the same level as  was applicable for obtaining rating 
certificate by the parallel marketeers for marketin g of LPG as per Liquefied Petroleum 
Gas (Regulation of Supply & Distribution) Order, 19 93 and subsequent Liquefied 
Petroleum Gas (Regulation of Supply & Distribution)  Order, 2000.  The Ministry further 
submitted that since they had not received any repr esentation objecting to the said level 
of fees for obtaining rating certificate, no need was felt to review the same. 
 
The Committee feels that just because no representa tion on the fees has been 
received, it does not mean that efforts should not be made to bring the fees in 
consonance with the Market forces. The Committee, therefore, recommends that the 
Ministry should review and, accordingly, revise the  fee periodically after making an 
assessment of the market conditions and the need to  protect the interest of the 
consumers. 
 
(VII)  Para 8(3) Maintenance of records and furnishing of information by parallel 
marketeers  - 
 
 
"Every parallel marketer shall furnish to the Minis try of Petroleum and Natural 
Gas, or to such authority as may be specified by th e Central Government, such 
information as may be required" 
 

The Committee felt that the words "to such authorit y as may be specified by the 
Central Government" were vague and wanted to know w hether the Ministry had any 
objection in qualifying the authorities contemplate d in the said para.  Also, the 
Committee felt that the provision appears to be gen eral giving wide discretion to the 
Ministry of Petroleum & Natural Gas or any authorit y which may lead to undue 
harassment and sought to know whether it was possib le to anticipate the information 
required and prescribe the same in the Order itself. 
 
The Ministry replied that the petroleum industry wa s passing through a transition 
period of dismantling of APM and that an Authority may be notified in the near future.  
Regarding Committee’s apprehension on discretionary  powers and undue harassment by 
the Ministry or the authority, the Ministry submitt ed that Paras 8(1) and 8(2) prescribe 
the information required from parallel marketeers 
The Committee considered the comments of the Minist ry and was of the opinion 
that the Ministry’s reply that paras 8(1) and 8(2) prescribe the information required from 
the parallel marketeers was not convincing because if this was the only information 
required from the parallel marketeers, there should  have been no necessity of prescribing 
in para 8(3) calling for “such information as may be required” from parallel marketeers. 
 
The Ministry clarified that apart from the informat ion to be provided by the 
parallel marketeers as per para 8(1) & (2), it may be required in future to call for the 
information from them such as investment details, s pecification of the product being 
imported/marketed by them, details of their marketi ng network etc. Therefore, provision 
to call for such other information has been include d in the Control Order in para 8(3). 
Such a provision exists in LPG (Regulation of Supply and Distribution) Order, 2000 also. 
 
(VIII)  Para 11  - Power to exempt  
 
"The Central Government may, if it considers necess ary, for avoiding any 
hardship or in consideration of public interest by notification in the Official 
Gazette, exempt any person or class of persons from  all or any of the provisions 
of this Order, either generally or for any specific  purpose, subject to such 
conditions as may be specified in the notification." 

 
The Committee was of the opinion that the provision  gave the Central 
Government power to exempt any person or class of p ersons from all or any of the 
provisions of this Order. The Committee, accordingl y, sought to know the justification 
for providing such exemption, the circumstances con templated to be in public interest, 
and, whether it was possible to enumerate them in the Order itself so as to be indicative. 
 
 
The Ministry clarified that Para 11 had been added in the order to take care of any 
exigencies/extra ordinary situation to avoid hardship or in consideration of public interest 
which may arise during the course of marketing Auto  LPG and which was not possible to 
anticipate/enumerate in the order. However, such ex emptions were to be notified in the 
official Gazette as per the provision of the Order. 
 
The Committee considered the comments of the Minist ry.  It was of the view that 
notification in the Official Gazette does not seem to be a sufficient safeguard or a 
justification for provisions of para 11 which autho rizes the Central Government to 
exempt any person from all or any of the provisions  of the Order either generally or for 
any specific purpose and sought to know whether it was possible to prescribe some 
guidelines for invoking provisions of para 11. 
 
The Ministry informed the Committee that the Centra l Government would 
examine critically before exempting any person from  all or any of the provisions of the 
Control Order. Such exemption may be required to be  given depending upon the 
circumstances prevailing at any point of time. Ther efore, specific guidelines for invoking 
the provisions of para 11 cannot be visualized in advance. Such a provision exists in LPG 
(Regulation of Supply and Distribution) Order, 2000 also. 
 
The Committee while accepting the views of the Mini stry was of the opinion 
that  since the Ministry already had the experience  of the implementation of the 
LPG (Regulation of Supply and Distribution) Order, 2000, hence, some basic 

guidelines for invoking para 11 should be framed by  them. This would help check 
arbitrariness and help in deciding cases in which exemptions could be granted .  
 
(IX)  The Committee raised a query that although penalti es of the nature of fine, etc. 
might be provided under the Essential Commodities A ct for violation of any provisions 
of the Order but, the penalties of other nature lik e cancellation of dealership, etc, or other 
deterrent actions for the purpose of ensuring stric t compliance of the provisions of the 
Order could be provided in the Order itself.  The C ommittee sought to know the views of 
the Ministry in this regard. 
 
The Ministry informed the Committee that penalties like cancellation of 
dealership etc. are covered separately in the 'Deal ership Agreement' which the 
Government oil companies/parallel Marketeers were e ntering into with their 
Dealers/Agents. The penalties for violation of any provisions of the Order are as laid 
down in the Essential Commodities Act itself. In fa ct, in appropriate cases there is 
provision for imprisonment also under Essential Com modities Act, which is harsher than 
cancellation of dealership. 
 
The Committee noted the Ministry’s reply and sought  clarification as to whether 
control over the dealers/agents would not be more e ffective if the penalties, which 
presently find place in the dealership agreement, a re incorporated in the Order itself.  
Also, would it not be obligatory on the part of the authorities to take action in that case.  
 
The Ministry explained that in the decontrolled reg ime, it would not be 
appropriate for the Government to notify penalties.  In order to protect their market share 
and survive in the competitive environment, oil com panies are expected to exercise 
control over their dealers as per the dealership ag reements concluded between them/any 
other guidelines such as Marketing Discipline Guide lines (MDG). Presently, oil 
companies take action against erring dealers as per  the MDG/dealership agreements. 
Further, enforcement agencies take action under the  provisions of the Essential 
Commodities Act, 1955.  
 

The Committee accepted the comments of the Ministry  but were of the 
opinion that the principles on the basis of which t he Marketing Discipline 
Guidelines are framed and the standard clauses incl uded in the dealership 
agreements should be incorporated in the Rules itse lf to bring transparency which 
would also provide Statutory backing to them. The C ommittee, therefore, 
recommends that the Rules may, accordingly, be amended to incorporate the same.  
 
3. The Committee, thereafter, discussed the said Or der with the State Government of 
West Bengal, Indian Oil Corporation, Indo-Burma Petroleum Company Ltd. and Ministry 
of Petroleum & Natural Gas at Kolkatta on 27 
th  October, 2004. A study note (Annexure 
V) on the said visit was forwarded to the Ministry o f Petroleum & Natural Gas for their 
comments/clarifications.  The comments/ clarifications received from the Ministry on the 
issues raised are placed at Annexure VI. On perusal of the comments furnished by the 
Ministry, the Committee recommends that  regarding para 6(1)(b) a time limit for 
issue of rating certificate be incorporated in the Order.  Also, the Committee feels 
that the status of the application should be put up  on the website of the Ministry so 
as to ensure transparency.   
 
4. The Committee also had discussion on the said Or der with the State Government 
of Maharashtra along with Indian Oil Corporation, H industan Petroleum Corporation 
Limited, Bharat Petroleum Corporation Limited and M inistry of Petroleum & Natural 
Gas at Mumbai on 1 
st  August, 2008. The Committee was informed that in o rder to stop 
the diversion of LPG cylinders, the Government had enacted “Liquefied Petroleum Gas 
(Regulation of Supply and Distribution) Order, 2000 ” and formulated “Marketing 
Discipline Guidelines, 2001” which provides for pen al action against LPG distributors 
indulging in diversion of LPG. It was also informed  that State Governments were also 
empowered to take action against diversion of domes tic LPG. Similarly, the Weights and 
Measures Departments of the States/UTs initiate leg al action against those LPG 
distributors found diverting LPG cylinders.A brief Note on the issues raised by the 
Committee along with the comments of the Ministry o f Petroleum & Natural Gas is 
enclosed ( Annexure VII).  

5. The Order was also taken up for discussion with the State Government of Tamil 
Nadu, Ministry of Petroleum & Natural and the Oil M arketing Companies at Chennai on 
17 th  September, 2008.  The Committee was apprised that Section 7 of the Essential 
Commodities Act, 1955 provides for prosecution and imposition of fine and that most of 
the cases of violation in Tamil Nadu is of Black Ma rketing. The Committee was further 
apprised that detection of adulteration was done by marker system and transportation was 
tracked through the GPS-tracking system installed i n oil tankers. It was also informed 
that 100 percent GPS based tracking system was to b e achieved in HPCL by 2010. The 
Committee was of the opinion that detention period of six months in Black Marketing 
Act should be increased to one year to make it stringent enough to act as a deterrent.  The 
Committee further insisted that Oil companies shoul d not depend on the State 
Government and make sure that the pilferage is not taking place. A study note of the said 
discussion is enclosed ( Annexure VIII). 
 
6.    The Committee is hopeful that the Ministry would ca rry out the 
recommendations  of the Committee expeditiously und er intimation to it. The 
Committee is also of the opinion that proper monito ring and inspections are 
essential for the proper implementation of the Orde r and stresses upon the Ministry 
to strengthen its enforcement mechanism to ensure t hat the objectives of the Order 
are achieved.

The Committee feels that just because no representa tion on the fees has been

opinion that the principles on the basis of which t he Marketing Discipline 
Guidelines are framed and the standard clauses incl uded in the dealership 
agreements should be incorporated in the Rules itse lf to bring transparency which 
would also provide Statutory backing to them. The C ommittee, therefore, 
recommends that the Rules may, accordingly, be amended to incorporate the same.  
 

12. The Committee recommends that  regarding para 6(1)(b) a time limit for 
issue of rating certificate be incorporated in the Order.  Also, the Committee feels

as to ensure transparency.   
 
13. The Committee is hopeful that the Ministry woul d carry out the 
recommendations  of the Committee expeditiously und er intimation to it. The 
Committee is also of the opinion that proper monito ring and inspections are 
essential for the proper implementation of the Orde r and stresses upon the Ministry

2. While scrutinizing these Orders, the Committee note d in some cases 
considerable time lag between their notifications a nd laying. The annexed 
statement also indicates the period of delay in cas es where notifications have 
not been laid as per the schedule prescribed by the  Committee. It also shows 
notifications not accompanied by a statement indica ting the reasons for the 
delay. The observations/recommendations of the Comm ittee in respect of the 
specific Ministries/Departments are as follows: -  
 
 
 
 
 
 

 
(i) Ministry of Civil Aviation 
 
 Ministry of Civil Aviation  have laid only one Not ification (Sl. No. 10) 
which has been delayed by 9 months and is accompani ed with delay statement. 
The reason given by the Ministry for delay is as under:- 
 
 “Though the Notification was published on 26 
th  November, 2011, 
however due to late receipt of printed copies of No tification in the Ministry, 
the approval of the Hon’ble Ministry of Civil Aviation could not be obtained in 
time for laying on the Table of the House in the Bu dget Session. Hence there 
was administrative delay in laying on the Table of the Rajya Sabha, the papers 
relating to G.S.R. 323 regarding amendment to the R ule 24 of the Aircraft Act, 
1937.” 
    
   The Committee take serious note of such a long dela y as 9 months 
and find the reasons of delay given by the Ministry  unconvincing and 
evasive. In view of the fact that this is a statuto ry obligation to lay the 
notifications/orders/rules on the Table of the Hous e in time, the situation 
should have been assessed well before and adequate arrangements were 
made in respect thereof. The Committee advise the M inistry of Civil 
Aviation to take precaution in future so that such delays do not recur and 
time schedule prescribed in Committee’s 131 
st  Report be strictly adhared 
to. 
 
(ii) Ministry of Commerce and Industry 
 (Department of Commerce) 
 
 Ministry of Commerce and Industry (Department of C ommerce)  have 
laid 5 Notifications (Sl. Nos. 12 to 16) during the  Session. Out of these 2 
Notifications (Sl. Nos. 13 – 14) have been delayed by 5 months and no delay 
statement is attached to both of delayed Notifications.  
 
   
The Committee take serious note of the delay in lay ing of 
Notifications by the Ministry of Commerce and Indus try (Department of 
Commerce). Further, there is no delay statement att ached to any of these 
Notifications. This is defiance of Committee’s reco mmendation contained 
in its 135 
th  Report which requires concerned Ministries/Departm ents to 
invariable append delay statement with the Notifica tion being laid so as to 
apprise Parliament of the causes of delay. The Comm ittee desire that the 
Ministry of Commerce and Industry should invariably  append delay 
statement in case of any delay actually taking plac e in laying of 
notifications and avoid recurrence of such delay in future. 
  
 
 

 
 
 
(iii)  Ministry of Communication and Information Te chnology 
 (Department of Telecommunications) 
 
Ministry of Communication and Information Technolog y (Department 
of Telecommunications) have laid 14 Notifications ( Sl. Nos. 24 to 37). Out of 
these, 5 Notifications have been delayed. The delay  period ranges from 4 
months to 6 months. One delayed Notification (Sl. N o. 24) has no delay 
statement attached with it while other 4 Notificati ons (Sl. Nos. 26 to 29) are 
appended with delay statement. The reasons given by  the Ministry for the said 
delay is reproduced as under:-  
 
“The Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) i s a statutory 
body set up under the Telecom Regulatory Authority of India Act, 1997. In 
exercise of the powers conferred upon it under sect ion 36 of the TRAI Act, 
1997, the Authority may, by notification, make regu lations consistent with the 
Act and the Rules made there under to carry out the purposes of the Act. Under 
section 37 of the Act, the regulations notified by TRAI are required to be laid 
before each House of Parliament. 
The Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) in  exercise of the 
powers conferred by Section 36 read with sub-clause s (vii) of clause (b) of 
sub-section (1) and clause (c) of sub-section (1) o f section 11 of the TRAI Act, 
1997 notified these regulations were given for printing to Government Press on 
the same day they were issued. In spite of pursuing  with the concerned 
officials of Government of India Press, the Gazette  of India notified copies of 
the regulations were received by TRAI form the Gove rnment of India Press on 
7
th  May, 2012. The Budget Session of Parliament ended on 22 nd  May, 2012 
with last day allotted for Ministry of Communicatio n & IT being 18 th  May, 
2012. Hence the time available for laying these reg ulations in the Parliament 
was less than 15 days and the regulations could not  be laid on the Table of the 
Rajya Sabha during the Budget Session 2012 of Parliament.” 
 
The Committee notes with concern the delay of four to six months 
in laying of the Notifications mainly due to late r eceipt of printed copies 
from Government of India Press and time taken in co mpleting the 
procedural formalities in the Ministry of Communication and Information 
Technology (Department of Telecommunications). In t his context the 
Committee observes that it is the Ministry’s respon sibility to ensure that 
the Notifications are laid before the Parliament wi thin the prescribed time 
schedule and accordingly, it is for the Ministry on ly to ensure that they 
receive the same timely from the statutory bodies u nder them and 
complete all formalities of laying well before the House is adjourned. As 
for time availability being less than 15 days, it m ay be stated that had the 
Ministry been prompt, the Notifications could well have been laid even on 
the last day of the Session with the consent of the  concerned Minister. The 

 
Committee recommends that the Department of Telecom munications may 
take necessary remedial measures to ensure that pap ers are laid well in 
time  on the Table of the House. It is also impress ed upon that all those 
Notifications which have been delayed should invari ably be accompanied 
with delay statements.  
 
(iv) Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution  
 (Department of Food and Public Distribution) 
 
 Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distr ibution 
(Department of Food and Public Distribution) have l aid 8 Notifications (Sl. 
Nos. 41 to 48). Out of these 5 Notifications (Sl. Nos. 41-45) have been delayed 
by 5 to 6 months. All of these delayed Notification s have been accompanied 
with a delay statement. The reasons for delay given  by the Ministry is as 
under:- 
 
 “Delay in laying the regulations on the table of b oth the Houses of 
Parliament is due to the reason that the WDRA becam e operational only on 
25 
th  October, 2010 and the appointments were made for t he posts of the 
Chairman on 27 th  October, 2010 and Members made on 1 st  November, 2010 
and on 1 st  February, 2011 respectively. The Warehousing (Deve lopment & 
Regulations) Act, 2007 required the approval of the  WDRA Advisory 
Committee and the Central Government for all the Re gulations framed under 
the Act. The Committee was constituted on 26 th  October, 2010. The draft 
regulations were approved by the Committee on 13 th  January, 2011. The 
Competent Authority approved the same on 7 th  September, 2011 and 16 th  
February, 2012. It also took long time in vetting a ll the draft regulations and 
their Hindi translations from the Official Language  Wing of the Ministry of 
Law and Justice, and hence, the resultant delay whi ch may kindly be 
condoned.” 
 
 The Committee do not approve the reasons given by the Ministry 
of Consumer Affairs for delay in tabling of Notific ations. The Committee 
further observe that there was sufficient time with the Ministry during the 
Budget Session as the three Notifications were publ ished well before the 
Session and other two Notifications were published during the first half of 
the Budget Session. The Committee further hopes tha t Ministry in such 
cases would strive to keep the delay to the minimum  and should take care 
that Notifications are laid on the Table of the Hou se at the first available 
opportunity after publication of Notifications. 
 
(v) Ministry of Corporate Affairs 
 
 Ministry of Corporate Affairs have laid 28 Notific ations (Sl. Nos. 49 to 
76).  Out of these 9 Notifications have been delaye d from 4 months to 18 
months. Eight (8) Notifications (Sl. Nos. 53-55, an d 59-63) have been attached 

 
with delay statement and other Notification (Sl. No. 57) has no delay statement 
attached to it. The reasons of delay given by the Ministry are as under:- 
 
 “In exercise of powers conferred by sub-section (3 ) of Section 20 of the 
Competition Act, this Ministry had enhanced the val ue of assets and the value 
of turnover, by 50% for the purpose of Section 5 of  the said Act vide 
notification No. S.O. 480 (E) dated 04.03.2011. 
 Similarly, in exercise of powers conferred by clau se (a) of Section 54 
of the Competition Act, this Ministry in public int erest vide notification No. 
S.O. 481(E) dated 04.03.2011 exempted the “Group” e xercising less than 50% 
of voting rights in other enterprises from the provisions of Section 5 of the Act, 
for a period of 5 years and also exempted an enterp rise, whose control shares, 
voting rights or assets being acquired has assets o f the value of not more than 
Rs. 250 crores or turnover of not more than Rs. 750  crores from the provisions 
of Section 5 of the Competition Act for a period of  5 years vide notification 
No. S.O. 482(E) dated 04.03.2011. 
 The notification dated 04.03.2011 relating to exem pting an enterprise 
whose control, shares, voting rights or assets bein g acquired has assets of the 
value of not more than Rs. 250 crores or turnover o f not more than Rs. 750 
crores was subsequently amended vide notification S .O. 1218(E) dated 
27.05.2011. 
 The above said notification is still under conside ration for further 
amendment continuously from the date of its notific ation in view of the 
concerns expressed by Competition Commission of India. 
 In view of the above, the above said notifications  could not be laid in 
time on the table of both the House of Parliament a s provided by sub-section 
(3) of Section 63 of the Competition Act.” 
 
The Committee is not happy with the inordinate dela y in laying  of 
papers on the Table of the House. The reason given by the Ministry of 
Corporate Affairs that the notification could not b e laid down because of 
the amendments taking place during the period is no t convincing. The 
notifications nos. S.O. 480, 481 and 482 dated 04.03.2011 should have been 
laid in time without waiting for amendments. As it is a Constitutional 
provision to lay the notifications within a prescri bed time schedule, the 
Ministry should have taken appropriate action to la y the same on the 
Table of the House. The Notification no. S.O. 1218( E)/dated 27/5/2011 
should have followed later. The Committee, therefor e, recommends that 
adequate precaution should be exercised to avoid re currence of such 
instances in future. 
 
(vi) Defence 
 
The only Notification that the Ministry of Defence (Sl. No. 77) have 
laid is delayed by 5 months with delay statement ap pended thereto. The 
reasons for delay given by the Ministry are as under:- 

 
 
 “The Amendments to Rules 71, 73, 108 and 129 of AF Rules, 1969 
were sent to the Government of India Press for publ ication in the Official 
Gazette of India on 31.03.2012. It took some time t o get the published copies 
of Notification from the Government of India Press.  The sitting of the Tenth 
Session of Fifteenth Lok Sabha and Two Hundred Twen ty Five Session of the 
Rajya Sabha concluded on 22 
nd  May, 2012. As such, the Notification could not 
be laid during aforesaid Session of Parliament, 2012. 
 The delay in laying of papers on the Table of Lok Sabha/Rajya Sabha is 
due to delay in getting published copies of the Not ification. It is requested that 
the marginal delay on the part of Ministry of Defen ce may kindly be 
condoned”. 
 
 The Committee would like to impress upon the Ministry of Defence 
that it is their responsibility to ensure that copi es of the Notifications are 
received timely from the Government of India Press and for this purpose 
they may evolve a suitable mechanism of check/count er check so that such 
instances do not recur.  The Committee hopes that M inistry of Defence 
would take action accordingly in order to comply wi th the prescribed 
schedule in the matter of laying of statutory Notifications . 
 
(vii) Ministry of Environment and Forests 
 
Ministry of Environment and Forests have laid 11 No tifications (Sl. 
Nos. 78 to 88)on the Table of the House.  Out of 9 Notifications which have 
been delayed, 6 Notifications (Sl. Nos. 83 to 88) h ave been delayed from 4 
months to 8 months and have no delay statement atta ched to any of these 
Notifications. Other 3 Notifications (Sl. Nos. 80 to 82) have been delayed from 
9 months to 11 months and accompanied with a delay statement. The Ministry 
have given reason for delay as non-availability of requisite number of printed 
copies from the Press in time. The reasons for dela y given by the Ministry are 
as under:- 
 
 “Delay was caused due to non-receipt of publication  and also due to 
pending decision on requirement of laying the Notif ication on the Table of the 
House”. 
 
The Committee are not convinced by the reason given  for delay by 
the Ministry that the printed copies of Gazette Not ifications could not be 
made available in time. Ministry should have mentio ned the date when 
printed copies were to be given to it by the Govern ment of India Press as 
also the efforts made by it to get the printing exp edited. Delay could have 
been avoided, had adequate precaution been taken by  the Ministry to 
expedite decision in the matter. The Committee feel   that the Ministry of 
Environment and Forests did not take it with requir ed seriousness. Such 
delays in future, particularly on account of delay in receiving printed 

 
copies of notifications will not be acceptable to t he Committee. Ministry 
would have to adhere to the time schedule for notifying as well as laying of 
papers as prescribed in Committee’s 131 
st  Report. 
 
(viii)  Ministry of Finance 
 (a)  (Department of Economic Affairs) 
 
Ministry of Finance (Department of Economic Affairs ) have laid 10 
Notifications (Sl. Nos. 89 to 98) during the Sessio n. Out of these, only one 
Notification (Sl. No. 89) has been delayed by 5 mon ths and has no delay 
statement appended to it. 
 
The Committee take a serious view not only about th e delay in 
laying of one of its Notifications on the Table of the House but also failure 
to append the delay statement with it. The Ministry /Department must 
ensure to append a delay statement in all such case s in future so as to 
apprise the Parliament of the reasons of delay . 
 
 (b)     (Department of Financial Services)  
 
 The Ministry of Finance (Department of Financial S ervices) have laid 6 
Notifications (Sl. Nos. 99 to 104) on the Table of the House.  Out of which 3 
Notifications (Sl. Nos. 99 – 100 and 102) have been  delayed from 4 months to 
17 months and have been accompanied with a delay st atement. The reasons 
given by the Ministry are as under:- 
 
“Copies of the Gazette Notification G.S.R. 276(E), dated 31 
st  March, 2011 
published in Part II Section 3 Sub-section (i) of E xtraordinary Gazette of India 
containing notification regarding the Securitisatio n and Reconstruction of 
financial Assets and Enforcement of Security Interest (Central Registry) Rules, 
2011, could not be placed on the table of Lok Sabha  owing to the fact that two 
more notifications were published in Part II-Sectio n 3 sub-section (i) on the 
same date-G.S.R. 277 (E) and G.S.R. 278 (E) for est ablishment of CERSAI at 
Rajendra Place, New Delhi and appointment of Sh. RV  Verma as Central 
Registrar of CERSAI under Sections 20 and 21 of the  Securitisation and 
Reconstruction of Financial Assets & Enforcement of  Security Interest Act, 
2002 (54 of 2002) respectively. However, a mistake was observed in GSR 277 
(E) as it was published in exercise of powers confe rred ‘under Section 21’ of 
SARFAESI Act, 2002 instead of ‘under section 20’ in  English version. The 
mistake was later got rectified by mooting one more notification”.  
  
The Committee has noted the reply given by the Mini stry of 
Finance (Department of Financial Services) regardin g  laying of 
Notifications on the Table of the House The Committ ee hopes that 
concerned organization will keep  itself vigilant a nd ensure that such 

 
things would not be repeated again in future. The M inistry of Finance 
(Department of Financial Services)  should in futur e ensure that all its 
papers were laid before the House as prescribed in the Committee’s 131 
st  
Report. The Ministry should also endeavour to avoid  such recurrence of 
delay in future. 
 
 (c)   (Department of Revenue) 
 
 During the session the Ministry of Finance (Depart ment of Revenue) 
have laid 123 Notifications (Sl. Nos. 105 to 227). Out of these 11 Notifications 
have been delayed. The delay period ranges from 4 m onths to 5 months. Only 
6 Notifications (Sl. nos.106 to 111) have delay sta tement appended to them.No 
delay statement has been appended with 5 Notifications (Sl. Nos. 126-128, 166 
and 182)). The reasons of delay  given by the Minis try is that the Notifications 
could not be laid on the Table of the House due to late receipt of printed copies 
of the Notifications by the Ministry. 
 
The Committee appreciates the hard work put in by t he Ministry 
of Finance (Department of Revenue) in laying of fai rly large number of 
Notifications on the Table of the House in time and  keeping the delay in 
laying the Notifications to the minimum.  However, the Committee takes 
strong exception to the Ministry’s failure to lay t he delay statement. The 
Committee in the absence of delay statements are no t able to know the 
reasons behind this delay. Therefore, the Committee invites attention to its 
recommendation contained in its 135 
th  Report  in this connection wherein 
it has been emphasized to append invariably delay s tatement in case of 
delay in laying of notifications by  the Ministry. The Ministry of Finance 
(Department of Revenue) should also endeavour to av oid recurrence of 
such delays in future. 
 
(ix) Ministry of Human Resource Development 
  (Department of Higher Education)  
 
  The Ministry of Human Resource Development (Depar tment of 
Higher Education) have laid 5 Notifications (Sl. No s. 259 to 263). Three of 
these Notifications (Sl. Nos. 259-261) have been de layed by  5 months to 6 
months and are accompanied with delay statement. Th e reasons given by the 
Ministry are as follows:- 
 
 “National Commission for Minority Educational Inst itutions (Financial and 
Administrative Powers) Amendment Rules, 2012 was is sued on 23 
rd  February, 
2012 and the Gazette Notification was received on 1 st  May, 2012. There has 
been an inadvertent delay in laying the Rule before Parliament”. 
    
The Committee are deeply anguished over the fact th at such delay 
was caused inadvertently by the Ministry. The Minis try should have kept 

 
vigilant to see that notifications are laid within the time schedule 
prescribed by the Committee. The Committee, therefo re, impress upon 
the Ministry of Human Resource Development (Departm ent of Higher 
Education) to be watchful so that laying is not delayed inadvertently. 
 
(x) Ministry of Micro,Small and Medium Enterprises  
  
The Ministry of Micro,Small and Medium Enterprises have laid only 
one  Notification (Sl. Nos. 274) during the Session  which has been delayed by 
5 months and moreover no delay statement has been appended to it.  
 
The Committee invite attention to its recommendatio ns made in 
135 
th  Report wherein it is laid down that it is essentia l to append a delay 
statement in case of delay in laying of statutory o rders. The committee, 
therefore, impresses upon the Ministry of Micro, Sm all and Medium 
Enterprises to strictly adhere to the time schedule  in laying of 
Notifications and should append delay statement in case of any delay .  
 
(xi)  Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions 
(Department of Personnel and Training) 
 
Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensio ns (Department of 
Personnel and Training) have laid 7 Notifications ( Sl. Nos. 276 to 282)on the 
Table of the House.  Out of which 2 Notifications ( Sl. Nos. 276 to 277) have 
been delayed by 3 months each and have no delay sta tement attached to any of 
these Notifications. 
  
The Committee hopes that  the Ministry of Personnel , Public 
Grievances and Pensions (Department of Personnel an d Training) would 
avoid such delays and would append a delay statemen t in all such cases of 
delay in future.  
 
(xii) Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas 
 
Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas have laid 4 N otifications (Sl. 
Nos. 283 to 286) on the Table of the House.  Out of  total 4 Notifications 2  
Notifications (Sl. Nos. 283 and 286) have been dela yed by 4 and 5 months 
respectively and no delay statement has been attach ed to any of these 
Notifications.  
 
The Committee takes strong view of the delay occurr ed in tabling 
the Notifications in time and hope that the Ministr y would avoid such 
instances of delay in laying of Subordinate Legisla tion in future. The 
Committee also impress upon the Ministry to take no te of the fact that in 
case there is a delay in the laying of any Statutor y Notification, the same 
should be accompanied by a delay statement while it is being laid . 

 
 
(xiii) Ministry of  Power 
 
The Ministry of Power have laid 3 Notifications (Sl. No. 287 - 289) and 
out of which 2 Notifications (Sl. Nos. 287-288) have been delayed by 5 months 
each. Moreover, no delay statement has been appende d to any of these delayed 
Notifications.  
 
The Committee take serious note for delay of laying  of 
Notifications in time on the Table of the House and  advise the Ministry of 
Power to take necessary steps to obviate such delay s and remove lacuna, if 
any in the system. The Committee also impress upon the Ministry to take 
note of the fact that in case there is a delay in t he laying of any Statutory 
Notifications, the same should be accompanied by a delay statement while 
it is being laid . The Committee also advises the Ministry to avoid 
recurrence of such delays in future. 
  
(xiv) Ministry of Road Transport and Highways 
 
The Ministry of Road Transport and Highways have la id 84 
Notifications (Sl. Nos. 293-376). There has been si gnificant number of 
Notifications which have been delayed. Out of 69 de layed Notifications, none 
of them have been attached with delay statement . T he delay period ranges 
from 5 Months to 22 months. In 51 cases, Notificati ons have been delayed 
ranging from 12 months to 22 months.  
 
The Committee is not happy over such large number o f delayed 
Notifications. This is just not acceptable to the C ommittee that 69 out of 
84 Notifications delayed did not have the delay sta tements, delay period 
being more than 12 months to 22 months in the case of majority  of 
Notifications laid. While there may be a reason for  the delay, but there 
cannot be any reason for not furnishing reason for that. The Ministry 
must understand the implications for not doing so a nd moreover in such a 
large number of cases. 
 
 
(xv) Ministry of Textiles 
 
The Ministry of Textiles  have laid 5 Notifications  (Sl. Nos. 378-382) out of 
which 4 Notifications (Sl. Nos. 378, 379, 380 & 381 ) have been delayed by 5 
months to 10 months. Three Notifications (Sl. Nos. 378, 379 & 381) have no

delay statement appended to it. The reason of delay  given therein is that the 
Notifications could not be laid on the Table of the  House in time due to 
oversight.  
 

 
The Committee cannot accept the reply given by the Ministry of 
Textiles that the Notifications could not be laid on time due to oversight. It 
only reflects the lack of seriousness in the Minist ry in fulfilling its 
constitutional responsibility to Parliament. The Co mmittee hopes the 
Ministry to be more careful about laying of its papers and see that persons 
responsible for this remain vigilant about it.  
 
3. Rules/Regulations/Orders/bye-laws are laid by di fferent Ministries on 
the Table of the House under various provisions of parent Acts passed by 
Parliament. These Rules/Regulations/Orders/bye-laws  are published in the 
official Gazette before being laid on the Table of the House. Even after they 
are laid, it is very difficult to get access to the se notifications. The Committee 
recommends that such Rules/Regulations/Orders, etc.  laid on the Table of 
the House should be invariably uploaded on the webs ites of respective 
Ministries immediately on the same day when they ha ve been laid on the 
Table of the House, for information of Members of P arliament and people 
at large for their easy access .  
 
 
4.   Committee impresses upon all the Ministries/De partments to take 
immediate steps to ensure timely and proper laying of subordinate legislation. 
The Committee, accordingly, wishes to bring to the notice of all 
Ministries/Departments of the Government of India, particularly, the defaulting 
ones, the following recommendations, as contained i n its 131 
st 
, 135 
th 
, 152 
nd    
and 192 nd  Reports: 
 
 “Orders required to be laid before the House shoul d be laid (i) if the 
House is not in Session, during the Session immedia tely following the date 
of publication of the Order in the Official Gazette  and (ii) if the House is 
in Session, on the date of the publication of the O rder, during its 
continuance and in case the time lag between the da te of publication and 
the date of the closing of the Session is less than  15 clear days, before the 
expiry of the Session immediately following the sai d Session. All the 
Ministries/Departments of Government of India shoul d henceforth 
comply with this schedule in the matter of laying o f the Orders issued 
under various Acts of Parliament on the Table of the Rajya Sabha. 
(131 st  Report) 
(Presented on 15 December 2000) 
 
 
 
 
 

 
 “The Committee has, time and again, emphasized tha t it is essential 
that in case there is a delay in the laying of Stat utory Orders, the 
concerned Ministry/Department should invariably app end a delay 
statement along with the notifications being laid s o as to apprise 
Parliament of the causes of delay. The Committee de sires all 
Ministries/Departments to take a note of this, sinc e the intension is that 
through the process of formulation of a delay state ment the Ministry is 
able to introspect, identify bottlenecks and devise remedial measures”. 
(135 th  Report) 
(Presented on 27 July 2001) 
 
 “In the opinion of the Committee, every notificati on should be 
assigned a distinctive number in order to give it a  separate identity and 
similarly, no notification should be published/laid  which does not carry a 
notification number. The Committee expects all Mini stries/Departments 
of Government of India to exercise caution in this regard. In case where 
there are more than one notification under a single  file, the 
Ministries/Departments should ensure that the file number on each 
notification should be suitably distinguished from one another.” 
(152 
nd 
 Report) 
(Presented on 26 August 2004)  
 
 “In addition to the concern expressed by the Commi ttee over delay 
in laying of Notifications on the Table of the Hous e, the Committee also 
express their deep concern over delay in framing of  rules/regulations 
under different Acts. The Committee in its 47 
th  report presented to the 
House on 14.9.1981 has recommended that the rule-ma king process 
should be completed within a period of six months of the coming into force 
on an Act. The committee has further recommended th at in case a 
Ministry is not able to adhere to this time limit, it should seek extension of 
time for completing the rule-making process. The re commendation of the 
committee reads as follows:- 
 
  “The Committee feels that the rule-making process c ould 
well have been completed within the time limit of s ix months which 
the Committee has laid down for making of rules under an Act after 
coming into force of that Act. Where however, a Min istry does not 
find it possible to adhere to the time limit, they should inform the 
Committee of the reasons why they cannot make rules  within the 
time limit and seek extension of time for completin g the rule-
making process.” 
 
 The Committee is constrained to take note of the f act that the 
Ministries/Departments of Government of India are n ot complying with 
the Committee’s recommendation to complete the proc ess of framing of 

 
subordinate legislation contemplated under various Acts of Parliament 
within a period of six months. At the same time, th e Committee also does 
not receive requests for extension of time for comp leting the rule-making 
process in terms of its recommendations as above fr om most of the 
Ministries/Departments. The committee takes a serio us note of the 
prevailing situation in which the Ministries/Depart ments are neither able 
to complete the task of framing rules/regulations u nder different Acts 
within the given six months’ period nor do they suo-motu  approach the 
Committee for seeking extension of time. The Commit tee further notes

respect of all legislations brought about by differ ent 
Ministries/Departments of Government of India from the year 2003

is not delayed. The Committee, however, finds that the responses from the

undertaken on behalf of the Committee. 
  
 In view of the above position, the Committee once again reiterates 
its recommendation that the Ministries/Departments should ensure 
putting in place subordinate legislation positively  within a period of six 
months of coming into force of the Act. The Committ ee further 
recommends that in case the Ministry fails to meet with this deadline, they 
should invariably approach the Committee for seekin g extension of time. 
The Committee further recommends that in cases wher e the time limit of 
six months is not adhered to, they should, while la ying rules/regulations 
before the Parliament invariably lay a statement ex plaining the reasons 
why the framing of rules/regulations was delayed be yond six months so as 
to keep the Parliament apprised of the compliance o f the Parliament’s 
mandate  conferred upon the Executive.”

nd 
 Report)

2. At the outset the Chairperson welcomed the Membe rs of the 
Committee to the meeting.  The following draft repo rts were taken up for 
consideration and adoption by the Committee: 
• The draft 201 
st  Report on Statutory Orders Laid on the Table of 
the Rajya  Sabha during its 226th  Session 
• The draft 202 nd  Report on the Railway Passengers (Manner of

3. The Committee took up for consideration its draf t 201 st  Report on 
Statutory Orders Laid on the Table of Rajya Sabha d uring the 226 th  Session. 
The Members noticed inordinate delays in the framin g of rules/regulations 
after Acts are enforced.  The Ministries are not adhering to the time limit of six 
months in this regard and also not taking Committee 's approval in cases of 
delays beyond six months, as recommended by the Com mittee.  Besides, the 
Committee also found that despite repeated observations and recommendations 
by the Committee in its various Reports, Ministries /Departments continue to 
lay their notifications, etc. on the Table of the H ouse after considerable delays 
spanning from months to years.  Around 33% delayed notifications are laid 
with no delay statement explaining the reason for d elay.  And even when such 
statements are attached, unacceptable excuses like delays in arranging printed 
copies are being given.  The Committee felt that th e Ministries/Departments 
are not taking its observations and recommendations  seriously and have a 
casual attitude towards framing and laying of these  rules/regulations - an 
important duty towards Parliament.  No senior offic ers, it appears, are 
monitoring this exercise in the Ministries.  The Co mmittee's concern centered 
mainly around the serious implications of delayed f raming and laying of 
notification containing rules/regulations/orders, e tc.  The Committee is 
constrained to infer that Ministries/Departments ma y be doing so deliberately 
with a view to evading Parliament's scrutiny of the  rules/regulations that are 
delegated by it to be framed by the Government.  Si nce such rules/regulations 
come into force even before they are laid before Pa rliament, any delay in 
laying before Parliament, in fact, prevents Members  to exercise their right to 
get them modified/annulled by moving a Motion.  And  this is what exactly 
happening today.  Another disturbing problem was de layed response to the 
Committee's communications from the Ministries, and  not acknowledging its 
letters, etc. in time.  So many cases of scrutiny o f rules/regulations are pending 
before the Committee mainly due to pending response s from them for many 

 
years.  They go on seeking extension on one pretext  or the other.  This has 
become a norm than exception.  It highly restricts the normal flow of 
Committee's work and then parliamentary scrutiny.  
4. In such a situation, the Committee felt not to r emain a mute spectator; 
but to protect its right to be informed, scrutiny a nd surveillance.  The 
Committee discussed possible courses of action on t his issue.  Since it 
amounted actually bypassing Parliament and disobeyi ng its authority, it is a 
serious breach of privileges not only of the Commit tee but also of the House 
and its members, which can be invoked in this case.   To begin with, however, 
it was decided that its Chairperson should write to  all the Ministers in this 
regard.  As per its earlier decision, the Committee  has already summoned 
Secretaries of some Ministries to explain about thi s state of affairs and would 
be calling others for this purpose.  The Committee also decided to apprise the 
Hon’ble Chairman, Rajya Sabha about the same. 
5. The Committee, thereafter, adopted the 201 
st  Report. 
6. The Committee then considered the draft 202 nd  Report  on the Railway 
Passengers (Manner of Investigation of Untoward Inc idents) Rules, 2003 and 
the Customs (Compounding of Offences) Rules, 2005 a nd the draft 203 rd  
Report on the Tea (Distribution and Export) Control Order,  2005. After some 
deliberations, the Committee adopted the 202 nd  and 203 rd  Reports.   
 
7. The Committee decided to present these Reports t o the House on the 
14
th  December, 2012.  Accordingly, it authorized its Ch airperson and in his 
absence Dr. K.P. Ramalingam and Shri Vijay Jawaharl al Darda, Members of 
the Committee, to present the Reports to the House.

I 
 
Report on the Railway Passengers (Manner of Investigation of Untoward 
Incidents) Rules, 2003  
 
The Railway Passengers (Manner of Investigation of Untoward Incidents) Rules, 
2003 (Annexure-I)  were framed under the Railways Act, 1989. In 1994,  through an 
amendment in Railways Act, 1989, Section 124-A was inserted providing for 
compensation on account of ‘untoward incidents’. Th is led to manifold increase in the 
number of claims on account of death/injury due to ‘untoward incidents’. To ensure that 
untoward incidents are thoroughly investigated and evidence collected and preserved, the 
“Railway Passengers (Manner of Investigation of Unt oward Incidents) Rules, 2003 were 
framed which came into force on the 8 th  August, 2003. The Rules prescribe the manner of 
investigation; duties of railway servants, Railway Protection Force (RPF) and the State 
Police with a view to substantively help in establi shing the correct position and also for 
collecting evidence.  
 
2. The said Rules were taken up for examination by the Committee on Subordinate 
Legislation, Rajya Sabha and a questionnaire on the  subject was forwarded to the 
Ministry of Railways (Railway Board) for comments/c larifications on the 13 
th  April, 
2005. The Ministry furnished comments/clarification s on the 26 th  October, 2005 
(Annexure-II) . The important points/issues raised by the Committ ee and the 
comments/clarifications furnished by the Ministry a re elaborated in the succeeding 
paragraphs. 
 
3.  The Committee noted that the Railways Act was e nacted in the year 1989, 
whereas the Rules were framed only in 2003. The Com mittee wanted from the Ministry 
justification for such a considerable delay in fram ing of the Rules and in what manner 
this area was regulated in the absence of the said Rules. The Ministry replied that 
insertion of Section 124-A in 1994 in fact, had led  to a marked increase in the number of 
claims for death/injury as a result of ‘untoward in cidents’. Though a number of claims 
were false, the decrees were awarded overwhelmingly  in favour of the applicants, 
because in the absence of proper investigation, the  Railways were not able to 

examine/defend the cases properly. To ensure that t he untoward incidents are thoroughly 
investigated and evidence collected and preserved, Rules have been framed under the 
Railways Act and notified in year 2003 for investig ation prescribing duties of railway 
servants, RPF personnel and the State Police. This is expected to substantively help in 
establishing the correct position and also for coll ecting evidence.  The Committee notes 
that there was an inordinate delay in the framing o f the Rules after the Act was 
amended in 1994 and observes that the Ministry fram ed the Rules only after 
encountering problems in the investigation and sett lement of claims in cases of 
‘untoward incidents’. The Committee feels that this inordinate delay could well have 
been avoided by framing the Rules within the normal  period of six months from the 
coming into force of the Amendment Act.   
 
4. Rule 2(1)(n)  defines technical survey, and states, “Technical Survey’ means 
survey carried out by a team of railway officials n ominated by the Station Superintendent 
or any other official being in charge of railway st ation”. The Committee pointed out that 
the rules, strictly speaking, do not define the ter m ‘technical survey’ nor do they lay 
down any parameters.  The Committee enquired whethe r the Government has any 
objection in prescribing the parameters and also po inted out that the Rule does not 
specify what rank/designation of railway personnel shall comprise the team which will 
carry out the technical survey of the untoward inci dent; and whether it is possible to 
specify such personnel by their rank/designation sp ecially because the technical survey 
involves a lot of expertise and responsibility. The  Committee further pointed out that in 
view of the definition of “Station Superintendent’  provided in Rule 2(i)(1) whether the 
words “or any other official being incharge of Railway St ation”  are not superfluous and 
whether the Ministry have any objection in deleting  these words.  In reply, the Ministry 
proposed that Rule 6 (iv) mentioning the term ‘tech nical survey’ may be deleted as 
it appears to be similar to Rule 6 (iii) and stated  that  action has been initiated to 
amend the same by notification in the Gazette.  The Ministry further stated that in 
view of proposed deletion, the question of specifyi ng rank/designation of railway 
personnel for technical survey and deleting the wor ds “or any other official being 
incharge of Railway Station ” in Rule 2(i)(l) does not arise. 

 
5. Rule 2(i)(o)  defines “Untoward incident” as, “Untoward incident” means an 
incident defined under clause I of section 123 of t he Act” .  The Committee pointed out 
that Clause I of Section 123 referred to in this Ru le does not exist in the Railways Act, 
1989 and enquired whether the Ministry would make t he necessary rectification. The 
Ministry replied that necessary rectification was d one vide  the Railways 
(Amendment) Act, 1994 dated the 26 
th  April, 1994. 
 
6. Rule 3: Report about untoward incident  states; “Any railway servant, 
including guard and driver of the train, on coming to know of the occurrence of an 
untoward incident, shall report the incident immedi ately to the nearest Station 
Superintendent” . The Committee wanted to know the medium available  to the railway 
servant for reporting the incident and asked whethe r it is not possible to prescribe some 
time period for reporting the incident after coming  to know about it. The Committee also 
asked as to why there is no mention about Form-I in Rule 3 if the report has to be made in 
Form-I. The Ministry replied that the guard/driver of the train communicates through 
memo immediately after reaching the station. The fi rst priority after accident is to protect 
the train and give first aid to the injured. As suc h, it is not possible to prescribe any fixed 
time frame for reporting the untoward incident. However, the incident is to be reported as 
early as possible. The Ministry further clarified t hat report of the incident in Form-I is to 
be made only by the guard/driver/Train Ticket Examiner who are “on duty”  in train. Rule 
3 is a general instruction for other railway servan ts who, on coming to know of the 
untoward incident, should bring the same to the not ice of the nearest Station 
Superintendent. Hence Form-I has not been mentioned in Rule 3. 
 
7.  Rule 5: Duties of Supervisor  “On receipt of a report in Form-I, the Supervisor 
shall forward the report of an untoward occurrence to the divisional Railway Manager”. 
Pointing out that there is no time period prescribe d in the Rule within which the 
supervisor shall forward the report of an untoward occurrence to the Divisional Railway 
Manager, the Committee suggested that some time per iod should be prescribed in the 
Rule itself to obviate any instance of delay. The Ministry replied that a period of three 

days may be specified for the purpose. This involve s amendment in Gazette 
Notification, for which action is being initiated.  
 
8. As per Rule 6(ii) , the Station Master, on receipt of information abo ut occurrence 
of an untoward incident is supposed to arrange for medical assistance to the injured 
passengers. The Committee enquired about the means available with the Station 
Superintendent for arranging the required medical a ssistance. The Ministry replied that 
the Station Master of the Station will arrange firs t aid to the passengers and thereafter 
make arrangements to shift them to nearest Government Hospital as early as possible. 
 
9. In Rule 6(iii) , the Committee enquired whether the Government hav e any 
objection in substituting the words “in-charge of the Force”  by the term “Divisional 
Security Commissioner” , keeping in view the provision of Rule 2(1)(f). The Ministry 
stated that they have no objection and accepted tha t the words “in charge of the 
Force”  may be replaced by the word “Divisional Security Commissioner/Senior 
Divisional Security Commissioner”.  
 
10.  As per Rule 6(iv) , on receipt of information of an untoward incident , the Station 
Superintendent is supposed to carry out technical s urvey of the incident himself or 
through his representative. The Committee enquired whether the Station Superintendent 
is competent to carry out such technical surveys. The Ministry replied that the issue 
does not arise in view of proposed deletion of Rule  6 (iv) and the definition in Rule 
2(1)(n).  
 
11.  Rule 7  relates to conduct of inspection and submission of  report by the Force. As 
per Rule 7 (2) , the officer of the Force, on completion of invest igation shall submit a 
report to the authorities specified under Rule 10(2 ). The Committee enquired whether 
Government has any objection in prescribing some ti me period for conduct of such 
investigations so that the matter does not get dela yed unreasonably. The Ministry 
accepted the Committee’s suggestion and proposed th at the period for conduct of 
such investigation may be prescribed as 60 days. The Ministry also stated that there 

are only 1754 Inspectors in Railway Protection Forc e all over India, therefore in Rule 7 
(1), Inspector should be read as Assistant Sub-Insp ector and above as defined in Sub-
Section (2) of Section 179 of Railways Act, 1989 so  that more than 10,000 ‘authorised 
officers’  are available to conduct speedy investigation in such cases.  
 
12. As per Rule 8 , on receipt of a report the police is supposed to initiate 
investigation and prepare inquest report or inquiry  in accordance with the procedure as 
laid down in the Criminal Procedure Code 1973. The Committee enquired about the 
procedure prescribed in this behalf in the Criminal  Procedure Code and whether the 
requirement of the Rules is suitably met by followi ng this procedure or it would be more 
effective to prescribe a specific procedure in the Rules itself. The Ministry replied that 
the procedure in this behalf is prescribed in Secti on 173 and 174 of the Criminal 
Procedure Code, 1973 and it is considered sufficient for the requirement of the Rules. 
 
13. As per Rule 10(1) , the police on completion of investigation is requ ired to 
forward the report to the Magistrate. The Committee  enquired whether Government has 
any objection in making it obligatory on the part o f police to supply copies of the inquest 
report, post-mortem report and jama talashi report to the officer of the Force, as required 
under Rule 7(1)(i). The Ministry agreed that it should be mandatory on the part of 
Police/GRP to supply copies of the inquest report, post-mortem report and jama 
talashi to the ‘authorised officer’ of the Force.  The Ministry however stated that it will 
be better if “N.O.C” of Ministry of Home Affairs is  obtained before hand, lest State 
Governments object later on. 
 
14. Rule 11  relates to action on part of the Divisional Railwa y Manager. As per sub-
rules (1) and (4), the Divisional Railway Manager i s supposed to examine the report 
‘immediately.”  The Committee enquired whether Government has any objection in 
prescribing some time period within which action on  the report should be taken by the 
Divisional Manager. The Ministry replied that a time period of fifteen days may be 
specified for the purpose and action has been initi ated to amend the Rule by 
notification in the Gazette.  

 
15. The Committee discussed the matter with the rep resentatives of the South Central 
Railways along with the representatives of the Mini stry of Railways (Railway Board) at 
Hyderabad on the 7 
th  November, 2005. Study note on the said discussion was sent to the 
Ministry for action taken on the 2 nd  May, 2006 ( Annexure-III ). After a couple of interim 
replies, the Ministry finally furnished the Action Taken Note on the subject on the 21 st  
April, 2009 stating that the amendments in the rule s, as suggested by the Committee on 
Subordinate Legislation, Rajya Sabha have been inco rporated in the rules by framing the

2007 (Annexure-IV) . Subsequently, the Committee also held discussion with the 
representatives of the Ministry of Railways (Railwa y Board) at Dharamshala on the 26 th  
June, 2012 and study note on the said discussion is placed at Annexure-V.  
 
16. The Committee is happy to note that the Ministry ha s accepted the 
suggestions of the Committee by incorporating them in the Railway Passengers 
(Manner of Investigation of Untoward Incidents) Amendment Rules, 2007 as under: 
 
(i)       By deleting Rule 2 (n) defining the term “technical survey”;  
(ii)        In Rule 6(iii), by substituting the words “i n-charge” with the words 
“Divisional Security Commissioner”; 
(iii)       In Rule 7(2), by prescribing a time lim it of 60 days for completion of 
investigation; 
(iv)       By inserting new sub-rule (3) in Rule 10 pres cribing that Divisional 
Security Manager shall submit the report to Divisio nal Railway Manager 
within 15 days of receipt of report by investigation; 
(v)      In Rules 11, by prescribing 15 days for examin ation of report by 
Divisional Regional Manager; and 
(vi)      By substituting Rule 13 and prescribing 15 day s for the investigation

17. On the remaining issues raised by the Committee, th e Committee notes with
