Report on the Gas Cylinder Rules, 2004  
 
The Gas Cylinder Rules, 2004 (Annexure-I)  were framed in exercise of powers 
conferred by Sections 5 and 7 of the Explosives Act , 1884. These Rules were framed in 
supersession of the Gas Cylinder Rules, 1981 for en suring safety in possession, filling, 
transportation and use of industrial gases. The eig hties and nineties witnessed massive 
expansion in the gas and related industries trigger ed by economic liberalization and 
globalization, use of Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG) , introduction of Compressed 
Natural Gas (CNG) and entry of new technologies nec essitated the framing of new Gas 
Cylinder Rules, 2004. 
 
2. The scope of the Gas Cylinder Rules, 2004 was wi dened to cover the application 
of the gas cylinder as automotive fuel storage tank s, cylinders made of materials other 
than metals paving way for entry of latest technolo gy in the field of cylinder 
manufacturing, CNG fueling stations and cylinders e xceeding water capacity of 1000 
litres for specific industrial applications. 
 
3. The Gas Cylinder Rules, 2004 outline provisions with regard to filling, 
possession, import and transport of cylinders; valv e specifications for different types of 
cylinders viz. industrial gas cylinders, medical ga s cylinders, domestic and other 
cylinders; safety relief devices; marking on cylind ers; marking on valves; identification 
of colours; labeling of cylinders; restriction on delivery or dispatch of cylinders; repairing 
of seamless gas cylinders during use; repairing of welded or brazed cylinders; prohibition 
of employment of children and intoxicated persons; prohibition of smoking, fires, lights 
and dangerous substances; general precautions, etc. The Rules also provide guidelines for 
examination and testing of cylinders.  
 
4. The Rules were taken up for examination by the C ommittee on Subordinate 
Legislation, Rajya Sabha and a questionnaire on the  subject was forwarded to the 
Ministry of Commerce & Industry (Department of Indu strial Policy & Promotion) for 

their comments/clarifications on the 23 rd  February, 2006. The Ministry furnished their 
comments/clarifications on the 29 th  May, 2006 (Annexure-II) . During the course of its 
examination, the Committee held one internal meetin g on the 26 th  August, 2008 and also 
had the oral evidence of the representatives of the  Ministry of Commerce & Industry 
(Department of Industrial Policy & Promotion) on th e 19 th  May, 2011. The Committee 
also undertook two study visits on the Rules to Bangalore and Srinagar on 21 st  June, 2011 
and 29 th  June, 2012 respectively. The important points/issu es raised by the Committee, 
the comments/clarifications furnished by the Minist ry and the 
observations/recommendations of the Committee are e laborated in the succeeding 
paragraphs. 
 
5. Rule 2 (iii) defines “Chief Controller” as the Chief Controller of Explosives, 
Government of India and Rule 2 (vii)  defines “Controller” as including the Joint Chief 
Controller of Explosives, the Deputy Chief Controll er of Explosives, the Controller of 
Explosives and the Deputy Controller of Explosives.  The Committee enquired about the 
method of appointment of the above-mentioned author ities; whether they are appointed 
for a specific period and what their service conditions are.  
 
The Ministry replied that as per recruitment rules,  Deputy Controller of 
Explosives (95% of total strength) are appointed by  direct recruitment through Union 
Public Service Commission (UPSC) and 5% by promotio n of Departmental Senior 
Technical Assistants. All other authorities from Co ntroller of Explosive to Chief 
Controller of Explosives are appointed by promotion  from the feeder grade. In case of 
non-availability of eligible officers for promotion , there are provisions in the recruitment 
rules for appointing these authorities on deputatio n (including short- term contract). In 
case of promotion and direct recruitment, there is no specific period of appointment. 
They are generally appointed till their age of supe rannuation. In case of deputation, the 
tenure is normally for 3 years. These posts belong to Group A Gazetted General Central 
Service (non-ministerial) and the service condition s are those applicable to Group A 
Services of Government of India. The Committee noted the replies furnished by the 
Ministry.     

 
6. Rule 2 (xxvii)  defines: “Inspecting authority” means a person having 
qualifications and wide experience in the field of design, manufacture and testing of gas 
cylinders and recognized by the Chief Controller as  authority for inspection and 
certification of gas cylinder”.   
 
The Committee pointed out that the definition of ‘i nspecting authority’ does not 
appear to be specific and suggested that the rank/level of the inspecting officer along with 
the qualifications and experience required for such  authority should be specified in the 
Rule itself.  
 
The Ministry replied that the definition has been c arried forward from Gas 
Cylinders Rules, 1981. The cylinders manufactured i ndigenously are covered under 
mandatory certification under BIS Certification Mar ks Scheme. In the case of cylinders 
of foreign origin, the same are manufactured under the certification of Inspection 
Agencies like Lloyd’s Register, Bureau Veritas, etc. with international accreditation only. 
As such laying down of qualification and experience is not considered necessary.   
 
The Committee does not agree with the argument of t he Ministry that laying 
down of qualification and experience for the inspec ting authority is not necessary. 
The Committee, therefore, recommends that certain m inimum eligibility criteria 
like educational qualifications and experience shou ld be prescribed for the 
inspecting authority in the Rules itself.  
 
7. Rule 24(2)  states “Dissolved acetylene cylinders, which have been dam aged by 
fire shall be condemned and destroyed by an experienced and competent person”.   
 
The Committee pointed out that the words “experienc ed and competent person” 
are vague and suggested that the experience require d of such a person for the purpose of 
the Rules should be specified in the Rules itself.   
 

The Ministry replied that it is considered that com petency cannot be judged by 
qualification and experience alone. The word ‘compe tent’ is having a much wider 
meaning. Precautions against safety are not exhaust ive. Only persons conversant with 
hazards involved in the handling of dissolved acety lene cylinder and also capable of 
handling a situation arising out of accidental expl osion of cylinder during condemnation 
can be allowed to undertake such job.  
 
The Committee does not agree with the argument of t he Ministry that 
competence cannot be judged by qualification and ex perience alone. While this may 
be true to some extent, it is not a valid excuse fo r not specifying the experience 
required for the purpose and not making the Rules m ore specific. The Committee 
reiterates its stand that vague words should not be  used while framing rules so as to 
avoid any misinterpretation and misuse. The Committ ee, therefore, recommends 
that the Rules should be made more specific by prescribing the experience required. 
 
8.  Rule 48 (1) states; “An applicant for a new licence in Form ‘G’, for a CNG 
dispensing station shall apply to the District Magi strate with two copies of site plan 
showing the location of the premises proposed to be  licenced under these rules for a 
certificate to the effect that there is no objection to the applicant’s receiving a licence  for 
a CNG dispensing station at the site proposed, and the District Magistrate, if satisfied, 
shall grant no objection certificate to the applica nt who shall forward it to the Chief 
Controller or Controller  with his application”. 
 
 The Committee pointed out that the words ‘if satisfied’ give discretionary powers 
to the District Magistrate and suggested that the p arameters governing the issue of a ‘No 
Objection Certificate’ by the District Magistrate t o the applicant for issue of a new 
licence should be specified in the Rule itself.  
 
The Ministry replied that CNG fuelling station is a  hazardous installation with a 
potential to affect the neighbourhood in the case o f a fire and explosion. As the District 

Magistrate is responsible for law and order and pub lic safety, he is required to look 
beyond legal physical possession of the premises, c ompliance of national/state highway 
regulations and issues concerning traffic, etc. The  presence of slums, thickly populated 
neighbourhood, important defence establishments, is sues relating to safety of public and 
emergency preparedness, etc. are also required to b e taken into consideration. District 
Magistrate is responsible for the preparation of of f-site emergency plan as per Rule 14 of 
Manufacture, Storage & Import of Hazardous Chemical s Rules, 1989. Hence, it is 
considered that it may neither be practical nor be advisable to lay down parameters 
governing the issues of No Objection Certificate by  the District Magistrate. The 
Committee noted the replies of the Ministry.  
 
9.  Rule 48(4)  states, “If the District Magistrate, either on a reference being made to 
him or otherwise, intimates to the chief Controller  or Controller that any licence which 
has been applied for, should not, in his opinion, g ranted, such licence shall not be issued 
without the sanction of the Central Government.”   
 
The Committee suggested that  the word ‘be’ may be inserted after the words 
“should not, in his opinion” in line ‘3’ of sub-rule (4).  
 
The Ministry replied that it is agreed that the wor d ‘be’ may be inserted after the 
words ‘should not in his opinion’ in line 3 of sub-rule (4).  
 
The Committee, however, notes that though the Ministry has agreed to insert 
the words ‘be’ after the words “should not, in his opinion” in line 3 of sub-rule (4), 
the Ministry has not carried out this amendment til l date. The Committee, 
therefore, recommends that the Ministry should amen d the Rule without further 
delay. 
 
10. Rule 53(3) states “If the Chief Controller or Controller, after scrut iny of the plan 
showing the proposed alteration and after making su ch enquiries as he deems fit, is 

satisfied that the proposed alteration may be carri ed out, he shall return to the licensee 
one copy of the plan signed by him and conveying hi s sanction subject to such condition 
or conditions as may be specified”   
 
The Committee pointed out that the words ‘after mak ing such enquiries as he 
deems fit’ empower the Chief Controller or the Cont roller, as the case may be, with wide 
discretionary powers. The Committee therefore sugge sted that requirements for allowing 
proposed alterations in the licensed premises that should govern the decision of the chief 
Controller or the Controller may be specified in the Rule itself.  
 
The Ministry in their reply stated that the area su rrounding a cylinder 
filling/storage premises may undergo a lot of chang es from the date of grant of licence 
and the date on which request for alternations/addi tions are proposed. 
Compressed/liquefied cylinders storage or a filling  plant is a potential hazard to the 
neighbouring areas. As such, it is necessary to asc ertain the developmental activities of 
the surrounding area with respect to density of pop ulation, commerce and trade, etc and 
also the past safety record, quality and safety man agement system of the firm. A 
provision, therefore, in the rules is considered ne cessary in the larger interest of the 
public safety. Such a provision is already in exist ence in Petroleum Rules, 2002, 
Explosives Rules, 1983 and Static and Mobile Pressu re Vessels (Unfired) Rules, 1981. 
The Committee noted the replies of the Ministry . 
 
11. Rule 56 states, “The Chief Controller or Controller refusing to gra nt, amend, 
renew or transfer a licence, shall communicate the reasons thereof to the applicant”.  The 
Committee suggested that the words  “thereof’ may be substituted by the word ‘therefor’ .  
 
The Ministry replied that the word ‘thereof’ is con sidered grammatically correct 
but submitted that suitable amendment, if any, will  be made after due consultation with 
the Ministry of Law.  
 

While the Ministry has agreed to substitute the wor ds “thereof” with 
“therefor” after due consultation with the Ministry  of Law, the Committee notes 
that the Ministry has not done so till date. The Co mmittee, therefore, recommends 
that the Ministry should accordingly amend the Rules expeditiously.  
 
12. Rule 57(3)  states, “The Chief Controller or Controller or the Central 
Government suspending or canceling a licence under sub-rule (1) shall communicate the 
reasons thereof to the applicant except when the li cence is suspended under sub-rule 
(2)”. 
 
 The Committee suggested that the words 'thereof' may be substituted by the word 
'therefor'. The Committee also enquired about the j ustification for not communicating the 
reasons for cancellation of a licence in case it ha s been suspended under sub-rule (2) of 
Rule 57.   
 
The Ministry replied that the word 'thereof' is con sidered grammatically correct. 
However, suitable amendment, if any, will be made a fter due consultation with the 
Ministry of Law. The Ministry also stated that the justification for not communicating the 
reasons for cancellation under sub-rule (2) of Rule 57 has been laid down in sub-rule 2(a) 
and (b) of Rule 57, which provide that "(a) before suspending or canceling a licence 
under this rule, the holder of the licence shall be  given an opportunity of being heard. (b) 
the maximum period of suspension shall not exceed t hree months". In the case of action 
originated from any Police/Intelligence inputs, Rul es shall provide enough safeguards 
against sharing confidential/secret information with the public.  
 
The Committee notes that the Ministry agreed in thi s case also to substitute  
the words 'thereof' by the word 'therefor' after du e consultation with the Ministry 
of Law. However necessary amendments have not been carried out by the Ministry 
so far. The Committee therefore recommends that the  rule should be amended 
accordingly. The Committee is satisfied with the ju stification given by the Ministry 
for not communicating the reasons for cancellation or suspension of a licence. 

 
13. Rule 59(2) and 70(2) & 3-Appeal  
Rule 59(2) states, “Every appeal shall be in writing and shall be acco mpanied by a copy 
of the Order appealed against and shall be presente d within sixty days of the Order 
passed. ”  
 
Rule 70(2) & 70(3) states,  “(2) Where the occupier or owner objects to an order  made 
under sub-rule (1), he may appeal to the Chief Cont roller within the time specified in the 
order for compliance with it.  
(3) Every appeal preferred under sub-rule (2) shall  be in writing and shall be 
accompanies by a copy of the order appealed against  and shall be made within a period 
of thirty days from the date of the order appealed against.” 
  
The Committee pointed out that the above Rules do n ot provide for disposal of 
appeals. The Committee suggested that a time period  should be specified within which 
the appeals should be processed and a final decisio n conveyed by the Central 
Government or the Chief Controller, as the case may  be, to the applicant for quick and 
timely disposal of cases.  
 
The Ministry replied that the above Rules are repro duction of old Gas Cylinder 
Rules, 1981, which do not provide time period for d isposal of appeals. The Ministry 
stated that however, if it is desirable to specify a time period for disposal of such appeals 
by the Central Government or Chief Controller of Ex plosives, as the case may be, such 
provision may be incorporated.  
 
While the Ministry has agreed that the time period for disposal of appeals 
may be specified, the Committee notes that the Mini stry has not carried out the 
necessary amendments in the Rules till date. The Co mmittee, therefore, 
recommends that the Ministry should amend the Rules immediately.  
 
14.   Rule 60-Procedure on death or disability of licensee 

"If a licensee dies or becomes insolvent or mentall y incapable or is otherwise disabled, 
the persons carrying on the business or legal heir of such licensee shall not be liable to 
any penalty or confiscation under the Act or these rules for exercising the powers granted 
to the licensee during such time as may reasonably be required  to allow him to make an 
application for a new licence or transfer of the existing licence in his own name" 
 
Provided that nothing in this rule shall be deemed to authorize the exercise of any power 
under this rule by any person after the expiry of the period of the licence. 
 
 The Committee pointed out that the words "such tim e as may reasonably be 
required" appear to be vague and enquired whether G overnment have any objection in 
specifying the time period.  
 
The Ministry replied that during the revision of th e Rules, the thrust was on 
making the rules user friendly. Stipulating a time period for submission of application by 
the legal heir will make the rule inflexible. A legal heir, who is already in a state of shock 
by the death or disability of licensee, may not sub mit application immediately till such 
time he comes into the grip of rules and regulation s. Further, in case of any dispute on 
legal inheritance, the matter has to be settled by court of law, which is normally time 
consuming. The Committee noted the replies of the Ministry.  
 
15.    Rule 65-Licence fee and other than licence fee "(1) The Central Government may, 
by notification in the official Gazette, revise the  fees as specified in Schedule V from time 
to time.  
(2) All fees payable under these ruels shall be pai d through crossed demand draft drawn 
on any Bank in favour of the Chief Controller of Ex plosives or Controller of Explosives 
of Department of Explosives payable at respective places as the case may be". 
 
              The Committee pointed out that the he ading of Rule 65 is not clear and 
suggested that it would be more appropriate if the word "fee” is added after the words 
"licence fee and" in the heading.  

 
The Ministry agreed that it would be appropriate if  word 'fee' is added after the 
words 'licence fee and'.  
 
The Committee notes that the Ministry agreed that t he words 'fee' be added 
after the words 'licence fee and', but necessary am endments have not been carried 
out by the Ministry. The Committee therefore recomm ends that the rule should be 
amended accordingly. 
 
16.   Rule 66-Power to exempt – “If the Chief Controller is satisfied that in respe ct of 
any cylinder or any mode of conveyance, any of the requirements of these rules may be 
safely suspended or modified, he may, by written or der, authorize such suspension or 
modification for such period and under such conditi on as he may think fit and such order 
may be revoked at any time.”  
 
        The Committee pointed out that the Rule giv es wide discretionary powers to exempt 
which are likely to be misused.  
 
         The Ministry replied that the above Rule h as been carried forward from Gas 
Cylinders Rules, 1981. Whether it is approval, gran t, suspension, cancellation or 
exemption under the above Rule, justification shall  be recorded in writing for such 
approval, grant, suspension, cancellation or exempt ion, etc. The above provision is to 
make the Rule more flexible so that any of the prov isions under the Rules does not come 
in the way of development of the industry as some of the Rules may become redundant or 
inadequate to address to the changing industrial sc enario due to continuous technological 
development. In the light of Right of Information A ct, 2005, the apprehension of misuse 
of power may not be relevant.  
 
             The Committee does not accept the stand of the Mini stry that in the light of 
Right to Information Act, 2005, the apprehension of  misuse of power may not be 
relevant. The Committee felt that adequate safeguar ds should be provided against 

misuse of the power to exempt. The Committee, there fore, recommends that there 
should be a provision in the Rule for recording of reasons for making exemption to 
obviate misuse of the power of exemption. 
 
17. The Committee considered the matter during its meeting on the 26 
th  August, 2008 
and decided to have the oral evidence of the repres entatives of the Ministry of Commerce 
& Industry (Department of Industrial Policy & Promo tion) for further elucidations on the 
subject. Accordingly, the Committee heard the Secre tary, Ministry of Commerce & 
Industry (Department of Industrial Policy & Promoti on) on the 19 th  May, 2011. The 
Committee also decided to have a discussion with th e representatives of the major oil 
companies who are involved in the implementation of  the Rules for further elucidations 
on the subject. Accordingly, the Committee held dis cussions with the representatives of 
Indian Oil Corporation, Hindustan Petroleum Corpora tion Limited (HPCL), Bharat 
Petroleum Corporation Limited (BPCL), Oil Industry Safety Directorate (OISD) and 
Petroleum Explosives Safety Organization (PESO) alo ng with the Ministry of Petroleum 
& Natural Gas and the Ministry of Commerce & Indust ry (Department of Industrial 
Policy & Promotion) at Bangalore on the 21 st  June, 2011 and with Indian Oil 
Corporation, Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Limite d (HPCL), Bharat Petroleum 
Corporation Limited (BPCL) along with the Ministry of Petroleum & Natural Gas and 
the Ministry of Commerce & Industry (Department of Industrial Policy & Promotion) at 
Srinagar on the 29 th  June, 2012.  Study notes on the said discussions a re placed at 
Annexure-III and Annexure-IV .  Certain issues which come up during the discussi ons 
are outlined in the following paras. 
Conformity to Indian standards 
 
18.  The Committee notes that  as per the Gas Cylinder Rules 2004, the LPG 
Cylinders, Valves and Regulators of Indian Origin w ere required to conform to the 
relevant Indian Standards under a licence to use BI S Standard mark on these 
products. The Committee, however, notes that for LP G cylinders, Valve and 
Regulators of external origin (i.e. manufactured in  foreign countries), Gas Cylinder 
Rules 2004 prescribe conformity to standards other than Indian Standards, which is 
outside the preview of BIS. The Committee also note s that there are many other 

similar products, like tyres and cement being produ ced in companies abroad, but 
when imported to India, all such products have to m eet the relevant Indian 
standards under a licence from BIS. As such, the Co mmittee recommends that all 
the products covered under Gas Cylinder Rules, when  imported to India should be 
as per Indian Standards, irrespective of whether th ey were produced in India or 
abroad. 
Safety Instructions 
 
19. The Committee notes that safety instructions for ha ndling gas cylinders are 
written mainly in English and Hindi. The Committee,  therefore, suggests that safety 
instructions should also be printed in regional lan guages so that more people can 
benefit from the safety instructions. 
 
Training on safety norms  
20. The Committee feels that there should be safety nor ms for storage at 
distributor level and that these should be strictly  adhered to. Drivers/Cleaners 
should be properly trained to handle emergency.  
 
Small Cylinders 
 
21. The Committee notes that small cylinders available in the market posed 
threat to the safety of consumers. The Committee wa s informed that no licences 
were issued for small cylinders by the Ministry.  T he Committee, therefore, 
recommends that the rules should be amended, if nee d be, to tackle this problem. 
The Committee feels that this is happening at a ver y large level and cannot be done 
at the small distributor level. The Committee feels  that it needs immediate action 
from the Ministry and urges the Ministry to take re sponsibility to devise a 
mechanism to tackle this problem in consultation wi th the oil companies. The 
Committee also noted that filling of these small cy linders is being done at local level 
from LPG cylinders supplied by oil companies. So th e oil companies also owe 
responsibility to devise mechanism to check this ma lpractice. The Committee 
recommends that the Bureau of Indian Standards which is responsible for providing 
standards should devise/prescribe appropriate stand ards/guidelines to regularize 

the sale of small cylinders so that safety is not c ompromised. The Committee, 
accordingly, recommends that the rules should be amended accordingly.  
 
22. The Committee was informed that amendment to th e Gas Cylinder Rules, 2004 is 
under consideration by the Ministry. The Committee hopes that the Committee’s 
recommendations and observations outlined in the pr eceding paras will be considered by 
the Ministry at the time of carrying out the amendment to the Rules.  
 
 
 
 
SUMMARY OF RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS OF THE 
COMMITTEE  
 
Rule 2 (xxvii) 
 
23.  The Committee does not agree with the argument of the Ministry that laying 
down of qualification and experience for the inspec ting authority is not necessary. 
The Committee, therefore, recommends that certain m inimum eligibility criteria 
like educational qualifications and experience shou ld be prescribed for the 
inspecting authority in the Rules itself.  
 
Rule 24(2) 
 
24.  The Committee does not agree with the argument of the Ministry that 
competence cannot be judged by qualification and ex perience alone. While this may 
be true to some extent, it is not a valid excuse fo r not specifying the experience 
required for the purpose and not making the Rules m ore specific. The Committee 
reiterates its stand that vague words should not be  used while framing rules so as to 
avoid any misinterpretation and misuse. The Committ ee, therefore, recommends 
that the Rules should be made more specific by prescribing the experience required. 
 
Rule 48(4) 
 

25.  The Committee, however, notes that though the Mini stry has agreed to insert 
the words ‘be’ after the words “should not, in his opinion” in line 3 of sub-rule (4), 
the Ministry has not carried out this amendment til l date. The Committee, 
therefore, recommends that the Ministry should amen d the Rule without further 
delay . 
 
Rule 56 
 
26.  While the Ministry has agreed to substitute the wo rds “thereof” with 
“therefor” after due consultation with the Ministry  of Law, the Committee notes 
that the Ministry has not done so till date. The Co mmittee, therefore, recommends 
that the Ministry should accordingly amend the Rules expeditiously.  
 
Rule 57(3) 
 
27.  The Committee notes that the Ministry agreed in th is case also to substitute  
the words 'thereof' by the word 'therefor' after du e consultation with the Ministry 
of Law. However necessary amendments have not been carried out by the Ministry 
so far. The Committee therefore recommends that the  rule should be amended 
accordingly. The Committee is satisfied with the ju stification given by the Ministry 
for not communicating the reasons for cancellation or suspension of a licence. 
 
Rule 59(2) and 70(2) & 3-Appeal 
 
28.  While the Ministry has agreed that the time period  for disposal of appeals 
may be specified, the Committee notes that the Mini stry has not carried out the 
necessary amendments in the Rules till date. The Co mmittee, therefore, 
recommends that the Ministry should amend the Rules immediately.  
 
Rule 65 
 
29.  The Committee notes that the Ministry agreed that the words 'fee' be added 
after the words 'licence fee and', but necessary am endments have not been carried 

out by the Ministry. The Committee therefore recomm ends that the rule should be 
amended accordingly. 
 
Rule 66-Power to exempt 
 
30.      The Committee does not accept the stand of the  Ministry that in the light of 
Right to Information Act, 2005, the apprehension of  misuse of power may not be 
relevant. The Committee felt that adequate safeguar ds should be provided against 
misuse of the power to exempt. The Committee, there fore, recommends that there 
should be a provision in the Rule for recording of reasons for making exemption to 
obviate misuse of the power of exemption. 
 
 
 
Conformity to Indian standards 
 
31. The Committee notes that  as per the Gas Cylinder Rules 2004, the LPG 
Cylinders, Valves and Regulators of Indian Origin w ere required to conform to the 
relevant Indian Standards under a licence to use BI S Standard mark on these 
products. The Committee, however, notes that for LP G cylinders, Valve and 
Regulators of external origin (i.e. manufactured in  foreign countries), Gas Cylinder 
Rules 2004 prescribe conformity to standards other than Indian Standards, which is 
outside the preview of BIS. The Committee also note s that there are many other 
similar products, like tyres and cement being produ ced in companies abroad, but 
when imported to India, all such products have to m eet the relevant Indian 
standards under a licence from BIS. As such, the Co mmittee recommends that all 
the products covered under Gas Cylinder Rules, when  imported to India should be 
as per Indian Standards, irrespective of whether th ey were produced in India or 
abroad. 
 
Safety Instructions 
 
32. The Committee notes that safety instructions for ha ndling gas cylinders are 
written mainly in English and Hindi. The Committee,  therefore, suggests that safety 

instructions should also be printed in regional lan guages so that more people can 
benefit from the safety instructions. 
 
Training on safety norms 
 
33. The Committee feels that there should be safety nor ms for storage at 
distributor level and that these should be strictly  adhered to. Drivers/Cleaners 
should be properly trained to handle emergency.  
 
Small Cylinders 
 
34. The Committee notes that small cylinders available in the market posed 
threat to the safety of consumers. The Committee wa s informed that no licences 
were issued for small cylinders by the Ministry.  T he Committee, therefore, 
recommends that the rules should be amended, if nee d be, to tackle this problem. 
The Committee feels that this is happening at a ver y large level and cannot be done 
at the small distributor level. The Committee feels  that it needs immediate action 
from the Ministry and urges the Ministry to take re sponsibility to devise a 
mechanism to tackle this problem in consultation wi th the oil companies. The 
Committee also noted that filling of these small cy linders is being done at local level 
from LPG cylinders supplied by oil companies. So th e oil companies also owe 
responsibility to devise mechanism to check this ma lpractice. The Committee 
recommends that the Bureau of Indian Standards which is responsible for providing 
standards should devise/prescribe appropriate stand ards/guidelines to regularize 
the sale of small cylinders so that safety is not c ompromised. The Committee, 
accordingly, recommends that the rules should be amended accordingly.

(ii) 

I 
Report 
On 
The Motor Spirit and High Speed Diesel (Regulation of Supply and Distribution and 
Prevention of Malpractices) Order, 2005 
 
 The Motor Spirit and High Speed Diesel (Regulation  of Supply and Distribution and 
Prevention of Malpractices) Order, 2005 (Annexure-I)  have been framed under the Essential 
Commodities Act, 1955.  The Order has been framed i n supersession of the Motor Spirit and High 
Speed Diesel (Regulation of Supply and Distribution and Prevention of Malpractices) Order, 1998. 
 
2. In view of the importance and enormity of the is sues involved, the Committee has had 
several meetings with major Oil Companies like Indo  Burma Petroleum, Hindustan Petroleum 
Corporation, Indian Oil Corporation and Bharat Petr oleum Corporation.  The Committee also 
discussed about the enforcement of the Order with t he State Governments of West Bengal, 
Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh . Views/ suggestions were also received from agencie s engaged in the 
supply, distribution and sale of these commodities as well as other associations/ bodies and the 
public in general like the Centre of Science & Envi ronment, an NGO; Federation of All India 
Petroleum Traders Association; Petrol & High Speed Diesel Dealers Association; Gramin Vikas 
Samity; Petrol Dealers Associations etc.. 
 
3. The said Order of 2005 incorporates various chan ges like (i) introduction of short delivery 
under the malpractices; (ii) “Authorized officer” having power of search and seizure under clause 7; 
(iii) introduction of restriction on marketing of M otor Spirit and High Speed Diesel (MS/HSD); (iv) 
grant of authorization to market Motor Spirit and High Speed Diesel; (v) supply of Motor Spirit and 
High Speed Diesel blended with ethanol and bio-dies el, respectively; (vi) specification of time 
frame for sending test report by the laboratory and  for communication of the test results to the 
concerned; (vii) details of norms for permissible s tock variation, (viii) powers of search and seizure  
of the officers of the State Government and the Oil  Marketing Companies in the Public Sector; and, 
(ix) sampling procedure to be adopted for drawing s amples of petroleum products for testing at 
laboratories listed have been specified.  The Motor  Spirit and High Speed Diesel (Regulation of 

Supply and Distribution and Prevention of Malpracti ces) Order, 2005, while under consideration, 
was amended twice- first was in 2007 and again in  2009.   
 
4. The Committee in fact had earlier taken up the M otor Spirit and High Speed Diesel 
(Regulation of Supply and Distribution and Preventi on of Malpractices) Order, 1998 for 
examination and a questionnaire on the subject matt er was forwarded to the Ministry of Petroleum 
& Natural Gas for comments/ clarifications.  The Co mmittee also held discussions with the 
representatives of Oil Marketing Companies like Ind o Burma Petroleum, Hindustan Petroleum and 
Indian Oil Corporation alongwith the Ministry of Pe troleum & Natural Gas in 2000. Views/ 
suggestions were also invited from organizations, a ssociations, traders, and public in general on the 
efficacy of the Order.   In the meanwhile, the Mini stry of Petroleum & Natural Gas vide  their 
notification No. G.S.R. 729(E) dated 21 
st  December, 2005 notified the Motor Spirit and High Speed 
Diesel (Regulation of Supply and Distribution and P revention of Malpractices) Order, 2005 in 
supersession of the  Motor Spirit and High Speed Diesel (Regulation of Supply and Distribution and 
Prevention of Malpractices) Order, 1998.  
 
5. Thereafter, the Committee took up the discussion  on the new Order and a freash 
questionnaire on the subject was prepared and forwa rded to the Ministry of Petroleum & Natural 
Gas for their comments/ clarifications on the 22 nd  May, 2007. The comments of the Ministry are 
enclosed ( Annexure II) .  The points raised by the Committee and the comme nts/ clarifications 
received from the Ministry are reproduced in the subsequent paragraphs. 
 
6. When asked about the reasons for framing the Ord er of 2005 in supersession of the earlier 
one and the major points of distinction between the Orders of 1998 and 2005, the Ministry informed 
that the earlier Order was framed in 1998 and since  then several amendments had been made to 
incorporate necessary changes for making it relevan t in the liberalized scenario.  The new Order of 
2005 incorporated all the amendments into a single Order.  There are additions/ changes in the 2005 
Order to incorporate the changing environment and t o give clarity to the provisions.  The major 
points of distinction include additions/ changes in  the definition clause to the terms ‘Adulteration’;   
‘Authorized Officer’; ‘Consumer’, ‘Malpractices’; c lause 3(ii) under Product, Supply and 

Transportation; Clause relating to Power of Search and Seizure; Clause 7(1)(d) under Power of 
Search and Seizure and Clause 8(5)&(6) under Sampling of Product.   
 
7. The Committee is happy to note that a new clause  8(5) & (6) under Sampling of 
Product which did not exist in the earlier Order ha s been incorporated in the 2005 Order so 
as to provide that the notified laboratory shall fu rnish the test report to the authorized officer 
within twenty days of the receipt of samples at the  laboratory and also the authorized officer 
shall communicate the test results to the dealer or transporter or concerned person and the oil 
company, as the case may be, within five days of re ceipt of test results from the laboratory for 
appropriate action.   The Committee feels that fixing time line for different stages will quicken 
the process which earlier used to take longer time.   
 
8. The Committee is happy to know that its suggesti ons for fixing of a time period for 
testing of samples under Clause 5(5) of the 1998 Or der was accepted by the Ministry.  The 
earlier Order did not provide the time limit within  which the samples were to be tested by the 
laboratory.  As per Clause 8(4) of the 2005 Order, the authorized officer shall forward the 
sample of the product taken within ten days to the laboratory for analyzing with a view to 
checking whether the density and other parameters o f the product conform to the 
requirements of the BIS specification number of IS- 2796 and IS-1460 for Motor Spirit and 
High Diesel respectively.   
  
9. Clause 5(2)  states that ‘After scrutiny of the application, the Central Gov ernment shall, if it 
is satisfied with the details furnished by the appl icant, after requiring the applicant to furnish ban k 
guarantee for an amount specified by the Government , issue authorization to market motor spirit 
and High Speed Diesel indicating the terms and cond itions of such authorization.’  The Committee 
inquired whether Government had any objection in sp ecifying in the Order itself the time period 
within which the Government shall scrutinize the ap plications and issue a certificate of 
authentication.  Also, what was the basis for calcu lation of the Bank Guarantee required to be 
furnished by the applicant for the purpose of the Order.  
 

10. The Ministry informed that Government did not h ave any objection in specifying the time 
period in the Order itself within which the Governm ent shall scrutinize the applications and issue a 
certificate of authentication.  Regarding requireme nt of Bank Guarantee, the Ministry informed that 
the Company proposing to make the specified level o f investment in the eligible activities or a 
Company which has already made the total minimum in vestment required in the eligible activities 
but is yet to complete the project/ projects will b e required to sign an agreement, containing 
conditions and milestones, with the Ministry of Pet roleum & Natural Gas/ Regulatory Board.  The 
agreement would inter-alia , have specific provisions for bank guarantee of a specified amount for 
the proposed investment.  The guarantee, where prop osed, would be discharged on completion of 
the specified level of investment, but the obligati on of the applicant to complete the project would 
continue till final completion of the project.  Whi le formulating the guidelines regarding grant of 
authorization to market transportation fuel, it was  considered to have specific provisions for 
performance guarantee and bank guarantee/ interest bearing deposit of 1/4 th  of the specified amount. 
 
11.   In the view of the Committee, guidelines regarding grant of authorization to market 
transportation fuel should be specific and have cla rity with regard to all technicalities 
pertaining to provisions for performance guarantee and bank guarantee so as to leave no 
scope for any kind of arbitration and discretion an d, accordingly, recommends to the 
Ministry/ Regulatory Board to take immediate/ neces sary action in this regard to ensure the 
same.   
 
12. Clause 7(1) states that  ‘Any Gazetted Officer of the Central Government or a State 
Government or any police officer not below the rank  of Deputy Superintendent of Police duly 
authorized by general or any special order of Centr al Government or a State Government, as the 
case may be, with a view to scrutinizing compliance  with the provisions of this Order, or for the 
purpose of satisfying himself that this Order or an y Order made thereunder has been complied with 
or there is reason to believe that all or any of th e provision of this Order have been and are being 
or are about to be contravened’.  The Committee was of the view that the words ‘reason to believe 
that all or any of the provisions of this Order hav e been and are being or are about to be 
contravened’  leave scope for harassment by the concerned office rs as it gives them discretionary 

power.  The Committee, accordingly, desired that th e rule may be rephrased with suitable words to 
obviate such eventuality. 
 
13. The Ministry submitted that the Control Order o f 2005 is a tool available for effective 
implementation of the Essential Commodities Act.  U nder clause 7(1), the power of search and 
seizure has been vested with reasonably senior and responsible officers of Central Government, 
State Government and Oil Companies.  Under clause 7 (2), before exercising the power of seizure 
the authorized officer shall record in writing the reasons for doing so and shall also provide a copy 
of such recording to the dealer, transporter, consumer or any other concerned person. 
 
14. The Committee pointed that the word ‘officer’ s hould come between the words ‘the’ and 
‘authorized’ in Clause 8(1) which reads as  ‘The authorized under clause 7 shall draw the sampl e 
from the tank, nozzle vehicle or receptacle, as the  case may be, in clean aluminum containers, to 
check whether density and other parameters of the p roduct conform to the requirement or BIS 
specifications number IS 2796 and IS 1460 for motor  spirit and high speed diesel respectively.  
Where samples are drawn from retail outlets, the re levant tank-truck sample retained by the dealer 
as per clause 3(b) would also be collected for labo ratory analysis’.  The Ministry accepted the 
typographical error and agreed to amend the Motor Spirit and High Speed Diesel (Regulation 
of Supply and Distribution and Prevention of Malpra ctices) Order, 2005 to remove the 
typographical error. 
 
15. The Committee was of the view that Clause 8(6) which states that  ‘The authorized officer 
shall communicate the test result to the dealer or transporter or concerned person and the oil 
company, as the case may be, within five days of re ceipt of test results from the laboratory for 
appropriate action’  provides for appropriate action on the part of the  dealer, transporter, oil 
company, etc., once the test results are communicat ed to them without specifying the same and that 
it was desirable that the action to be taken for be tter implementation of the Order should be  
specified in the Order itself. In reply the Ministr y submitted that Clause 8(6) of the 2005 Order 
provides that the authorized officer shall communic ate the test results to the dealer or transporter o r 
concerned person and the oil company, as the case m ay be, within five days of receipt of test report 
from the laboratory for appropriate action. The aut horized officer, after receipt of test report from 

the laboratory under clause 8(5), if the product passes in the laboratory test, communicates the same 
to the dealer or transporter or the concerned perso n.  In case of failure of sample in the laboratory 
test i.e. sample failure with respect to any of the  parameters specified in the BIS number IS 2796 
and IS 1460 for Motor Spirit and High Speed Diesel respectively, the competent authority of the oil 
marketing companies may take further necessary acti on such as suspension of sale and supplies and 
also issue of a show cause notice alongwith a copy of test results, to the dealer giving him 
opportunity to explain his case before taking any p enal action under Dealership Agreement, 
Marketing Discipline Guidelines (MDG) and transport er under Transport Discipline Guidelines.  
Since further action depends on the outcome of the test reports, the same cannot be specified in the 
Control Order.  Under the given situations, the Committee feels tha t the Government/ OMCs 
should ensure that specific norms and guidelines ar e in place with regard to all activities and 
operations of the retailers, traders, transporters and oil companies to curb adulteration.  
 
16. When asked about the reasons for deleting Sched ule I of the Order of 1998 pertaining to 
requirements and specifications of the products fro m the Order of 2005, which according to the 
Committee otherwise provided a ready reference in t he matter, the Ministry informed that Schedule 
I of MS/HSD Control Order, 1998 provided various pa rameters of BIS specification IS-2796:1995 
and IS-1460:1995 for Motor Spirit and High Speed Di esel respectively.  The Bureau of Indian 
Standards makes amendment to the specifications of MS and HSD which requires amendment of 
MS/HSD Control Order.  As the changes in the specif ication of the products (MS/HSD) are more 
frequent than the changes in the Control Order, and  by incorporating specifications in the MS/HSD 
Control Order the same would be required to be amen ded every time BIS specifications are 
amended.  Without incorporation the BIS specificati ons by way of a schedule, HSD and MS has 
been defined in clause 2(e) and clause 2(g) respect ively by mentioning the BIS specification 
number.   
 
17. The Committee took note of the fact that the pr oblems of adulteration and under supply were 
serious both in rural and urban area, and, accordin gly, inquired whether oil companies were also 
entrusted with the responsibility of taking penal a ction against retail outlet if found indulging in 
under supply.  Also,  whether Government would expl ore the possibility, by way of, guidelines for 
oil companies in this regard.  In response, the Min istry informed the Committee that Oil Marketing 

Companies (OMCs) undertake regular and surprise ins pections of Retail Outlets and also take 
action under Marketing Discipline Guidelines (MDG) and Dealership Agreements against those 
indulging in adulteration and malpractices includin g short delivery found to be due to deliberate 
tempering dispensing units or unauthorized fittings  in the dispensing units.  MDG provide for 
termination of dealership in the first instance its elf for serious malpractices like adulteration, 
tampering of seals, unauthorized fittings/ gears in  dispensing units.  Checking of adulteration was a 
continuous process and the Ministry of Petroleum & Natural Gas had been reviewing steps taken to 
curb adulteration from time to time.  In the process, several technological and institutional measures 
had been taken to contain adulteration.  In order to monitor the activities at retail outlets by adopting 
the latest technological improvements, Government h as directed the Public Sector Oil Marketing 
Companies (OMCs) to undertake automation of retail outlets selling more than 200 KL per month  
and to complete third party certification of all the retail outlets selling more than 100 KL per month.  
OMCs had already commenced the automation of these outlets in a phased manner. 
 
18. The Committee observed that Indian Oil Corporat ion, Hindustan Petroleum, Bharat 
Petroleum, HPCL have carried out automation for the ir retail outlets.  The Committee feels 
that these Oil Companies being mega scale projects on all India basis and considering that 
rolling out of automation essentially involves repl ication of the same solution at all retail 
outlets, these mega Companies should design and pro vide a system at their Retail Outlets 
(ROs), which is robust, rugged and scalable on a lo ng-term basis to accommodate all the new 
technological advancements in retail of petroleum.  The Committee recommends that all the 
OMGs should have a time bound programme to complete  the process of automation for all 
their retail outlets which would be a significant s tep in curbing the malpractices at the 
dispensing units effectively. 
 
19. The Committee was of the opinion that chemicals / solvents available in the market like 
kerosene, naphtha, etc., which are cheaper in cost and can be easily mixed with Motor Spirit and 
HSD which were the main cause of adulteration and d esired to know the views of the Government 
for considering bringing to par the prices of these  adulteratives with the sale price of MS/HSD to 
obviate the problem of adulteration.  The Committee  also expressed serious concern over the grave 
effect of adulteration on the environment and sought to know the steps taken by the Ministry to stop 

adulteration and pilferage.   The Ministry submitte d that the possibility of adulteration of petrol/ 
diesel by some unscrupulous elements could not be r uled out due to huge price difference between 
petrol/ diesel and various adulterants available in  the market and the easy miscibility of these 
products with petrol/ diesel.  To check adulteratio n in auto fuels and diversion of PDS kerosene, 
Government has asked Oil Marketing Companies (OMCs)  to take the following various steps to 
contain the menace of adulteration:- 
(i)   Government has requested the State Government s/ Union Territory Administrations to take 
steps to control adulteration under the Control Ord ers issued by the Government to prevent fuel 
adulteration, under the Essential Commodities Act, 1955 wherein State Governments are 
empowered to take action against those indulging in adulteration. 
 
(ii) OMCs are required to undertake regular and sur prise inspections of retail outlets and also 
take action under Marketing Discipline Guidelines ( MDG) and Dealership Agreements against 
those indulging in adulteration and malpractices.  Infact, MDG provide for termination of dealership 
in cases of adulteration being established. 
 
(iii) Government has taken initiatives to expedite the installation  of Global Positioning System 
(GPS) to monitor the movement of tank trucks. 
 
(iv) OMCs have introduced new tamper proof tank-tru ck locking systems to prevent en-route 
adulteration by transporters. 
 
(v) Keeping in view the misuse/ diversion of Suprem e Kerosene Oil (SKO) for adulteration, the 
import of SKO by private parties has been canalized through OMCs. 
 
(vi) As advised/ required by Government, OMCs have created a separate wing to report to a 
Director other than Director (Marketing), which wil l oversee and monitor all activities and 
operations to curb adulteration and specify norms and guideline in this regard.    
 
20.  The Committee notes that the Government has taken i nitiatives in the form of 
technological and institutional measures to contain  adulteration of petrol/ diesel and 

streamlining PDS kerosene distribution.  The Commit tee, however, feels that there is  need to 
establish a monitoring regime and a system of fines  and penalties that can act as a strong 
deterrent to fuel adulteration.   
 
21. The Committee noted that the Center of Science & Environment in its study had observed 
that the regulatory framework should be treated and  developed separately from the system of self-
regulation by the Oil Companies currently in force.   In keeping with this observation, the 
Committee felt that some vertical accountability an d liability should be established along the 
entire supply chain i.e. oil companies, transporter  and retailer, for ensuring effective checks 
and balances .  
 
22.  In response, the Ministry submitted that while  the vertical accountability of PSU and OMCs 
was in-built in the system itself, these companies being public sector companies were also 
accountable to Parliament through various Parliamen tary Committees.  Further, in order to develop 
an independent regulatory framework, Government had  decided to set up a Petroleum & Natural 
Gas Regulatory Board to regulate the refining, proc essing, storage, transportation, distribution, 
marketing and sale of petroleum, petroleum products and natural gas, excluding production of crude 
oil and natural gas to protect the interests of con sumers and entities engaged in specified activities  
relating to petroleum, petroleum products and natur al gas and also to ensure uninterrupted and 
adequate supply of these products in all parts of t he country and to promote competitive markets 
and for matters connected therewith or incidental t hereto.  As far as Petroleum & Natural Gas 
Regulatory Board is concerned, Government has the p ower to issue policy directions to the Board 
under Section 42 of the PNGRB Act, 2006.  Further, the Board would also be subject to 
Parliamentary control in terms of the following provisions of the Act:- 
i. Every rule made by Central Government and every reg ulation made by the Board, as 
soon as it is made, would be laid before each House of Parliament. 
ii. The Parliament has the power to make modification t o each rules and regulations or to 
decide that such rule or regulation shall not be made. 
iii. The rules or regulations shall have effect only in such modified form or be of no effect, 
as the case may be. 

iv. The Annual Report and the Accounts of the Board shall be laid before each House of the 
Parliament. 
 
23. The Committee appreciates that the Ministry of Petroleum & Natural Gas are aware 
of their duty and the need and importance of lying the statutory rules/ regulations/orders and 
Annual Reports before each House of Parliament. The  Committee expects that the Ministry 
would continue to adhere to the timely framing and laying of the notifications/ Annual 
Reports   in future also. 
 
24. Views/ suggestions received from concerned agen cies, organizations, associations, traders, 
individuals, etc. on the efficacy of the 1998 Order  included the following issues and were duly

kerosene and diesel; (b) naphtha, solvents and petr ol including (c) uniform excise duty, sales tax

(xii) transportation and supply of petroleum produc ts; (xiii) inspection of retail outlets and

25. The Committee also discussed the matter with th e representatives of Indian Oil Corporation 
and the State Government of West Bengal alongwith t he Ministry of Petroleum & Natural Gas at 
Kolkata on 6 
th  June, 2007.  Study note on the said discussion is enclosed (Annexure III).   During 
the course of discussion, the Committee was informe d that States were not responding to the 

Ministry’s communication regarding end-use certific ates because there were no complaints.  As 
regards quantum of bio-diesel being mixed by oil companies, the Committee was informed that bio-
diesel was at a developing stage.  As per approval of Government, 5% ethanol was mixed in petrol. 
However, some State Governments were levying export  duty on ethanol coming from other States 
which made the cost of petroleum to go up.  On bein g informed that IOC was producing seed and

Department of Biotechnology of the Government of We st Bengal had taken up the project for 
production of bio-diesel, though,  no concrete resu lts had been achieved so far. In addition, it was 
informed that the Anti-Adulteration Cell did not report to Director (Marketing) of the oil companies 
to ensure its independence.  The procedure followed  was that of third party checking.  Kerosene 
was the main adulterant in the petroleum products a nd consumers could not check it.  However, 
there was a mechanism where even one per cent of ad ulteration could be detected.   Marker was 
used for detection of adulteration which was rampan t even at depot level with the connivance of 
transporters.  Dealers were given option to keep sa mples of Truck-tank with them.  There was huge 
price difference between the kerosene and petrol/ d iesel.  Otherwise if distribution of kerosene was

26.  The Committee also took up the matter with Ind ian Oil Corporation, Hindustan Petroleum 
Corporation, Bharat Petroleum Corporation, Ministry  of Petroleum & Natural Gas and the State 
Governments of Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh and Goa at  Bangalore, Hyderabad and Goa on the 26 th  
May, 2008, 20 th  December, 2010 and 30 th  September, 2011, respectively .   The following points

R&D as compared to total expenditure and how these compare in respect to other countries, and (x) 
need, if any, for revision in the Act/ Order.    
 
27. In response to the points raised, the Committee  was informed that inspections of retail

surprise inspections at retail outlets, random samp le collection for testing, introduction of CFR

premises, installing tamper proof locking system et c.  However, when it came to expenditure spent 
on R&D as compared to the company’s total expenditu re and also in comparison with other 
countries,  the Committee observed that the total expenditure towards R&D against the total 
turnover of the oil companies was very less and was  too meager in comparison to some
