II. Taking over of Distance Education Council of IG NOU by UGC through 
administrative order  
 
6. The Committee then heard the representatives of the Ministry of Human Resource 
Development (Department of Higher Education), Vice- Chancellor, IGNOU and 
Chairman, UGC on the issue of taking over of Distan ce Education Council of IGNOU by 
UGC through administrative order without making the  necessary legislative enactments. 
The Convenor asked the Ministry to clarify whether the mandate of regulating ODL 
mode of education can be taken away from IGNOU simp ly by abolishing the DEC 
without amending the relevant provisions of the IGN OU Act, 1985 for this purpose.  He 
also asked about the specific Sections of an Act/Ru le/Statute, etc. under which the said 
mandate was shifted to UGC and AICTE.  The Committe e also questioned about the 
urgency with which DEC was shifted to UGC without w aiting till proper legislation in 
the matter is passed by Parliament.  
 
7. The Ministry could not give convincing and legal ly tenable replies to the queries 
raised by the Committee.  It could not deny the fac t that mandate to regulate standards of 
education through distance mode still remained with  the IGNOU Act and that it did not 
cease to exist merely on the repeal of Statute 28 a bolishing DEC.  On the question as to 
which Section of UGC Act empowers UGC to regulate d istance education, Chairman, 
UGC informed the Committee that Section 12 of the U GC Act empowers UGC to 
regulate distance education which says, “It shall be the duty of the Commission to  take, in 
consultation with the Universities or other bodies concerned, all such steps as it may 
think fit for the promotion and co-ordination of Un iversity education and for the 
determination and maintenance of standards of teach ing, examination and research in 
Universities..”  . He further stated that the Ministry has issued a  direction to UGC to take 

over DEC under Section 20(1) of UGC Act which says that the Central Government has 
the power to give direction to the UGC, which is binding.   
 
8. As regards the urgency, the Ministry replied tha t the Madhava Menon Committee 
was aware that passing of the Distance Education Co uncil of India Bill as suggested by it 
may take some time. It also felt that the position of UGC vis-à-vis IGNOU as a Regulator 
is stronger and more acceptable to the whole univer sity system including the open 
universities.   Therefore, the Madhava Menon Committee recommended  that the 
Government should issue a policy direction/notifica tion to UGC for assuming the 
responsibilities of maintaining standards in ODL system and creating a DECI like interim 
authority for the purpose. That is the reason why D EC had been shifted to UGC as an 
interim arrangement.  
 
9. The Ministry also informed the Committee that as  the Higher Education and 
Research Bill is unlikely to be cleared by Parliame nt, a decision has now been taken to 
have a separate legislative enactment as suggested by the Menon Committee for setting 
up of Distance Education Council of India and that the DECI Bill has been prepared.  A 
Cabinet Note would be prepared, the opinion of the Legislative Department would be 
taken and after following due procedure, the Bill will be introduced in Parliament.  
 
10. On the Committee’s query in regard to regulatin g technical education in distance 
mode, the Ministry clarified that even earlier when  the regulation of distance education 
was with DEC under IGNOU, it was only for general e ducation and that technical 
education is regulated by AICTE only.  An Order iss ued by the Ministry of Human 
Resource Development on 29 
th  December, 2012 gave direction to both UGC and AICT E 
to regulate distance education and that AICTE shall look at ODL for technical education. 
 
11. The Committee was further informed that DEC is not going out of existence 
because of its disassociation with IGNOU. DEC will be very much in existence, 
performing its current duties, but it will do so un der the UGC until the Higher Education 

and Research Bill is passed.  The Convenor, in his concluding remarks stressed that 
Parliament should not be bypassed.

I. Issue of taking over of Distance Education Counc il of IGNOU by UGC through 
administrative order  
2. At the outset, the Committee decided to hear fir st the representatives of IGNOU 
on the matter. While initiating the deliberations, the Chairperson expressed the 

Committee’s apprehension about transferring the fun ction of regulating distance 
education from DEC to UGC when the latter was alrea dy overburdened.  She also sought 
to know as to why IGNOU agreed to it and whether IGNOU ever objected to the proposal 
of shifting of DEC to UGC.  
 
3. The Vice Chancellor, IGNOU stated that IGNOU Act  entrusted it with the 
responsibility of promoting, coordinating and maint aining the standards of distance 
education in the country and DEC was created as an authority of IGNOU under Section 
16(7) read with Section 5(2) of the Act for this pu rpose.  He stated that the ‘Madhava 
Menon Committee’ recommended to create an independe nt regulatory body for distance 
education through a separate legislation and also r ecommended that the government may 
issue a policy direction/notification for UGC to re gulate distance education in the 
meantime. This was accepted by the Government and S tatute 28 establishing DEC was 
repealed. Subsequently, the Ministry of Human Resou rce Development, by an Executive 
Order dated the 29 
th  December, 2012, authorized UGC and AICTE to regula te distance 
education.  He also stated that IGNOU was for making DEC an independent body. 
 
4. The Committee observed that as far as giving the  mandate of DEC to UGC is 
concerned, it was a decision taken on the basis of the Madhava  Menon Committee  
recommendation and accepted by Government/Ministry.   The Committee also observed 
that there was no note of dissent attached to the M inutes of the meeting presided over by 
Vice- Chancellor, IGNOU and that the Minutes were w ritten and re-written thrice which 
in the Committee’s view has been done with mala fide  intention.     
 
5. The Chairperson expressed that if the Government  had created an independent 
and autonomous body through a separate legislation to regulate distance education, the 
Committee would not have had any objection.  Repeal ing Statute 28 while not coming 
before Parliament and shifting this responsibility to UGC by an executive order without 
amending the IGNOU Act reflects badly both on IGNOU  and the Ministry.  The 
Committee felt that these questions would be best a nswered by the Ministry of HRD and 
UGC. 

 
6. The Committee then heard the representatives of UGC on the matter. The 
Chairperson enquired how UGC having been burdened w ith extra work of regulating 
distance education felt about it.  She sought UGC’s  reaction on the issue as the Ministry 
had given them neither any grant nor any manpower for the purpose.  
 
7. Chairman, UGC submitted to the Committee that pr ior to 1991, the entire higher 
education was regulated by UGC which has the mandat e to maintain standards of 
teaching, examinations and research in higher educa tion. He further stated that UGC is 
happy about the transfer of DEC to them and that th ey have already put a system in place 
for this purpose.   He claimed that they had cleare d all pendency which was there when 
the work was transferred to them in December, 2012.   He also informed the Committee 
that previously, DEC was regulated through guidelines.  But now, they had come up with 
Regulations which had been sent to the Ministry of Human Resource Development for its 
concurrence. Once the concurrence of the Ministry i s received, the Regulations would be 
notified.  
 
8. Stating that taking responsibility was fine but whether it was done legally or 
illegally was the moot question, Chairperson expressed the concern of the Committee that 
this decision was taken by the Ministry by an Execu tive Order which could not be done 
without amending the IGNOU Act and the UGC Act.  Re sponding to the Committee’s 
concern, Chairman, UGC replied that under Section 2 0(1) of UGC Act, the Ministry can 
issue Directions.  The Ministry is within its manda te to issue Directions to UGC and 
UGC has also within its ambit to regulate distance education. Chairperson countered this 
argument saying that such Direction can be issued o nly in extraordinary circumstances 
but even in that case it would be a temporary solution.    
 
9. She stated that there was a basic difference bet ween the nature of formal 
education and distance education. Therefore, IGNOU was established to regulate, among 
others, distance education in the country because o f its vast area and population.  She, 
accordingly, sought Chairman, UGC’s  opinion on mix ing the two.   Chairman, UGC 

stated that there was a conflict of interest in the  sense that on the one hand IGNOU was 
itself a University and on the other hand it was al so entrusted with the responsibility of 
regulating distance education in other Universities  of the country, to which other 
universities were taking objection. Madhava Menon C ommittee recommended that until 
the establishment of an independent DECI through a separate legislation, the work of 
regulating distance education may be transferred to UGC.     
 
10. The Chairman, UGC expressed his opinion that th ere was no need to have another 
regulatory authority.  He was of the view that inst ead of creating a large number of 
regulatory bodies, we can have only one authority, an overarching body in the country for 
the purposes of regulating higher education, under which there could be a number of 
instruments to take care of the different facets of  education.  The Chairperson of the 
Committee  remarked that UGC was doing the responsi bility which had been ‘thrust 
upon’ them and thanked Chairman, UGC for doing his best to carry out its new mandate.   
 
11. In conclusion, the Committee observed that a faux pas  was made by the Ministry 
of HRD by hurriedly repealing DEC and transferring its work to UGC by an Executive 
Order and IGNOU did not put any kind of formal resi stance to this.  The Committee was 
of the view that these questions would be best answ ered by the Ministry of HRD. 
Accordingly, it decided to hear the Ministry of HRD  again before reporting the matter to 
the House.

13. A verbatim record of the proceedings of the Com mittee was kept. 
 
 The meeting adjourned at 5.17 p.m.

2.  While scrutinizing these Orders, the Committee note d that there was a 
considerable time lag between issue  of Notificatio ns and their laying in some 
cases. The annexed statement also indicates the per iod of delay in cases where 
Notifications have not been laid as per the time sc hedule prescribed by the 
Committee. The Committee observed that out of the t otal 133 delayed 
Notifications there were 119 Notifications where no  delay statement was 
appended to. However, the bulk of delayed Notificat ions were from the Ministry 
of  Road Transport and Highways which comes to arou nd 64.6% of the total 
delayed Notifications. 
 
The observations/recommendations of the Committee i n respect of the 
specific Ministries/Departments where delay in layi ng of Notifications has been 
noticed, are as follows: -  
 
(i) Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers (Department o f 
Pharmaceuticals)  
  
 Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers (Department of Pharmaceuticals) 
have laid 4 notifications (Sl. Nos. 19 to 22),  out of which 2 notifications (Sl. Nos. 
19 & 21) have been delayed. Both of the delayed not ifications have been delayed 
by 6 months and there is no delay statement attache d to any of these delayed 
notifications.  
 
 The Committee is not happy over the delay of 6 mon ths in laying of  
two notifications  by the Ministry of Chemicals and  Fertilizers (Department 
of Pharmaceuticals). Further there is no delay stat ement appended thereto 
giving details as to what caused such a delay. The Committee, therefore, 
impresses upon the Ministry to take care that such instances of delay do not 
recur in future and in case of any delay in laying,  a delay statement should 
invariably be appended thereto. 
  
(ii)  Ministry of Coal  
 
Ministry of   Coal have laid 4 Notifications (Sl. N os. 23-26). One of them 
(Sl. No. 25) has been delayed by 29 months  though  accompanied with  a delay 
statement. The reason given by the Ministry for del ay is that due to excessive 
work involving Coal investigation with CBI, SC, CBC , PAC, PMO etc., the 
Notifications could not be laid in time:-  
 

The Committee expresses its unhappiness over the fa ct that it took 2 
years and five months in laying of  one (out of 4) Notifications laid by the 
Ministry of Coal on the Table of the House. The rea sons cited for delay is 
that due to excessive work involved in reconstituti on of different branches in 
the Ministry of Coal and timely disposal of work fo r  Supreme Court, CBC, 
Public Accounts Committee, Central Bureau of Invest igation, Prime 
Minister’s Office and Attorney General relating to Coal allocation, the laying 
of Notification could not be accomplished timely. T he Committee would like 
to emphasise here that the work related to laying o f Notifications is not as 
complicated as the work relating to CBI enquiry in Coal allocation and 
Ministry was not left with sufficient time to accom plish the  Parliamentary 
work i.e. laying of Notification. The Ministry shou ld have accorded top 
priority to the Parliamentary work. The Committee a dvises the Ministry of 
Coal to endeavor to stick to the laying schedule st rictly so as to inform the 
Parliament about the Notification in time as this is a case of unusual delay. 
 
(iii) Ministry of Communications and Information Te chnology 
 
(a)   (Department of Electronics and Information Technology) 
  
 Ministry of Communications and Information Technology  (Department of  
Electronics and Information Technology)  have laid 2 Notifications (Sl. Nos. 31 - 
32).  Out of these, one Notification (Sl. No. 31) h as been delayed by 30 months 
and has no delay statement  appended to it. 
  
  The Committee takes a serious view, not only about the delay in 
laying of one of its Notification on the table of t he House, but also of its 
failure to append a delay statement with them. The Ministry/Department 
must know about the possible implications of failin g to meet this 
requirement. It must ensure to append a delay state ment in all such cases in 
future so that Parliament can be apprised of the reasons therefor.  
 
(b)  (Department of Telecommunications) 
 
Ministry of Communications and Information Technolo gy (Department of 
Telecommunications) have laid 9 Notifications (Sl. No. 35 to 43). Out  of these 
one Notification (Sl. No. 35) has been delayed by 9  months and has no delay 
statement appended to it.  
 
The Committee does not appreciate the delay in laying of Notifications 
on the part of Ministry of Communications and Infor mation Technology  
(Department of  Telecommunications) and would sugge st them to stick to the 
laying schedule as given in Committee’s 131 
st  Report. 
 
(iv) Ministry of Environment, Forests and Climate C hange  

  
 Ministry of Environment, Forests and Climate Chang e have laid 9 
Notifications (Sl. Nos. 104 to 112) on the Table of  the House during the Session. 
One of them  (Sl. No. 108) has been delayed by 6 mo nths and has no delay 
statement appended thereto. 
    
 The Committee observes that Ministry of Environment , Forests and 
Climate Change did not act promptly to lay the Noti fication (Sl. No. 108) on 
the Table of the House. Had they taken prompt actio n the delay would not 
have occured. The Committee, therefore,  recommends  that the Ministry of 
Environment, Forests and Climate Change  should act  promptly to avoid 
such delay and incase of delays in laying of Notifi cations, delay statements 
should invariably be accompanied with them.  
  
 
(v) Ministry of Finance 
(a)    (Department of Economic Affairs) 
 
 Ministry of Finance (Department of Economic Affair s) have laid 33 
Notifications (Sl. Nos. 115 to 147).  Out of these 6 Notifications (Sl. Nos. 132 – 
134 & 139 – 142) have been  delayed by 5 months to 13 months. There is no 
delay statement appended to any of these delayed Notifications.  
 
 The Committee are not happy with the delay in layin g of Notifications 
by the Ministry of Finance (Department of Economic Affairs) particularly 
Notifications at Sl. Nos. 132, 133 and 139 where de lay period spans from  a 
period of  9 months to over one year. In the absenc e of any delay statement, 
Committee would not know the reasons of delay and s uggest remedial 
measures for rectifying it. The Committee, therefor e, directs that the 
Ministry of Finance (Department of Economic Affairs ) append delay 
statements where there is delay in laying of Notifi cations and avoid 
recurrence of such delays in future.  
 
(b)    (Department of Financial Services) 
 
Ministry of Finance (Department of Financial Servic es) have laid 22 
Notifications (Sl. Nos. 148 to 169), out of which 1 0 Notifications have been 
delayed.  Out of 10 delayed Notifications,  6  Noti fications (Sl. Nos. 157 to 162) 
have  been delayed from 6 to 7 months and have no d elay statements attached to 
them. 4 Notifications (Sl. Nos. 148 to 151) have be en delayed  each by 6 months 
with delay statement appended thereto. The reasons forwarded by the Ministry for 
delay is as under:- 
 
“Gazette Notifications dated 12.12.2013 regarding a mendment in 
Regulations 50(1) & 50(6) of Andhra Bank (Employees ’) Pension Regulations, 

1995 and Regulation 4(1) of the Andhra Bank Officer Employees’ (Acceptance of 
Jobs in Private Sector concerns after retirement) R egulations, 2000 were 
published in the Gazette of India, No. 9 & 10 dated  08.01.2014. As the Bank 
furnished the requisite copies of Gazette Notificat ion after the stipulated period, 
clarification was sought from the Andhra Bank. 
The Bank has reported that amendments were publishe d in the Gazette on 
08.01.2014 and the copy of the Gazette Notification  were received on 17 th  
February, 2014. The Bank submitted the requisite nu mber of copies to this 
Department vide  letter dated 20.02.2014 which were received in thi s Department 
on 25.02.2014 after the stipulated time period. 
In view of above, the said Notification could not b e laid on the Table of 
the both the Houses during the last Session of Parl iament ending on 21.02.2014. 
Delay in this regard is deeply regretted and may please be condoned.” 
 
The Committee takes a serious view not only about t he delay in laying 
of ten Notifications  by the Ministry of Finance (D epartment of Financial 
Services) on the Table of the House but also of  it s failure to append the 
required delay statement. The Committee observes th at Parliamentary 
sessions are declared much in advance and had the M inistry of Finance 
(Department of Financial Services) taken prompt ste ps for laying of the 
notifications, in coordination with Banks for suppl y of Gazette Notifications,  
the delay could have been well avoided. It reflects  the bad management 
planning on the part of the Ministry. The Committee , therefore,  
recommends that the Ministry should complete the pr ocedural formalities at 
the earliest to avoid such kind of delays in future. 
 
 
(c) (Department of Revenue) 
 
 Ministry of Finance (Department of revenue) have l aid 166 Notifications 
(Sl. Nos. 170 to 335) during the 232 
nd  Session. Out of these 7 Notifications (Sl. 
Nos. 195 – 197, 217, 221 – 222  & 238) have been  d elayed by 5 months to 7 
months. There is no delay statement appended to any of these.  
 
 The Committee appreciates that the Ministry of Fina nce (Department 
of Revenue) has to lay a huge volume of statutory p apers during any 
Parliamentary Session.  While only 7 Notifications have been delayed, none 
had a delay statement appended to it.  As a result Committee does not know 
the reason for this delay. The Committee reiterates   its recommendations as 
contained in its 131 
st  and 135 th  Reports emphasizing timely laying of  
Notifications  on the Table of the House and append ing a delay statement 
wherever  there has been a delay. Not appending del ay statement is akin to 
infringement of Parliament’s right to know the facts of the case.  
 

(vi)  Ministry of Health and Family Welfare and Dep artment of Health  & 
Family Welfare 
 
 Ministry of Health and Family Welfare have laid 15 Notifications (Sl. 
Nos. 336 to 350), out of which 3 Notifications have  been delayed which ranges 
from 6 to 10 months. One Notification (Sl. No. 340)  has delay statement attached 
to it and another 2 Notifications have no delay sta tement appended to them. The 
reasons of delay given by the Ministry is as under:- 
 
 “The Ministry of Heal & Family Welfare has amended  the Pre-conception 
and Pre-natal Diagnostic Techniques (Prohibition of  Sex Selection) Rules, 1996 
vide the Notification No. G.S.R. 77(E) dated 31.01. 2014 – Pre-conception and

 The aforesaid Notification could not be laid on th e Table of both Houses

th  Lok Sabha and 231 st  Session

 Now, the Notification G.S.R. 77(E), dated 31.01.20 14 is proposed to be

 Department of Health and Family Welfare have laid 3 Notifications, out of 
which 2 Notifications have been delayed by seven mo nths each (Sl. Nos. 351-

 The Committee does not approve lackadaisical approa ch on the part

The Committee would like to draw attention of the M inistry to its

st  and 135 th  Reports for laying the

(vii) Ministry of Home Affairs 
  
Ministry of Home Affairs have laid 25 Notifications  (Sl. Nos. 356 to 380). 
Out of these 5 Notifications have been delayed by 5  to 33 months. There is no 
delay statement appended to 2 Notifications (Sl. No s. 361-362). 3 Notifications 
have delay statement appended to them (Sl. Nos. 364 , 367 and 369). The Ministry 
have cited administrative reasons for not laying the Notifications in time. 
 
The Committee hopes that the Ministry would avoid s uch instances of 
delay in laying of subordinate legislation in futur e and would remove lacuna, 
if any, administrative or otherwise, causing delay.  The Committee also 

impress upon the Ministry to take note of the fact that in case there is a delay 
in the laying of any Statutory Notification, the sa me should be accompanied 
by a delay statement while it is being laid . The Committee also advises the 
Ministry to avoid recurrence of delays due to administrative reasons. 
 
 
 (viii) Ministry of Power 
 
 The Ministry of power have laid 8 notifications ( Sl. Nos. 417-424) out of 
which 3 notifications (Sl. Nos. 418-420) have been delayed. The delay period 
ranges  from 6 to 8 months and all of delayed Notif ications have delay statements 
appended. The reasons for delay  given by the Ministry is  as under:- 
 
 “The Notification Nos. L-1/(5)/2013-CERC and  L-1/ 132/2013-CERC 
were published in the Gazette of India Extraordinar y dated 14 
th  November, 2013 
and 7 th  January, 2014. Copies of these Notifications could  not be laid on the table 
of the Rajya Sabha before conclusion of the Budget Session 2014 as printed 
copies of the same were received only on 8 th  January, 2014 and 30 th  January, 2014 
by Central Electricity Regulatory Commission from t he Department of 
Publication. The CERC forwarded the same to Ministry of Power on 5 th  February, 
2014. The Budget Session concluded on 21 st  February, 2014. Hence the 
Notification is laid on the first opportunity.” 
 
 
The Committee does not accept the late receipt of p rinted copies of 
Notifications as a valid reason for  delayed laying  of Notifications etc. The 
Committee does not accept this as a convincing reas on in respect of laying of 
statutory papers before the Parliament. The Ministr y of Power  should, 
therefore,  in future ensure that all its papers ar e laid before the House 
within the time frame as prescribed in the Committe e’s 131 
st  Report. The 
Ministry should take it up with the Ministry of Urb an Development for late 
receiving of printed copies of the Notifications. 
 
The Committee, therefore,  reiterates its earlier d irection to all the 
Ministries that in case there is delay in procuring  printed copies in time, they 
may obtain G.S.R. and S.O. numbers from the Governm ent of India Press 
and prepare requisite number of copies in cyclostyl ed form for laying in the 
Parliament as suggested by Secretary, Ministry of  Urban Development, the 
controlling Ministry of Government of India Press, in its meeting held on 30  
July, 2013. The Committee also once again recommend s that this process 
may be adopted by Ministries suo moto  on immediate basis so as to avoid 
such delays henceforth. 
 
(ix) Ministry of Road Transport and Highways 
 

Ministry of Road Transport and Highways have laid 1 70 Notifications (Sl. 
Nos. 428-597)  Out of these 86  Notifications (Sl. Nos. 428 – 485, 530, 550– 575  
& 597) have been  delayed by 6 months to 2 years an d 8 months. There is no 
delay statement appended to any of these delayed Notifications. 
 
 The Committee takes a serious note of the fact tha t Ministry of Road 
Transport and Highways have laid a number of Notifi cations without delay 
statements where delay has been inordinate. This re flects their negligence of 
Parliamentary practices and procedures.  Delay peri od of more than 2 years 
without  a delay statement, is a reflection on the functioning of the Ministry 
of Road Transport and Highways. The Ministry should , therefore,  look into 
the matter seriously to eliminate recurrence of such delays in future. 
 
 
(x) Ministry of Shipping 
 
The Ministry of Shipping have laid only one Notific ation (Sl. No. 598) 
which has been delayed by 6 months. The Ministry ha ve appended delay 
statement with the Notification and the reasons given by the Ministry is as under:- 
 
“The Merchant Shipping (Recruitment and Placement o f Seafarers’) 
Amendment Rules, 2014, were published in the Gazett e of India vide  Notification 
G.S.R. 33(E) dated 20 
th  January, 2014. Copies of the said Notification wer e 
personally obtained from Government of India Press,  Ring Road, Mayapuri, New 
Delhi by 19 th  March, 2014. As per instructions contained in the Rajya Sabha 
Secretariat O.M. No. RS.4/2014-T, dated 26/06/2014,  the said Rules were 
required to be laid on the Table of both the Houses  of Parliament within a period 
of 30 days. 
The reasons for delay in laying the paper on the Ta ble of both the Houses 
of Parliament is that there is no Parliament Sessio n convened during the 
intervening period i.e. 19 th  March, 2014 to 6 th  July, 2014. The said notification is 
now proposed to be laid on the Table of both the Ho uses in the current Budget 
Session of Parliament.” 
 
 The Committee expects the Ministry of Shipping  to  exercise caution 
in such matters and ensure that the schedule of lay ing of Subordinate 
Legislation, as prescribed by the Committee, is fol lowed meticulously in 
future.  
 
(xi) Ministry Social Justice and Empowerment 
 
 Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment  have l aid 3 Notifications 
(Sl. Nos. 599 to 601). 2 Notifications have been de layed. The delay period ranges 
from 7 to 8 months. No delay statement has been attached to both of these delayed 
Notifications.  

 
 The Committee are not able to know the reasons beh ind this delay in 
the absence of delay statements. Therefore, the Com mittee invites attention 
to its recommendation as contained in its 131 
st  Report  in this connection, 
where it is observed to append invariably delay sta tement(s) in case of delay 
in laying of Notifications by  the Ministry. 
 
 (xii) Ministry of Textiles 
  
The only Notification that the Ministry Textiles (S l. No. 602) have laid is 
delayed by 5 months. There is no delay statement attached to it. 
 
The Committee expects the Ministry of Textiles to l ay their papers on 
the Table of the House in time. Further, if there i s delay in laying, the 
Ministry of  Textiles is excepted invariably to app end a delay statement. 
Appropriate steps may be taken to prevent any delay  in future for laying of 
Notifications on the table of the  House by the Ministry of Textiles. 
 
 
 
(xiii) Ministry of Urban Development 
 
 Ministry of Urban Development have laid three noti fications on the table 
of the House. Out of which only one Notification ha s been delayed the delay 
period covers the span of six  months. The reasons of delay given by the Ministry 
is as under:- 
 
 “In accordance with Section 58 of Delhi Developmen t Act, 1957, every 
rules and every regulation made under this Act shal l be laid, as soon as may be 
after such rule or regulation is made, before each House of Parliament, while it is 
in session, for a total period of thirty days which may be comprised in one session 
or in two or more successive sessions aforesaid, bo th Houses agree in making any 
modifications in the regulation or both Houses agree that the regulation should not 
be made, the regulation shall thereafter have effec t only in such modified form or 
be of no effect, as the case may be; so, however, t hat any such modification or 
annulment shall be prejudice to the validity of any thing previously done under 
that regulation. As per rules, Notification was, th erefore to be laid in both the 
Houses of Parliament during the Budget Session, but  by the time the process was 
initiated for laying of the notifications, the Hous es were adjourned sine die on 
21.2.201”. 
 
 The Committee observes that Session are declared mu ch in advance 
and Ministries are well informed of the summoning o f Session 21 days in 
advance but Ministry of Urban Development has state d that by the time the 
process was initiated the Houses adjourned sine die . This reflects a pathetic 

attitude on the part of the Ministry to lay Parliam ent papers. The 
Committee, therefore, urge the Ministry of Urban De velopment to be more 
careful in future, and to lay the papers in time on  the Table of the Houses to  
avoid unreasonable delay in this regard. 
 
3.   Committee impresses upon all the Ministries/De partments to take 
immediate steps to ensure timely and proper laying of subordinate legislation. The 
Committee, accordingly, wishes to bring to the noti ce of all 
Ministries/Departments of the Government of India, particularly, the defaulting 
ones, the following recommendations, as contained i n its 131 
st 
, 135 
th 
, 152 
nd  ,   
192 nd  and 201 st  Reports: 
 “Orders required to be laid before the House shoul d be laid (i) if the 
House is not in Session, during the Session immedia tely following the date of 
publication of the Order in the Official Gazette an d (ii) if the House is in 
Session, on the date of the publication of the Orde r, during its continuance 
and in case the time lag between the date of public ation and the date of the 
closing of the Session is less than 15 clear days, before the expiry of the 
Session immediately following the said Session. All  the 
Ministries/Departments of Government of India shoul d henceforth comply 
with this schedule in the matter of laying of the O rders issued under various 
Acts of Parliament on the Table of the Rajya Sabha. 
(131 st  Report) 
(Presented on 15 December 2000) 
 
 “The Committee has, time and again, emphasized tha t it is essential that 
in case there is a delay in the laying of Statutory  Orders, the concerned 
Ministry/Department should invariably append a dela y statement along with 
the Notifications being laid so as to apprise Parli ament of the causes of delay. 
The Committee desires all Ministries/Departments to  take a note of this, 
since the intention is that through the process of formulation of a delay 
statement, the Ministry is able to introspect, iden tify bottlenecks and devise 
remedial measures”. 
(135 th  Report) 
(Presented on 27 July 2001) 
 
 “In the opinion of the Committee, every notificati on should be assigned a 
distinctive number in order to give it a separate i dentity and similarly, no 
notification should be published/laid which does no t carry a notification 
number. The Committee expects all Ministries/Depart ments of Government 
of India to exercise caution in this regard. In cas e where there are more than 
one Notifications under a single file, the Ministri es/Departments should 
ensure that the file number on each notification sh ould be suitably 
distinguished from one another.” 

(152 
nd 
 Report) 
(Presented on 26 August 2004)  
 
 “In addition to the concern expressed by the Commi ttee over delay in 
laying of Notifications on the Table of the House, the Committee also express 
their deep concern over delay in framing of rules/r egulations under different 
Acts. The Committee in its 47 
th  report presented to the House on 14.9.1981 
has recommended that the rule-making process should be completed within a 
period of six months of the coming into force on an  Act. The Committee has 
further recommended that in case a Ministry is not able to adhere to this 
time limit, it should seek extension of time for co mpleting the rule-making 
process. The recommendation of the committee reads as follows:- 
 
  “The Committee feels that the rule-making process could well 
have been completed within the time limit of six mo nths which the 
Committee has laid down for making of rules under a n Act after 
coming into force of that Act. Where however, a Ministry does not find 
it possible to adhere to the time limit, they shoul d inform the 
Committee of the reasons why they cannot make rules  within the time 
limit and seek extension of time for completing the  rule-making 
process.” 
 The Committee is constrained to take note of the f act that the 
Ministries/Departments of Government of India are n ot complying with the 
Committee’s recommendation to complete the process of framing of 
subordinate legislation contemplated under various Acts of Parliament 
within a period of six months. At the same time, th e Committee also does not 
receive requests for extension of time for completi ng the rule-making process 
in terms of its recommendations as above from most of the 
Ministries/Departments. The Committee takes a serio us note of the 
prevailing situation in which the Ministries/Depart ments are neither able to 
complete the task of framing rules/regulations unde r different Acts within 
the given six months’ period nor do they suo-motu  approach the Committee 
for seeking extension of time. The Committee furthe r notes that in order to 
ensure timely framing of rules/regulations it has t aken an initiative to 
monitor the progress of framing of subordinate legi slation in respect of all 
legislations brought about by different Ministries/ Departments of 
Government of India from the year 2003 onwards with  a view to ensure that 
the framing of subordinate legislation is not delay ed. The Committee, 
however, finds that the responses from the Ministri es/Departments have not 
been prompt in this monitoring exercise undertaken on behalf of the 
Committee. 
  
 In view of the above position, the Committee once again reiterates its 
recommendation that the Ministries/Departments shou ld ensure putting in 

place subordinate legislation positively within a p eriod of six months of 
coming into force of the Act. The Committee further  recommends that in 
case the Ministry fails to meet with this deadline,  they should invariably 
approach the Committee for seeking extension of tim e. The Committee 
further recommends that in cases where the time lim it of six months is not 
adhered to, they should, while laying rules/regulat ions before the Parliament 
invariably lay a statement explaining the reasons w hy the framing of 
rules/regulations was delayed beyond six months so as to keep the Parliament 
apprised of the compliance of the Parliament’s mand ate  conferred upon the 
Executive.” 
(192 
nd 
 Report) 
(Presented on 26 August 2011)  
 
 
  Rules/Regulations/Orders/bye-laws are laid by dif ferent Ministries on 
the Table of the House under various provisions of parent Acts passed by 
Parliament. These Rules/ Regulations/Orders/bye-law s are published in the 
official Gazette before being laid on the Table of the House. Even after they 
are laid, it is very difficult to get access to these Notifications. The Committee 
recommends that such Rules/Regulations/Orders, etc. laid on the Table of the 
House should be invariably uploaded on the websites  of respective Ministries 
immediately on the same day when they have been lai d on the Table of the 
House, for information of Members of Parliament and  people at large for 
their easy access. 
201 
st  Report 
(Presented on 14 th  December, 2012)  
 
 
 
The Committee observes that the whole process of en acting laws is 
defeated if rules are not framed and laid on the Ta ble of the House in time.  
A reasonable delay could be understood but unjustif iably long delays should 
be avoided and the Ministries should work towards i mproving this position.   
The Committee hopes that Ministry would strive to k eep the delay to the 
minimum and take care that Notifications are laid o n the Table of the House 
at the first available opportunity after publication of Notifications. 
  
The Committee would like to impress upon the Ministry that it is their 
responsibility to ensure that copies of the Notifications are printed timely and 
for this purpose, they need to evolve a suitable me chanism to ensure that 
notifications are laid in time.   The Committee is happy that the Ministry has 
evolved an internal mechanism/ procedure for this p urpose.  The Committee 
hopes that it would take action accordingly in orde r to comply with the 
prescribed schedule in the matter of laying of statutory Notifications. 
 

The Ministry must take appropriate step to remove l acuna, if any, 
administrative or otherwise causing such long delay  by being little proactive 
and prompt.  Further, the Ministries should take it  up with the Ministry of 
Urban Development for late receiving of printed copies of the Notification.

DRAFT REPORT  
ON  
THE KHADI AND VILLAGE INDUSTRIES COMMISSION RULES, 2006  
  
I.  BACKGROUND 
 
The Khadi and Village Industries Commission Rules, 2006 (Annexure-I)  
were framed in supersession of the Khadi and Villag e Industries Commission 
Rules, 1957, in exercise of powers conferred by Sec tion 26 (1) and (2) of the 
Khadi and Village Industries Commission Act, 1956. The rules were taken up for 
detailed examination by the Committee and a questio nnaire on the subject was 
forwarded to the Ministry of Micro, Small and Mediu m Enterprises for their 
comments/clarifications on 22 nd  August, 2007. The Ministry furnished their 
replies on 8 th  February, 2008 (Annexure-II) . During the course of its 
examination, the Committee also had discussion with  the representatives of (i) 
Khadi and Village Industries Commission (KVIC), Sta te Government of Jammu 
& Kashmir along with the Ministry of Micro, Small &  Medium Enterprises at 
Srinagar on 30 th  June 2012 and (ii) KVIC, State Government of Mahar ashtra 
along with the Ministry of Micro, Small & Medium En terprises at Mumbai on 
11 th  November 2014. Study note on the said study visits  are enclosed as 
Annexure-III & Annexure-IV respectively.  
 
2. The Committee enquired about the reasons that ne cessitated the framing of 
the Khadi and Village Industries Commission Rules, 2006, in supersession of the 
Khadi and Village Industries Commission Rules, 1957 . The Ministry replied that  
with a view to revamp the structure and functioning  of KVIC, the Government 
had constituted an Expert Committee in December 200 4 to recommend suitable 
measures for revamping of KVIC after reviewing its structure, functioning and 
performance. Based on the recommendations of the Ex pert Committee, KVIC 
(Amendment) Bill, 2005 to amend the KVIC Act, 1956 was drafted and 
introduced in the Lok Sabha on 22 
nd  August, 2005 and finally the KVIC 
(Amendment) Bill, 2005 as passed by both Houses of Parliament, after receiving 

the assent of the President in March 2006, became a n Act of Parliament and the 
amended provisions came into force with effect from 15 th  May, 2006. 
 
3. Consequent upon the amendment to KVIC Act, 1956 and also as per the 
provisions of the KVIC (Amendment) Act, there was a  necessity to suitably 
amend the then existing KVIC Rules, 1957 also. Acco rdingly, the Government of 
India, in supersession of the KVIC Rules 1957, noti fied the KVIC Rules 2006 in 
the Gazette of India on 17 
th  August, 2006. The KVIC Rules, 2006 were further 
amended vide  KVIC (Amendment) Rules, 2006 on 30 th  November, 2006 and 
KVIC (Amendment) Rules on 15 th  September, 2007. 
  
II EXAMINATION OF RULES, OBSERVATIONS AND 
RECOMMENDATIONS  
 
4. In response to the important points/ issues rais ed by the Committee 
through a detailed questionnaire and discussion wit h the   representatives of the 
Khadi and Village Industries Commission (KVIC), the  Ministry of Micro, Small 
& Medium Enterprises etc., the Ministry has furnish ed their comments/ 
clarifications which are elaborated in the succeedi ng paragraphs along with the 
observations/ recommendations of the Committee. 
 
5. Rule 7-Power to Appoint  
 “The Commission may appoint officers and other empl oyers as it 
considers necessary for the efficient performance o f its functions, with 
prior approval of the Central Government regarding creation of posts and 
filling of vacancies, in accordance with the Govern ment instructions in 
this regard.” 
  
The Committee pointed out that the Rules did not pr ovide for the terms 
and conditions of appointment like qualification, e xperiences, tenure, etc for the 
officers and other employees of the Commission. The  Committee suggested  that 
it would be more appropriate to provide terms and c onditions of service in the 

Rules itself as the existing provisions of Rule 7 w ere not specific. The Ministry 
replied that KVIC, with the previous sanction of th e Central Government, had 
framed various KVIC Employees’ Regulations for gove rning the service 
conditions of the employees. The qualifications, ex perience etc., of various 
categories of Group ‘A’ and Group ‘B’ posts of KVIC  have been provided in 
detail under the “Ministry of Industry, Khadi and V illage Industries Commission, 
Group ‘A’ and Group ‘B’ posts Recruitment Rules, 19 98” notified as G.S.R. 358 
(E) dated 26 th  June, 1998. Hence, the terms and conditions of app ointment like 
qualification, experiences, tenure, etc for the off icers and other employees of the 
KVIC have not been provided under the KVIC Rules, 2 006 and such inclusion in 
the KVIC Rules, 2006 would also not be appropriate.  The Committee noted the 
replies furnished by the Ministry. 
 
6. The Committee pointed out that  the words “important papers”  and “as 
early as practicable” in Rule 10(2) (a) were vague and capable of varied 
interpretation. The Committee proposed that these p rovisions should be made 
more precise and specific.  The  Ministry replied that the Commission, i.e. the 
decision making body as established under Section 4  of the KVIC Act, 1956 
normally holds its meetings only once in a month an d as per Section 5 (1) of the 
KVIC Act, the Chief Executive Officer (CEO), KVIC i s authorized to exercise 
such powers and discharge such functions in respect  of general superintendence 
over the affairs of the Commission and its day to d ay management as may be 
prescribed. Therefore, all the routine matters conc erning the day-to-day 
management of the affairs of the Commission need no t be referred to the 
Commission and the decisions on such routine matter s can be taken by the CEO. 
Only those important matters affecting the policy o f the Commission or requiring 
the approval of the Commission, papers relating to financial implication, etc. were 
to be submitted to the Commission in its meetings f or decisions. By Rule 
10(2)(a), the Chairman of the Commission was empowe red to cause those 
important papers and matters to be presented to the  Commission as early as 
practicable. The significance of the word “as early as practicable”  may be that 

since the Commission was meeting only once in a mon th, it may not be possible 
for the Commission to take decision on all the matt ers referred to it immediately. 
The Ministry accepted that a time limit of two cons equent Commission 
meetings may be fixed within which they need to be presented before the 
Commission and necessary changes may be effected ac cordingly. The 
Committee accordingly recommends that this should be incorporated in Rule 
10(2)(a) immediately.  
 
7. The Committee questioned the justification for a llowing submission of 
accounts by the Commission “normally” by the end of  October as prescribed in 
Rule 25  and asked whether there was any objection if the w ord “normally”  is 
deleted. The Ministry replied that the intention be hind mentioning the word 
“normally”  in Rule 25 may be to bring flexibility and to avoi d rigidity as regards 
the date of submission of account by the Commission . Since there was a 
provision in Rule 25 extending the date of submissi on of accounts by Central 
Government, the Ministry accepted the Committee’s s uggestion that the 
word “normally”  appearing in Rule 25 could be considered for delet ion. The 
Committee accordingly recommends that necessary ame ndment in Rule 25 
be carried out immediately.   
 
8. The Committee also questioned whether Government  had any objection in 
specifying the extended period beyond the end of Oc tober within which the 
Commission shall have to submit its accounts as pro vided in Proviso to Rule 25 . 
The Ministry replied that there was no need to chan ge the existing provision as 
the reports so submitted by KVIC were also required  to be laid on the Table of 
each House of the Parliament within a period of 9 months from the date of closure 
of KVIC’s accounts, i.e., by 31 December which is w ithin two months of the end 
of October. In case more time beyond December was r equired, extension of time 
had to be sought from the respective Houses of Parl iament. Therefore, there was 
no need to specify the extended period beyond the e nd of October as mechanism 

is already there in place to check the delays. The Committee noted the reply 
furnished by the Ministry. 
 
9. The Committee pointed out that the words “within a reasonable period”  
in Rule 26 (2)  were vague and suggested that a specific time peri od, say three 
months, be incorporated within the Rule itself. The  Committee also pointed out 
that the words “as it things fit”  may be substituted by the words “as it thinks fit” 
so as to rectify the typographical error. The Minis try accepted that a time limit of 
3 months may be prescribed as suggested by the Comm ittee and stated that this 
period was necessary considering the fact that the KVIC is having offices in 
different parts of the country and sometimes the re levant information may have to 
be collected from those offices. On several occasio ns further clarifications are 
also required to be obtained in the matter. As rega rds the suggestion for 
substituting the words “as it thinks fit” in place of the words “as it things fit” , 
action was being taken for correction of the same t hrough an amendment. The 
Committee is happy to note that the Ministry has ag reed that a specific time 
frame of three months may be prescribed to replace the words “within a 
reasonable period ” in Rule 26(2) and hopes that the Ministry will ca rry out 
the amendment expeditiously. The Committee also not es that the Ministry is 
taking action for substituting the words “as it things fit” with the words “as it 
thinks fit”  and recommends that the Ministry should carry out this 
correction immediately if not done so earlier. 
  
10. The  Ministry pointed out another typographical  error in line 5 of Rule 26 
(2) wherein the words “any defect or regularity”  appear while the correct words 
should have been “any defect or irregularity”  and stated that action was being 
taken to substitute the words “any defect or regularity”  with the words “any 
defect or irregularity” . The Committee recommends that the words “any 
defect or regularity”  should be substituted with the words “any defect or 
irregularity”  in line 5 of Rule 26(2) immediately so as to recti fy the 
typographical error.   

 
 
 
11. Rule 30 (2)  
“On receipt of a request under sub-rule (1) the Cen tral Government may 
constitute a Tribunal in accordance with the provis ions of section 19B of 
the Act and refer the question mentioned in such re quest to the Tribunal 
for decision.” 
 
The Committee queried whether there was any objecti on to specifying in 
the Rule itself the time period within which the Tr ibunal shall be constituted upon 
receipt of a request for its constitution. The Mini stry replied that it was felt that 
the existing provisions in this regard should be al lowed to exist keeping in view  
the difficulties/procedural delays in the constitut ion of Tribunal like identifying 
suitable person to be appointed as Tribunal, decidi ng the headquarters, etc., 
references to be made to the Legislative Department  of the Ministry of Law & 
Justice for the vetting of the notification for con stitution of such tribunals, 
preparation of authorized Hindi version of the Engl ish notifications, and getting 
these notifications published in the Gazette of Ind ia, which usually take 
considerable time. Therefore, it would not appear a ppropriate to prescribe any 
time limit. The Committee accepted the reply of the Ministry .  
 
12. Rule 31 (2)  
“The Commission may authorize the Chief Executive O fficer, the 
Financial Adviser or taking into account the recomm endation of the Chief 
Executive Officer in this behalf any other officer of the Commission, such 
powers of entering into contract on its behalf as it may think fit.” 
  
The Committee pointed out that the words “any other officer”  in Rule 
31(2) were vague and provide scope for excessive di scretion which is liable to be 
misused. The Committee suggested the Rule may speci fy the rank/designation of 

such an officer so that the delegation remains reas onable. The Ministry replied 
that the Committee’s suggestion had been considered and the existing words “any 
other officer”  were being considered for substitution by the word s “any other 
officer not below the rank of Director”  through an amendment to the KVIC 
Rules. The Committee notes with satisfaction that the Mini stry has accepted 
its suggestion to substitute the words “any other officer”  with the words “any 
other officer not below the rank of Director”  in Rule 31(2) so as to avoid 
excessive scope for discretion and accordingly reco mmends that the 
amendment should be carried out immediately.  
 
13. Rule 33 (2)  
“The Commission shall not be competent to modify, a mend or otherwise 
vary the provisions of the loan rules.” 
  
The Committee questioned the objective behind the p rovision of Rule 33 
(2).  In Committee’s opinion if loan rules are stat utory then obviously the 
amendments therein shall be as per the provisions o f the Act.  The Committee 
failed to understand the justification behind Rule 33 (2). The Ministry replied that 
it agreed with the views of the Committee and Rule 33 (2) was being considered 
for deletion through an amendment to the KVIC Rules . The Committee, 
accordingly, recommends that Rule 33(2) should be d eleted immediately as 
agreed to by the Ministry .  
 
14. Rule 34 – Power to borrow 
“The Commission may, with the previous sanction of the Government, 
borrow on the security of its funds or assets for t he purpose specified in 
section 21 of the Act.” 
 
 The Committee enquired about the terms and conditi ons under which the 
Commission has the power to borrow on the security of its funds or assets. The 
Ministry replied that the provision for borrowing m oney had been prescribed in 

the Section 21 of the Khadi and Village Industries Act, 1957 as, ‘Subject to such 
rules as may be made in this behalf, the Commission  shall have power to borrow 
on the security of the Khadi Fund or the Village In dustries Fund or any other 
assets for any purpose for which such funds may be applied. ’ The Ministry stated 
that the terms and conditions for granting loans we re generally laid down by the 
lending agency and not by the borrower. Hence no st andard terms and conditions 
had been prescribed by KVIC so far. However, KVIC w as being instructed to 
obtain the approval of the Central Government to th e terms and conditions of 
borrowing money if it decides to obtain any such lo an against security of its funds 
or assets for the purposes specified to Section 21 of KVIC Act, 1957.  The 
Committee noted the reply furnished by the Ministry. 
 
15. The Committee enquired about the method of calc ulation for writing off 
losses by the Commission  in Rule 35 and how the amount specified in the rules 
are arrived at. The Ministry pointed out that the “ Delegation of Financial Power 
Rules, 1978” were administered by the Ministry of  Finance, Department of 
Expenditure  and further amended by the “Delegation  of Financial Power 
(Amendment) Rules, 2001” on 23th October, 2001.  Th e revised monetary limits 
upto which the losses may be written off mentioned in Rule 35 of KVIC Rules are 
based on “Delegation of Financial Power (Amendment)  Rules, 2001”. The 
Committee noted the reply of the Ministry . 
 
16.  Rule 38 – Periodical returns 
“The Commission shall submit such periodical return s to the Government 
and to such other authority as it may specify. The returns shall be in such 
form as the Government may, from time to time, direct.” 
  
The Committee enquired about the present authority to whom the 
Commission is submitting the periodical returns and  questioned the 
reason/justification for allowing the Commission to  submit the periodical returns 
to an authority other than the Government. The Mini stry replied that the words  

“and to such other authority”  were being considered for omission through an 
amendment to the KVIC Rules. The Committee notes that the Ministry is 
considering omission of the words “and to such other authority”  in Rule 38 
and accordingly recommends that the Rule should be amended immediately. 
 
17. During the course of discussion with the repres entatives of the Khadi and Village 
Industries Commission (KVIC), State Government of J ammu & Kashmir along with the 
Ministry of Micro, Small & Medium Enterprises at Sr inagar on 30 th  June, 2012, the 
Committee was informed that the Khadi Reform and De velopment Programme had been 
initiated by the Government of India with support from Asian Development Bank to fully 
realize significant growth potential of KVI Sector in terms of employment generation; 
enhance earning of artisans and their empowerment a nd ensure positioning of khadi in 
consonance with current marketing needs. The Commit tee also noted that KVIC and 
KVIBs were implementing the Prime Minister’s Employ ment Generation Programme 
(PMEGP) and that KVIC was the nodal agency at the n ational level. Further, regarding 
human resource development, the Committee was infor med that KVIC was conducting 
training programme through 39 departmental and non- departmental training Centres and 
74,754 persons were provided training during the year 2011-12.  
 
18. The Committee appreciated that KVIC has made concer ted efforts in 
promotion of exclusive brands coupled with quality improvement and product 
development, design intervention and packaging. The  Committee noted that during 
this process, KVIC has expanded the coverage of pro ducts under it’s exclusive 
brands i.e. ‘Khadi’, ‘Sarvodaya’ and “Desi Aahar’ f or gaining customer confidence 
in KVI products and that the government has envisag ed a distinct identity for 
khadi, “Khadi Mark”, to guarantee the genuineness o f khadi sold in the market.  
This mark would help the customers to identify the difference between real and 
spurious khadi .  
 
19.      During the course of discussion with the r epresentatives of the Khadi and Village 
Industries Commission (KVIC), State Government of M aharashtra along with the 

Ministry of Micro, Small & Medium Enterprises at Mu mbai on 11 th  November, 2014, the 
Committee expressed its concern on the decline in t he popularity of the Khadi products. 
In response, the Committee was informed about the s teps taken in the recent past to 
reinvigorate Khadi like providing interest subsidy for setting up Khadi units; providing 
Marketing development assistance even on khadi sales; collaborating with Institutions for 
Research & Development in the field of Khadi tools & technology; and, initiation of a 
Khadi Reform Development Program. The Committee was  also informed that the 
Ministry was making efforts to make Khadi compulsor y in all government departments 
like Railways and government hospitals.    The Comm ittee felt that much more was 
needed to be done to promote Khadi and village indu stries. Amongst the foremost steps 
needed to be taken is to popularize it particularly  among the youth. It was felt that khadi 
is an instrument to help revive India’s rural secto r and provide a measure of financial 
security especially to rural women. 
  
III SUMMARY OF THE OBSERVATIONS / RECOMMENDATIONS  
OF THE COMMITTEE  
 
20. Rule 10 (2) (a) 
 
In Rule 10 (2) (a), the Ministry accepted that a ti me limit of two 
consequent Commission meetings may be fixed within which they need to be 
presented before the Commission and necessary chang es may be effected 
accordingly. The Committee accordingly recommends t hat this should be 
incorporated in Rule 10 (2) (a) immediately.   
 
 21. Rule 25  
 Since there is a provision in Rule 25 extending th e date of submission 
of accounts by Central Government, the Ministry acc epted the Committee’s 
suggestion that the word “normally”  appearing in Rule 25 can be considered 
for deletion. The Committee accordingly recommends that necessary 
amendment in Rule 25 be carried out immediately.   
 
 

 22. Rule 26(2)  
 The Committee notes that the Ministry has agreed th at a specific time 
frame of three months may be prescribed to replace the words “within a 
reasonable period ” in Rule 26(2) and hopes that the Ministry will ca rry this 
out expeditiously. The Committee also notes that th e Ministry is taking 
action for substituting the words “as it thinks fit” in place of the words “as it 
things fit”  and recommends that the Ministry should carry out this 
correction immediately if not done so earlier. The Committee also 
recommends that the words “any defect or regularity”  should be substituted 
with the words “any defect or irregularity”  in line 5 of Rule 26(2) immediately 
so as to rectify the typographical error.   
 
23. Rule 31(2)  
The Committee notes that the Ministry has accepted the suggestion of 
the Committee to substitute the words “any other officer”  with the words 
“any other officer not below the rank of Director”  in Rule 31(1) so as to avoid 
excessive scope for discretion and accordingly reco mmends that the 
amendment should be carried out immediately.  
 
24. Rule 33(2)  
The Committee fails to understand the justification  behind Rule 33 
(2). The Ministry replied that it agrees with the v iews of the Committee and 
Rule 33 (2) is being considered for deletion throug h an amendment to the 
KVIC Rules. The Committee, accordingly, recommends that Rule 33(2) 
should be deleted immediately as agreed to by the Ministry.  
 
 25. Rule 38 
 
The Committee is happy to note that the Ministry is  considering 
omission of the words “and to such other authority”  in Rule 38 and 
accordingly recommends that the Rule should be amended immediately.
