Report  
on  
The Framing of Rules & Regulations under  
the National Trust for Welfare of Persons with Autism, Cerebral Palsy, Mental Retardation 
and Multiple Disabilities Act, 1999  
 
 
Introduction 
 
1.  The National Trust for Welfare of Persons with Auti sm, Cerebral Palsy, Mental 
Retardation and Multiple Disabilities Act, 1999 (Commonly known as National Trust Act, 1999) 
was enacted on 30 
th  December, 1999. The Sections 34 & 35 of this Act p rovide for framing 
Rules and Regulations by the concerned Ministry as subordinate legislation.  As per its mandate, 
the Committee amongst others, scrutinizes the rules /regulations so made and reports to the 
Parliament its findings.  The Committee found that following rules and regulations have been 
prepared.   
 
(i)  National Trust for Welfare of Persons with Autism, Cerebral Palsy, Mental 
Retardation and Multiple Disabilities Rules, 2000 (notified on 26 th  July, 2000; and  
 
(ii)  National Trust Regulations, 2001 (notified on  3 rd  August, 2001).  
 
Mandate of the Act  
 
(ii)  The Act is a progressive piece of legislation which  seeks to achieve the following 
objectives: 
 
1.  to enable and empower Persons with Disabilities (Pw Ds) to live as independently 
and as fully as possible within and as close to the community to which they belong; 
2.  to strengthen facilities to provide support to PwDs to live within their own families; 
3.  to extend support to registered organizations to pr ovide need based services during 
period of crisis in the family of PwDs; 
4.  to deal with problems of PwDs who do not have family support; 
5.  to promote measures for the care and protection of PwDs in the event of death of 
their parent or guardian; 

6 
 
6.  to evolve procedures for the appointment of guardia ns and trustees for PwDs 
requiring such protection; 
7.  to facilitate the realization of equal opportunitie s, protection of rights and full 
participation of PwDs; and  
8.  to do any other act which is incidental to the aforesaid objects. 
 
 Shortcomings noticed in the Rules/Regulations 
  
(iii)  In view of the importance of this Act, it was decid ed to undertake these Rules & 
Regulations for examination.  The Committee during the course of examining/scrutinizing the 
Rules and Regulations framed under the National Tru st Act, 1999, noticed that these Rules & 
Regulations were not in the proper form as there we re several inexplicable discrepancies and 
gaps between the Act and the Rules/Regulations fram ed thereunder, both in letter and spirit.   
The Committee noticed the following: 
  
(i)   Not all the aspects provided in the Act had b een covered in the Rules and 
Regulations; 
(ii)   The provisions contained in the Rules and Re gulations were very sketchy and 
lacked necessary details; 
(iii)   At some places, both in the Rules and Regul ations, the provisions of the Act had 
been reproduced verbatim without specifying required details; 
(iv)   Certain powers have been abrogated under Rul es/Regulations that are not 
provided by the Act; 
(v)   No guidelines, rules and regulations are ther e in respect of registration, selection 
and grant/fund disbursal to various organizations working in the field. 
  
Oral Evidence of the Ministry 
 
4. The Committee thereafter, summoned the Secretary , Department of Disability Affairs, 
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment and the Ch airperson and CEO of the National Trust 
on 13 
th  May, 2014 for oral evidence. During the discussion , the Committee expressed serious 
reservations on the lack of comprehensive Rules/ Re gulations under the Act.  So many aspects 
where specific provisions were required to be made,  were left open ended.  For example, 

7 
 
Recruitment Rules for officials of the National Trust have yet not been framed.  When asked, the 
Ministry stated that files relating to this exercis e were untraceable.  The Committee was at a loss 
to know that the  draft Recruitment Rules were fram ed and approved by the Board but were 
never notified. Similarly, Recruitment Rules spelli ng out the qualifications, experience and other 
details for the post of Chairman, National Trust ha ve also not been framed. Issue regarding 
appointment of 'short term Consultants' was also ra ised.  The Committee wanted to know under 
which Section of the Act, short-term Consultants we re being appointed.  Neither the Secretary of 
the Ministry nor the Chairperson of the National Tr ust was able to give any legally 
convincing/tenable reason for doing so.  Similarly,  the Ministry was asked about the guidelines, 
if any for providing grants/funds to the intended c ategory of person and organizations and also 
about the guidelines regarding appointing Boards' Members.   
 
5. Responding to queries raised by the Committee, t he Secretary stated that the Ministry 
was not aware of these gaps in Rules/Regulations an d that it came to know only after the 
Committee Secretariat wrote them about it.  She ass ured that she will do as directed by the 
Committee in this regard.  After 2006, she said, fi les are missing and attempts are being made to 
reconstruct them and do the needful in "shortest possible time".   
 
6. Reacting to the prolonged continuance in office of the National Trust Chairperson and the 
Ministry's inability to find a successor, Secretary  clarified that the Section 3 (4)(a) of the Act 
which empowers the Central Government to appoint Ch airperson of the Trust does not contain any 
explicit provision for framing of Rules regarding s election of Chairperson unlike some other Acts.  
In the absence of explicit provision in the Act, Re cruitment Rules for selection of Chairperson 
have not been notified by the Ministry.  
 
7. The Committee is not convinced by this clarificatio n of the Ministry and is of the 
opinion that for the sake of transparency and clari ty, the rules, regulations, etc.  should 
have been framed even if the Act did not mention ab out it specifically.  The Committee 
does not accept the contention of the Ministry that  Section 3(4)(a) provided the areas of 
expertise of persons who could be considered for se lection to the post of Chairperson.  The 
Committee is of the view that provisions of an Act are generic in nature and it is not 

8 
 
possible to provide for every possible detail there in, otherwise, where was the need for 
delegated legislation to be done by the Ministries?   It is the Ministry which has to see that 
all the necessary processes/procedures and requirem ents for implementing the provisions 
of the Act are laid down to maximum possible extent  for the sake of clarity, transparency 
and accountability under intimation to Parliament.  Therefore, it was the responsibility of 
the Ministry to see that proper rules giving detail s of the basic qualifications including 
educational qualifications, essential as well as de sirable, number of years of experience, 
theoretical as well as practical, along with the pr ocedure for appointment of the 
Chairperson, National Trust with definite time-line have been framed. The Committee also 
took note of the fact that twice the request for ex tension of Chairperson, National Trust 
was sent to the Appointment Committee of the Cabine t (ACC), which had also raised 
serious objection regarding repeated attempt by the Ministry seeking extension to the same 
person at the post of Chairperson, National Trust f or almost one decade. Although 
attempts were made to recruit Chairperson but the m anner in which qualifications, etc. 
were being fixed and tweaked one after another and including M.Ed. and B.Ed. as 
qualifications for Chairperson, leave serious doubt s in one's mind.  One apprehension 
could be that the process of recruitment was being delayed deliberately on one pretext or 
the other so many times basically to allow the same  person to continue in the post as the 
Act said that same incumbent would continue till a next person was selected.  This 
apprehension in the mind of the Committee was recon firmed by the following observations 
of  DoPT sent to the Department of Social Justice & Empowerment: 
 
“…… to urgently examine whether the eligibility criteri a for the post are too restrictive 
given the fact that even after open advertisement a nd receipt of as many as 97 
applications not one person could be located who fu lfilled the prescribed educational 
qualification and experience” 
 
8. The Committee takes note of the following points : 
(a)  On the one hand the Ministry states that the Act does not provide for the framing of rules 
specifying the eligibility criteria in relation to educational qualifications and experience 

9 
 
for the post of Chairman of the National Trust, but  then detailed qualifications were 
published in the advertisement for the post of Chairperson, National Trust.  
 
(b)  Not finding any one suitable out of as many as 97 a pplicants and not having criteria for 
constituting Search/Selection Committee. 
 
(c)  Reasons for publishing a third advertisement for the post of Chairperson when the Search 
cum Selection Committee had found two eligible cand idates for the said post.  In the 
given situation, one could have been selected and r ecommended for appointment.  After 
all who, they were looking for? 
 
9. In the Committee’s view, such a situation came u p primarily because of the absence 
of Rules relating to qualification, procedure of re cruitment etc. of the Chairperson.  Due to 
absence of guidelines, etc. in this regard, the Com mittee feels that one person had managed 
to occupy the ‘post’ for close to a decade although  Act fixed its tenure for only three years.  
The Committee does not accept this argument of the Ministry that the National Trust being 
an autonomous body, it had nothing much to do in th is regard.  It is basically the 
responsibility of the Ministry to have seen that co mprehensive and all inclusive 
Rules/Regulations have been framed in consultation with Ministry of Law. 
 
10. It may be pointed out that despite the assuranc e given by the Secretary of the 
Ministry during her oral evidence to fill the gaps/ discrepancies in the existing Rules and 
Regulations , this Committee did not hear anything from the Ministry even after seven 
months.  However, the Committee has learnt that aft er it took up the issue with the 
Ministry, the existing Chairperson of the Trust has  resigned and the CEO of the Trust has 
been asked to leave.  Another curious aspect in thi s regard is that the Chairperson 
submitted her resignation on 1 
st  October, 2014.  But instead of taking a decision o n her 
resignation, she was given an extension upto 31 st  December, 2014 through an Office Order 
dated 22 nd  October, 2014.  Surprisingly, her resignation submitted on 1 st  October, 2014 was 
accepted through an Office Order dated 24 th  October, 2014 i.e.  two days after granting her 
extension. The Committee would like to be informed about the grounds on which the 

10 
 
Chairperson had resigned and the CEO was asked to l eave and granting her extension 
after she resigned, particularly when the Committee  was seized of the issue mentioned in 
this Report relating to the working of the National Trust.           
 
11. The Committee, therefore, recommends that the M inistry should, without any 
further delay, frame guidelines with details regard ing the basic qualifications including 
educational qualifications and experience along wit h the procedure for appointment of the 
Chairperson, National Trust.  
 
12. As regards the appointment/selection of Board M embers and their tenure, the Ministry 
informed that as per Section 3(4)(b) of the Nationa l Trust Act, 1999, 9 persons are to be 
appointed as Members from amongst Registered Organi zations, out of which 3 Members each 
shall be from Voluntary Organizations; Associations  of parents of persons with autism, cerebral 
palsy , mental retardation and multiple disability and Association of PwDs as per the procedure 
prescribed in Rules. The other Members of the Trust  are to be nominated from various 
Ministries/ Departments by the Government and from associations of trade, commerce and 
industry by the Board in terms of Section 3(4)(c) a nd (d) of the Act.  Further, the procedure for 
election of Members (for 9 Members in terms of Sect ion 3(4)(b) for the Act) has been prescribed 
under Rule 3 of the National Trust Rules, 2000. The re is no provision to debar a person from re-
election or re-nomination. The Ministry also stated  that since the National Trust is an 
autonomous organization, it is not involved in its day-today activities.      
13. The Committee notes the comments of the Ministr y and is of the considered view that 
regarding selection/nomination of Board Members exc ept ex-officio members, there should be 
some guidelines and procedure apart from the proced ure of election enshrined in Rule 3 of the 
National Trust Rules, with a view to ensure wider r epresentation to the organizations working in 
the field and to avoid only a few being able to get  them nominated/elected continuously.  It 
should have same cap in this regard and eligibility  restrictions for anyone indulging in 
unwarranted activities.   
 

11 
 
14. The Committee, accordingly, recommends that the  Ministry should frame Rules 
clarifying the procedure for selection of the Board  Members other than ex-officio and the 
said Rules should incorporate the views of the Comm ittee regarding re-nomination and 
removal of Members.  
15.  Regarding appointment of short-term Consultant s, the Committee observed that while  
Regulations 4(4) & 4(5) provided for appointment of  short term consultants, the Parent Act did 
not provide, directly or indirectly, for such a cla ss of consultants to be appointed .  Even if such 
provision  was made (which is illegal), again no guidelines/ rules were laid down for engaging the 
so called 'short term consultants'.  As a result, p ersons were engaged under this category at one’s 
whims and fancies.  Thus, the entire exercise was d esigned in a manner leaving enough scope to 
be misused.   
16. The Committee expresses serious reservations on  this issue and recommends that 
the Ministry should re-examine the said Regulations and also have it vetted by the Ministry 
of Law & Justice for ironing out any such discrepan cies in the subordinate legislation 
framed by the National Trust/ Ministry.  
17. Regulation 7(1) & 8(1 & 2) of the Board of Trust Regulations, 2001 lays down Procedure 
for Grant of Registration and Procedure of Evaluati on of Registered Organization for 
Participation in Trust’s Scheme and Programmes.  The Committee observed that Section 12(4) of 
the Act empowers the Board to grant registration to  applicants or reject such applications.  For 
the purpose, Trust has to frame and  notify Regulat ions providing minimum standards for 
registration as provided for under Section 35 of th e Act.  The Committee is surprised that 
instead of framing the Regulations on  minimum stan dards for registration, it has further 
delegated the power to the Board under Regulation 7  (1) , which is against the spirit of the 
Act. 
18. In another instance, the Committee again found that Sections 19 and 35(g) of the Act lays 
down provision for framing of Regulations on the pr ocedure for evaluation of registered 
organizations for participation in the Trust’s Sche me and programmes.  The Act further says that 
the Regulations may also provide for guidelines to monitor and evaluate the activities of the 
registered organizations receiving financial assist ance from the Trust.  The Committee takes 

12 
 
serious note of the fact that instead of framing pr oper criteria for participation in the 
Trust’s Schemes and Programmes and explaining/ deta iling the mechanism for evaluation 
and monitoring in Regulations itself, it has again further delegated the responsibility to the 
Board.   
19. Taking a serious view in the matter, the Commit tee recommends that the Ministry 
should seriously go through the Regulations framed and ensure that such further 
delegation of power, which is against the spirit of   the Act is avoided.  The Committee 
further recommends that the Ministry should refrain  from reproducing the provisions 
from the Act in the Regulations and wants that Regu lation 7(1) and 8(1) & (2) may be 
redrafted specifying the required details.    
20. Another fact that came to the Committee's notic e related to the legal status of the 
"ARUNIM" by the National Trust.  This Trust was cre ated in 2008 for marketing of goods and 
services of various NGOs registered with National T rust and other working with persons with 
disabilities.   Large numbers of grants were being released to this organization by the National 
Trust for their future expenditure.  The ARUNIM is said not to be following any Government 
rules, regulations, guidelines of the National Trus t and several audit objections were raised on 
the release of funds or advances given to it from N ational Trust Account.  Interestingly, the 
ARUNIM never considered it as a part of National Tr ust and therefore, resisted any 
watch/control over its funds and working.  Even the  Ministry was aware of this irregularity 
committed both in its creation as well as funding.   
21. The Committee takes this very seriously and fee ls that this is another off-shoot of 
the lack of distinct rules, regulations, etc. for r unning the National Trust and it also 
reinforces the Committee's apprehensions that such a situation was suitable to the vested 
interest and they had conveniently forgotten to lay  down rules and regulations for 
introducing proper command and control in the worki ng of the Trust.     The Committee 
would like to have a Report on the ARUNIM delineati ng its legal status and as well as the 
legality of the funds released to this organization  so far and the Ministry's response 
thereon. 
 

13 
 
CONCLUSION 
22. The Committee is pained to find that sensitivit y shown by Parliament to have made 
a pioneering law to provide much needed help and su ccour to the most vulnerable and 
needy sections of our society is being dealt in the  most insensitive and callous manner.  The 
manner in which this law is being implemented leave s much to be desired.  The absence of 
specific guidelines, rules, regulations, etc. on various aspects for enforcing the Act as per its 
letter and spirit, has bred to secrecy, scope for discretion and hence lack of transparency in 
the working of National Trust.  Thus, the Ministry due to reasons best known to it, failed to 
perform its responsibility as an administrative con troller as it did not carefully see that all 
the Guidelines, Rules and Regulations have been fra med.  More serious thing is that the 
Ministry, it appears, did not consult Legislative D epartment in vetting the Rules, 
Regulations as is usually done by all the Ministrie s.  Had it been done so, much of the 
problems pointed out by the Committee now may not have arisen at all.   
23. The Committee re-emphasizes that the Ministry s hould expedite framing the 
Recruitment Rules not only for the post of Chairman , National Trust but also for the 
officers and employees of the National Trust at the  earliest.  The Committee is of the view 
that this process can be completed in a fixed time schedule given that much ground work 
on the educational qualifications and experience re quired for the said post has already 
been done with help of DOPT.  Even the suggestions of the DoPT have not been properly 
ingrained into the existing criteria.  Further, not ifying the Rules would give the candidates 
an opportunity to know the requirements for the req uisite post apart from giving publicity 
to the working of the National Trust. 
 
24. The Committee recommends that the Ministry shou ld re-visit the Rules/  
Regulations framed under the National Trust for Wel fare of Persons with Autism, 
Cerebral Palsy, Mental Retardation and Multiple Dis abilities Act, 1999 and re-examine 
them in the light of the observations made by the C ommittee in the preceding paragraphs 
and effect necessary modifications as needed. 
 

14 
 
25 . The Committee further recommends that the Ministry may look into the possibility 
of increasing the Corpus Fund of the National Trust . In Committee’s view, lack of 
adequate funding should not be a limiting factor fo r the working of the National Trust for 
fulfilling its mandate.  Increased corpus is needed  urgently keeping in view the enhanced 
coverage of the schemes being operated by the National Trust.  
 
 26 .  The Committee is hopeful that the Ministry would ca rry out the recommendations 
of the Committee expeditiously under intimation to it. The Committee would further like to 
impress upon the Ministry that proper monitoring an d inspection are essential for the 
proper and effective implementation of Rules and Re gulations, and, stresses upon the 
Ministry to strengthen its enforcement mechanism to  ensure that the objectives of the 
Order are achieved.

2.  While scrutinizing these Orders, the Committee noted that there was a considerable time lag 
between issue  of Notifications and their laying in  some cases. The annexed statement also 
indicates the period of delay in cases where Notifi cations have not been laid as per the time 
schedule prescribed by the Committee. The Committee  observed that out of the total 280 delayed 
Notifications, there were 145 Notifications where n o delay statement was appended to. However, 
the bulk of delayed Notifications were from the Min istry of  Road Transport and Highways which 
comes to around 83.5% of the total delayed Notifications. 
 
The observations/recommendations of the Committee i n respect of the specific 
Ministries/Departments where delay in laying of Notifications has been noticed, are as follows: -  
 
(i) Ministry of AYUSH  
  
 Ministry of AYUSH  have laid one Notification (Sl.  No. 15) which is delayed by 5 months. 
There is no delay statement  appended thereto.  
 
 The Committee is anguished to note that Ministry o f AYUSH have delayed the laying 
of their only Notification by 5 months and there is  no delay statement attached thereto. The 
Committee observes  that the Ministry of AYUSH stri ctly adheres to the time schedule as 
recommended by Committee  in its 131 
st  Report  in laying of the Subordinate Legislation 
before Parliament. Further, where there is delay in  laying of the notifications, a delay 
statement should also invariably be appended therewith. 
  
(ii)  Ministry of Commerce and Industry 

 (Department of Commerce)  
 
Ministry of Commerce and Industry (Department of Co mmerce)  has laid  one Notification  
and that has no delay statement appended thereto. The delay period is of 8 months. 
 
The Committee is not happy about the delay in layin g of the only one Notification by 
the Ministry of Commerce and Industry (Department o f Commerce) on the Table of the 
House but also failure to append the delay statemen t with it. The Ministry/Department must 
ensure that Notification to be laid on the Table of  the House should be laid in time. It also 
must ensure to append a delay statement in all cases in future. 
 
 
 
 
 
(iii) Ministry of Communications and Information Te chnology 
(Department of Telecommunications) 
 
Ministry of Communications and Information Technolo gy (Department of 
Telecommunications) have laid 5 Notifications (Sl. No. 25 to 29). Out  of these, 3 Notifications (Sl. 
Nos. 27-29) have  been delayed. There is delay of 4  months in each case and no delay statement 
has been  appended.  
 
The Committee is constrained to note  that 3 out of  5 Notifications that Ministry of 
Communications and Information Technology (Departme nt of Telecommunications) have 
laid, have been delayed. Further, there is no reaso n given for this delay.  This is in 
contravention of Committee’s recommendation given i n its 135 Report that Notifications 
which are delayed should invariably be accompanied by a delay statement. The Committee 
would like the Ministry of Communications and Infor mation Technology (Department of 
Telecommunications)  to take necessary steps to obviate such delays and in case of delay in 
laying of Notifications, delay statements should invariably be appended to them. 
 
(iv) Ministry of Corporate Affairs 
 
 Ministry of Corporate Affairs  have laid 27 Notifi cations (Sl. Nos. 36 to 62) out of which 7 
Notifications have been delayed by 4 to 6 months. T here is no delay statement  appended to 6 of 
these delayed Notifications and only one Notificati on (Sl. No. 46) delay statement is attached. The 
reason of delay given by the Ministry is as under:- 
 
 “The Notification relating to the G.S.R. No. 397 (E ) dated 12.06.2014 on the Amendment 
in Rule 3 for sub-rule (5) of the Companies (Declar ation and Payment of Dividend) Amendment 
Rules, 2014 was sent to Government Press for printi ng. The Said Notification could not be laid 
before both the Houses of Parliament during the Bud get Session of the Parliament, 2014 due to 
delay in receiving the Gazette copy of the said Not ification by this Ministry and when it was 
collected, the session was over on 14.08.2014. The said Notification got delayed and hence it may 
be kindly be condoned.” 
 
 The Committee have time and again pointed that dela y in receiving printing copies of 
Notifications from the Government Press, is a lame excuse. Ministry of Corporate Affairs 
should plan beforehand that ample time is given to printing press  so that printed copies are 

received timely. The Committee suggests the Ministr y of Corporate Affairs to take adequate 
precaution to avoid such delay in future and append delay statement where  required. 
 
 
 
(v) Ministry of Environment, Forests and Climate Ch ange  
  
 Ministry of Environment, Forests and Climate Chang e have laid 7 Notifications (Sl. Nos. 
63 to 69) on the Table of the House during the Sess ion. Three of them  (Sl. Nos. 63-65) have been 
delayed by 4 months to 8 months and no delay statement is appended to any of these Notifications. 
    
 The Committee have emphasized the timely laying of Notifications on the Table of the 
House in its 131 
st  Report. Further, Committee has emphasized in its 135 th  Report that a delay 
statement should invariably be appended in case of delay in laying of Notifications. Ministry 
of Environment, Forests and Climate Change  have not only delayed the laying of 
Notifications on the Table, but also failed to appe nd a delay statement which is negligence on 
the part of Ministry of Environment, Forests and Cl imate Change  towards adhering to the 
Committee’s recommendations of another takes a serious  view of this negligence.  
  
(vi) Ministry of Finance 
(a)    (Department of Economic Affairs) 
 
 Ministry of Finance (Department of Economic Affair s) have laid 32 Notifications (Sl. Nos. 
71 to 102).  Out of these, 17 Notifications (Sl. No s. 76 – 89, 91 –  92 & 96) have been  delayed by 
5 months to 8 months. There is no delay statement appended to any of these delayed Notifications.  
 
 The Committee notes with regret that the Ministry o f Finance (Department of 
Economic Affairs) have made inordinate delay in lay ing of Notifications. Neither is there a 
delay statement appended therewith to know the reas ons of such delay. The Committee 
would like the Ministry of Finance (Department of E conomic Affairs) to take corrective 
measures so as to curtail delay in future and in ca se such delay does take place it should 
invariably be accompanied by statements giving the reasons for the delay in laying.  
 
(b)    (Department of Financial Services) 
 
 Ministry of Finance (Department of Financial Servic es) have laid 10 Notifications (Sl. Nos. 
103 to 112) out of which 2 Notifications (Sl. Nos. 104 – 105) have been delayed by five months 
and there is no delay statement appended to both these Notifications. 
 Another Notification (Sl. No. 109) has been delaye d by six months with delay statement 
appended thereto. The reason for delay given is as under:- 
 
“The Notification regarding amendment in Syndicate Bank Officers’ Service Regulations, 
1979 incorporating the provision of the Joint Note dated 02.06.2005 on pay revision for officers 
was published in the Gazette of India, No. 24 dated  June 14 – June 20, 2014. The Bank has stated 
that they received copy of the Gazette Notification  from Department of Publication late and hence, 
there was delay in submitting the papers in time. W hile regretting the delay, Bank has noted to 
comply with the time schedule in future.” 
 
 

The Committee notes that the Department of Financia l Services (Ministry of Finance) 
have again failed to strictly adhere to the time schedule in laying of Gazette Notifications. The 
Committee recommends that the Department of Financi al Services (Ministry of Finance) 
should put an effective mechanism in place to elimi nate such instances of delay in future, 
particularly, finalization of the work of laying of  paper by the Department of Financial 
Services. The Committee further recommends that the  Ministry of Finance should put in 
place checks and counterchecks so that such delays do not recur in future. 
 
 
(c) (Department of Revenue) 
 
 The Ministry of Finance (Department Revenue) have laid 59 notifications (Sl. Nos. 113 – 
171). Out of these, 7 Notifications  have been  del ayed with delay period of 4 to 6 months and no 
delay statement is attached  with them except with two Notifications (Sl. Nos. 113 – 114 ). The 
reasons forwarded by the Ministry for delay in this case is as under:-  
 
 “The Central Board of Excise & Customs has issued two  notifications G.S.R. 335 (E) and 
G.S.R. 336 (E) dated 12.05.204 for operationalising  the provisions of the Agreement between the 
India-Taipei Association in Taipei and the Taipei E conomic and Cultural Center in India on the 
FICCI/TAITRA Carnet for the Temporary Admission of Goods which was signed on 20 
th  March, 
2013. 
 
 These two notifications have come into effect on 1 2 
th  May, 2014, i.e., the date of its 
publication in the Gazette of India. 
 The aforesaid two notifications could not be laid down before the Parliament during 2 
nd  
Session of 16 th  Lok Sabha as the Government of India Press, Mayapu ri, Delhi could not provide 
requisite copies of the Gazette of India of the notifications in time.” 
 
 The reasons cited by Ministry of Finance (Departmen t of Revenue)  i.e. Notifications 
could not be laid down because the copies of Notifi cations could not be provided by the 
Printing Press in time, is an oft-repeated excuse. It is a Constitutional provision to lay the 
notification within the prescribed time schedule an d the Ministry should have taken 
appropriate action to lay the same in time on the T able of the House. It reflects the 
lackaidaical approach on the part of the Ministry. The Committee, therefore, impress upon  
the Ministry to  devise suitable mechanism to avoid  such instances of delay in future, 
particularly, on account of delay in getting printed copies of Notifications from Printing Press 
so as to adhere to the time schedule as prescribed in Committee’s 131 
st  Report.  
 
 
(vii)  Ministry of Health and Family Welfare  
 
 Ministry of Environment and Forests have laid 3 Not ifications (Sl. Nos. 172 to 174).  Out 
of these, 2 Notifications (Sl. Nos. 173–174) have been delayed by  12 months and there is  no delay 
statement appended  to any of these delayed Notifications. 
 
 The Committee is constrained to note that there has been inordinate delay in  laying of 
the two Notifications by the Ministry of Health and  Family Welfare. Moreover, there is no 
delay statement appended to throw light on the fact ors which caused this delay. Further, the 
Committee have clearly mentioned in its 135 
th  Report that delay statements should invariably 
be appended where there is delay in laying of Notif ications but Ministry has failed to do this. 
The Committee, therefore, impresses upon the Minist ry to strictly adhere to the time 

schedule as prescribed in Committee’s 131 st  Report and  in case of any delay in laying, delay 
statement should invariable be appended.  
  
  
(viii) Ministry of Home Affairs 
  
Ministry of Home Affairs have laid 32 Notifications  (Sl. Nos. 176 to 207). Out of  these,  4  
Notifications have been delayed by 4 to 9 months. T here is no delay statement appended to 3 
Notifications (Sl. Nos. 176-177 & 199). Only one No tification has delay statement (Sl. No. 189). 
The reasons for delay  given by the Ministry is  as under:- 
 
“As per instructions of the Committee on Subordinat e Legislation, Recruitment Rules, 
(PRs) are required to be laid on the Table of both the Houses of Parliament within a period of 15 
days after its publication in official gazette, if the Houses are in session and if the Houses are not in 
Session, the same should be laid as soon as possibl e after the commencement of the following 
session. 
The printed copies of the Border Security Force Com batised Assistant Sub Inspector 
(Steno) and Head Constable (Ministerial) Recruitmen t (Amendment) Rules, 2014 (PRs) were 
delivered by Government of India’s printing press to BSF on 12 
th  August, 2014 and received in this 
Ministry on 13 th  August, 2014. The last session of the Parliament w as in motion from 07.07.2014 
to 14.08.2014. The authenticated copies of PRs were  sent to the Rajya  Sabha and Lok  Sabha 
Secretariat on 14.08.2014 but were not accepted as the session was concluded on that day itself. 
Therefore, these Rules could not be laid on the tab le of both the Houses of Parliament due to 
insufficient time.” 
 
 Although one-eighth of the total Notifications are  delayed, yet the Committee is to see 
that statutory obligation of laying the notifications as the Table of House as prescribed by it is 
fulfilled by the Ministries. It is for the Ministri es to see that this job is performed by them 
without flaw but Ministry of Home Affairs have fail ure on this count. Therefore, Committee 
urges upon the Ministry of Home Affairs to see to i t that hurdles causing delay in laying of 
Notifications, such as conclusion of Parliament Ses sion, should have been handled 
beforehand or preparations for laying made earlier so that the situation could have been 
avoided. 
 
 
(ix) Ministry of Personnel and Public Grievances an d Pensions 
 (Department of Personnel and Training) 
  
The Ministry of Personnel and Public Grievances and  Pensions (Department of Personnel and 
Training)  have laid 19 Notifications (Sl. Nos. 225 - 243). Ou t of these, 2 Notifications (Sl. Nos. 
241 & 243) have been delayed by five months to elev en months. There have no   delay statement 
appended to both of the them.  
 
The Committee, time and again, have emphasized that  laying of 
rules/regulations/orders is a statutory obligation of the Ministries and should be completed 
on priority within specified time-frame. The Minist ry of Personnel and Public Grievances 
and Pensions (Department of Personnel and Training)  should understand the implications of 
such failures. However, the Ministry of Personnel a nd Public Grievances and Pensions have 
failed to comply with the recommendations of the Co mmittee in this regard. This is in 
violation of the recommendation of the Committee in  this regards. The Committee 
emphasizes that Ministry should adhere to the time schedule in laying of Notifications as 

prescribed in Committee’s 131 st  Report and append a delay statement in case there is  delay 
in laying. 
 
(x) Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas 
 
The Ministry of  Petroleum and Natural Gas have lai d 10 Notifications (Sl. Nos. 244 – 253) 
out of which 8 Notifications (Sl. Nos. 246 – 253) h ave been delayed by 8 to 9 months. No delay 
statements have been appended to any of them. 
 
The Committee reiterates its earlier recommendation , that in case of delay in laying, 
notifications should be accompanied with delay stat ement. Attention to recommendation 
contained in 135 
th  Report of the Committee is drawn here. The Ministr y should take care 
that repetition of such delay is avoided in future.  
 
 
(xi) Ministry of Power 
 
The Ministry of  Power have laid 9 Notifications (S l. Nos. 254-262). Out of these,  4  
Notifications have been delayed. The delay period r anges from 5 months to 9 months. All 
Notifications delayed are accompanied by delay stat ement. The reasons for delay given is as 
under:- 
   
  “The Notifications No. L-1/144/2013-CERC and No. L-1/148/2014-CERC were published 
in theGazette of India Extraordinary dated 12 
th  March, 2014 and 10 th  June, 2014 respectively. 
Printed copies of the same were received on 19.06.2 014 and 08.07.2014 by Central Electricity 
Regulatory Commission from the Department of public ation. However, CERC forwarded the same 
to Ministry of Power on 7 th  November, 2014 and 13 th  November, 2014  only. Therefore these 
Notifications could not be laid on the Table of the  Rajya Sabha before conclusion of the Monsoon 
Session on 14 th  August, 2014. CERC has regretted the delay in layi ng of the above Notifications. 
The Notifications are laid on the first opportunity.” 
  
The Committee has noted the reply given by the Mini stry of Power in regard to delay 
in laying of Notifications on the Table of the Hous e. The Ministry of Power  should in future 
ensure that all its papers are laid before the Hous e as prescribed in the Committee’s 131 st  
Report. Ministry should frame a suitable mechanism for this purpose. 
  
(xii) Ministry of Railways 
 
 The Ministry of Railways have laid 4 Notifications  (Sl. Nos. 263 – 266) and one of these 
have been delayed by 7 months. There is no delay statement appended with the Notification. 
  
 The Committee is unhappy over the delay in laying o f one of its Notification on the 
Table of the House. The Committee desires the Minis try of Railways to strictly adhere to the 
time schedule in laying of Notifications and should  append delay statement in case of any 
delay. The Committee further stresses that the Mini stry of Railways should append a delay 
statement where there is delay in laying of Notification on the Table of the House.  
 
 
(xiii) Ministry of Road Transport and Highways 
 

 The Ministry of Road Transport & Highways have lai d 318 Notifications  on the Table of 
the House (Sl. Nos. 267 to 584) 214 Notifications h ave been delayed out of which 123 
Notifications are accompanied by delay statements a nd 91 Notifications have no delay statements 
appended with them. The delay period ranges from 4 months to 18 months. The reasons given by 
the Ministry is that it took some time to complete the procedural formalities and therefore, papers 
could not be laid in time. 
 
 The Committee observes that the Ministry of Road T ransport and Highways lays a 
large number of Notifications every Session. This i s a voluminous task being handled by the 
Ministry of Road Transport and Highways. However, t he Committee find that 2/3 rd  of total 
Notifications laid by the Ministry of Road Transpor t and Highways have been delayed and 
only one third of the total Notifications are laid in time. The Committee notes the reasons for 
the delay given by the Ministry  that it took ‘some  time’ to collect the papers and complete 
the procedural formalities,  but cannot accept such  inordinate delay as of 18 months for 
laying of papers. The Committee feels that if the Ministry can lay some papers  in time, it can 
also lay other papers likewise, only due precaution  is required therefor. The Committee 
further surprisingly notes that even after delay of  one year in certain cases, the  Ministry did 
not care to append a delay statement so as to apprise the Parliament of the reasons of delay in 
laying of Notifications. The Committee hopes that M inistry will get this job accomplished in 
timely manner in future and keep the Parliament informed of the reasons of delay. 
 
(xiv) Ministry of Rural Development 
 (Department of Rural Development) 
 
Ministry of Rural Development (Department of Rural Development)  have laid 2 
Notifications (Sl. Nos. 585-586) during the Session . Out of these, one notification (Sl. No. 586) 
was delayed  by 4 months and there is no delay statement appended to it. 
 
The Committee observe that  the Ministry of Rural D evelopment has not complied 
with the recommendations of the Committee as contai ned in its 131 
st  Report in regard to 
laying of statutory notifications on the Table of t he House. The Committee desires that 
Ministry of Rural Development should adhere to the time schedule in laying of Notifications 
as prescribed in Committee’s 131 st  Report and append a delay statement in case there is  
delay in laying. 
 
 
 
(xv) Ministry of Shipping 
 
The Ministry of Shipping have laid only 4 Notificat ion (Sl. Nos. 587 - 590) out of which 2 
Notifications have been delayed by 4 to 6 months. The Ministry has appended delay statement with 
both the delayed Notifications and the reasons given by the Ministry is as under:- 
 
“The Merchant Shipping (Management for the Safe Ope ration of Ships) Amendment Rules 
2014 were published in the Gazette of India vide No tification GSR 351 (E) dated May 23, 2014. 
As per the instructions contained in the Rajya Sabh a Sectt. O.M. No. RS. 4/2014-T dated 
26/06/2014, the said Rules were required to be laid  on the Table of both the Houses of Parliament 
within a period of 30 days. 
Copies of the said Notification could not be obtain ed from the Government of India Press, 
Ring Road, Mayapuri, New Delhi on time. Therefore, a delay had occurred in laying the paper on 
the Table of both the House of Parliament during th e Budget Session from 7 
th  Jyly 2014 to 14 th  

August 2014. The said notification is now proposed to be laid on the Table of the both the Houses 
in the current Winter Session of Parliament.” 
 
 The Committee observes that it is for the Ministry  to plan that Subordinate 
Legislation is laid before the Parliament within th e prescribed schedule and accordingly, 
Ministry should ensure that they receive the printe d copies timely from the Government of 
India Press. The Ministry of Shipping should hencef orth take adequate precaution 
beforehand to lay the Notifications on the Table of the House in time. 
 
 3.   Committee impresses upon all the Ministries/De partments to take immediate steps to ensure 
timely and proper laying of subordinate legislation. The Committee, accordingly, wishes to bring to 
the notice of all Ministries/Departments of the Gov ernment of India, particularly, the defaulting 
ones, the following recommendations, as contained i n its 131 
st 
, 135 
th 
, 152 
nd  ,   192 nd  and 201 st  
Reports: 
 “Orders required to be laid before the House shoul d be laid (i) if the House is not in 
Session, during the Session immediately following t he date of publication of the Order in the 
Official Gazette and (ii) if the House is in Sessio n, on the date of the publication of the Order, 
during its continuance and in case the time lag bet ween the date of publication and the date 
of the closing of the Session is less than 15 clear  days, before the expiry of the Session 
immediately following the said Session. All the Min istries/Departments of Government of 
India should henceforth comply with this schedule i n the matter of laying of the Orders 
issued under various Acts of Parliament on the Table of the Rajya Sabha. 
(131 st  Report) 
(Presented on 15 December 2000) 
 
 “The Committee has, time and again, emphasized tha t it is essential that in case there is a 
delay in the laying of Statutory Orders, the concer ned Ministry/Department should 
invariably append a delay statement along with the Notifications being laid so as to apprise 
Parliament of the causes of delay. The Committee de sires all Ministries/Departments to take 
a note of this, since the intention is that through  the process of formulation of a delay 
statement, the Ministry is able to introspect, iden tify bottlenecks and devise remedial 
measures”. 
(135 th  Report) 
(Presented on 27 July 2001) 
 
 “In the opinion of the Committee, every notificati on should be assigned a distinctive 
number in order to give it a separate identity and similarly, no notification should be 
published/laid which does not carry a notification number. The Committee expects all 
Ministries/Departments of Government of India to ex ercise caution in this regard. In case 
where there are more than one Notifications under a  single file, the Ministries/Departments 
should ensure that the file number on each notifica tion should be suitably distinguished from 
one another.” 
(152 
nd 
 Report) 
(Presented on 26 August 2004)  
 
 “In addition to the concern expressed by the Commi ttee over delay in laying of 
Notifications on the Table of the House, the Commit tee also express their deep concern over 
delay in framing of rules/regulations under differe nt Acts. The Committee in its 47 
th  report 
presented to the House on 14.9.1981 has recommended  that the rule-making process should 

be completed within a period of six months of the c oming into force on an Act. The 
Committee has further recommended that in case a Ministry is not able to adhere to this time 
limit, it should seek extension of time for complet ing the rule-making process. The 
recommendation of the committee reads as follows:- 
 
  “The Committee feels that the rule-making process c ould well have been 
completed within the time limit of six months which  the Committee has laid down for 
making of rules under an Act after coming into forc e of that Act. Where however, a 
Ministry does not find it possible to adhere to the  time limit, they should inform the 
Committee of the reasons why they cannot make rules  within the time limit and seek 
extension of time for completing the rule-making process.” 
 The Committee is constrained to take note of the f act that the Ministries/Departments 
of Government of India are not complying with the C ommittee’s recommendation to 
complete the process of framing of subordinate legi slation contemplated under various Acts 
of Parliament within a period of six months. At the  same time, the Committee also does not 
receive requests for extension of time for completi ng the rule-making process in terms of its 
recommendations as above from most of the Ministrie s/Departments. The Committee takes a 
serious note of the prevailing situation in which t he Ministries/Departments are neither able 
to complete the task of framing rules/regulations u nder different Acts within the given six 
months’ period nor do they suo-motu  approach the Committee for seeking extension of ti me. 
The Committee further notes that in order to ensure  timely framing of rules/regulations it 
has taken an initiative to monitor the progress of framing of subordinate legislation in respect 
of all legislations brought about by different Mini stries/Departments of Government of India 
from the year 2003 onwards with a view to ensure th at the framing of subordinate legislation 
is not delayed. The Committee, however, finds that the responses from the 
Ministries/Departments have not been prompt in this  monitoring exercise undertaken on 
behalf of the Committee. 
  
 In view of the above position, the Committee once again reiterates its recommendation 
that the Ministries/Departments should ensure putti ng in place subordinate legislation 
positively within a period of six months of coming into force of the Act. The Committee 
further recommends that in case the Ministry fails to meet with this deadline, they should 
invariably approach the Committee for seeking exten sion of time. The Committee further 
recommends that in cases where the time limit of si x months is not adhered to, they should, 
while laying rules/regulations before the Parliament invariably lay a statement explaining the 
reasons why the framing of rules/regulations was delayed beyond six months so as to keep the 
Parliament apprised of the compliance of the Parlia ment’s mandate  conferred upon the 
Executive.” 
(192 
nd 
 Report) 
(Presented on 26 August 2011)  
 
 
  Rules/Regulations/Orders/bye-laws are laid by dif ferent Ministries on the Table of the 
House under various provisions of parent Acts passe d by Parliament. These Rules/ 
Regulations/Orders/bye-laws are published in the of ficial Gazette before being laid on the 
Table of the House. Even after they are laid, it is  very difficult to get access to these 
Notifications. The Committee recommends that such R ules/Regulations/Orders, etc. laid on 
the Table of the House should be invariably uploade d on the websites of respective Ministries 
immediately on the same day when they have been lai d on the Table of the House, for 
information of Members of Parliament and people at large for their easy access. 

201 st  Report 
(Presented on 14 th  December, 2012)  
 
 
The Committee observes that the whole process of en acting laws is defeated if rules 
are not framed and laid on the Table of the House i n time.  A reasonable delay could be 
understood but unjustifiably long delays should be avoided and the Ministries should work 
towards improving this position.   The Committee hopes that Ministry would strive to k eep 
the delay to the minimum and take care that Notific ations are laid on the Table of the House 
at the first available opportunity after publication of Notifications. 
  
 
The Committee would like to impress upon the Minist ry that it is their responsibility 
to ensure that copies of the Notifications are prin ted timely and for this purpose, they need to 
evolve a suitable mechanism to ensure that notifica tions are laid in time.   The Committee is 
happy that the Ministry has evolved an internal mechanism/ procedure for this purpose.  The 
Committee hopes that it would take action according ly in order to comply with the 
prescribed schedule in the matter of laying of statutory Notifications. 
 
 
The Ministry must take appropriate step to remove l acuna, if any, administrative or 
otherwise, causing such long delay by being little proactive and prompt.  Further, the 
Ministries should take it up with the Ministry of U rban Development for late receiving of 
printed copies of the Notification.

2.  While scrutinizing these Orders, the Committee noted that there was a considerable time lag 
between issue  of Notifications and their laying in  some cases. The annexed statement also 
indicates the period of delay in cases where Notifi cations have not been laid as per the time 
schedule prescribed by the Committee. The Committee  observed that out of the total 174 delayed 
Notifications, there were 84 Notifications where no delay statement was appended to. However, the 
bulk of delayed Notifications were from the Ministr y of  Road Transport and Highways which 
comes to around 48.2% of the total delayed Notifications. 
 
The observations/recommendations of the Committee i n respect of the specific 
Ministries/Departments where delay in laying of Notifications has been noticed, are as follows: -  
 
(i) Ministry of Civil Aviation  
  
 Ministry of Civil Aviation have laid one Notificat ion (Sl. No. 12) which is delayed by one 
year. There is no delay statement  appended thereto.  
 
 The Committee is anguished to note that Ministry o f Civil Aviation have delayed the 
laying of their only Notification by one year and t here is no delay statement attached thereto. 
There may be reason for delay in laying the Notific ation but there can’t be reason for not 
attaching a delay statement even after the lapse of  one year. The Committee therefore, 
observes  that the Ministry of Civil Aviation stric tly adheres to the time schedule as 
recommended by Committee  in its 131 
st  Report  in laying of the Subordinate Legislation 

before Parliament. Further, where there is delay in  laying of the notifications, a delay 
statement should also invariably be appended therew ith. The Committee recommends that 
the Ministry may clarify the reasons for delay in l aying and also why the delay statement has 
not been appended to the Notifications.  
  
 
(ii)  Ministry of Communications and Information Technology 
 (Department of Telecommunications) 
 
 Ministry of Communications and Information Technol ogy (Department of 
Telecommunications) have laid 2 Notifications (Sl. Nos. 15 – 16) and one of these (Sl. No. 16) has 
been delayed by 12 months. There is no delay statement appended to the Notification. 
  
The Committee regrets the delay in laying of one of  its Notification on the Table of the 
House. The Committee desires the Ministry of Commun ications and Information Technology 
(Department of Telecommunications)   to have communicated the circumstances causing 
delay in laying of Notification and also to have ap pended delay statement therefor. But 
Committee finds that the Ministry of Communications  and Information Technology 
(Department of Telecommunications)   have not only delayed the laying of one Notificati on 
but also did not append any delay statement thereto . The Committee, therefor, advises the 
Ministry of Communications and Information Technolo gy (Department of 
Telecommunications)   to strictly adhere to the time schedule in laying of the Notifications and 
append a delay statement where there is delay in la ying of Notification on the Table of the 
House. The Committee recommends that the Ministry m ay clarify the reasons for delay in 
laying and also why the delay statement has not been appended to the Notifications. 
 
(iii) Ministry of Environment, Forests and Climate Change 
 
Ministry of Environment, Forests and Climate Change  have laid 7 Notifications (Sl. Nos. 
19 to 25) on the Table of the House during the Sess ion. Two of them  (Sl. Nos. 20-21) have been 
delayed by 5 to 8 months and no delay statement is appended to both of these delayed 
Notifications. 
 
The Committee takes a strong view of the delay occu rred in tabling the Notifications 
in time and emphasise that the Ministry would avoid  such instances of delay in laying of 
Subordinate Legislation in future. The Committee al so impresses upon the Ministry to take 
note of the fact that in case, there is a delay in the laying of any Statutory Notifications, the 
same should be accompanied by a delay statement whi le it is being laid. The Ministry may 
clarify the reasons for delay in laying and also wh y the delay statement has not been 
appended to the Notifications. 
 
  
(iv) Ministry of Finance 
(a)    (Department of Economic Affairs) 
 
 Ministry of Finance (Department of Economic Affair s) have laid 20 Notifications (Sl. Nos. 
27 to 46).  Out of these 6 Notifications (Sl. Nos. 36 – 39, 44  & 46) have been  delayed by 4 
months to 9 months. There is no delay statement appended to any of these delayed Notifications.  
 

 The Committee are not happy with the delay in layin g of Notifications by the Ministry 
of Finance (Department of Economic Affairs), partic ularly Notifications at Sl. Nos. 36 and 44 
where delay period spans from  a period of  6 month s to 9 months. In the absence of any 
delay statement, the Committee would not know the r easons of delay, whatsoever,  and 
suggest remedial measures for rectifying it. The Committee, therefore, directs the Ministry of 
Finance (Department of Economic Affairs) to append delay statements where there is delay 
in laying of Notifications and avoid recurrence of such delays in future. The Ministry may 
clarify the reasons for delay in laying and also wh y the delay statement has not been 
appended to the Notifications.  
 
(b)    (Department of Financial Services) 
 
Ministry of Finance (Department of Financial Servic es) have laid 7 Notifications (Sl. Nos. 
47 to 53), of which 4 Notifications have been delay ed.  Out of 4 delayed Notifications,  3  
Notifications (Sl. Nos. 50 to 52) have  been delaye d each by 5 months with delay statement 
appended thereto. One Notification which has been d elayed  by 6 months, has no delay statement 
attached to it. The reasons forwarded by the Ministry for delay is as under:- 
 
“The Notification no. G.S.R. 686 (E), 687 (E) and 6 88 (E) dated 17.09.2014 pertaining to 
reorganization of jurisdiction of Debt Recovery Tri bunal (DRTs) under Debt Recovery Appellate 
Tribunal (DRATs) at Chennai, Kolkata and Mumbai was  published in the Gazette of India, vide 
No. 498 dated September 25, 2014. This Department h as received copy of the Gazette Notification 
from Government of India Press late on 16.02.2015 a nd hence, there was delay in submitting the 
papers in time. However, the inconvenience caused d ue to unintentional delay in submitting the 
papers is deeply regretted and may be condoned. Due  to promptness will be ensured in the future 
while submitting the papers in Parliament.” 
 
 The reasons cited by Ministry of Finance (Departmen t of Financial Services) that the 
Notifications could not be laid down because the copies of Notifications could not be provided 
by the Printing Press in time, seems to be true as the Ministry of Finance (Department of 
Financial Services) have stated that it was uninten tional. Further, they have requested to 
condone the lapse which they have regretted and hav e also assured promptness in laying of 
papers in Parliament in future. In view of the circ umstances delineated by the Ministry  of 
Finance (Department of Financial Services), the Com mittee feels satisfied with their reply 
and decides not to recommend  further and condone  it.  
 
(v) Ministry of Home Affairs 
  
Ministry of Home Affairs have laid 8 Notifications (Sl. Nos. 141 to 148). Out of  these,  one  
Notification (Sl. No. 147) has been delayed by 5 mo nths and  there is no delay statement appended 
to it. 
 
 The Committee are not able to know the reasons beh ind this delay in the absence of 
any delay statement. Therefore, the Committee invit es attention of the Ministry of Home 
Affairs to its recommendation as contained in its 1 35 
th  Report  in this connection, where it 
has been observed to append invariably delay statem ent(s) in case of delay in laying of 
Notifications by  the Ministry. 
 
(vi) Ministry of Law and Justice 

 
The only Notification that the Ministry of Law and Justice (Sl. No. 153) have laid is 
delayed by 12 months. There is no delay statement attached to it. 
 
The Committee expects the Ministry of Law and Justi ce to lay their papers on the 
Table of the House in time. Further, if there is de lay in laying, the Ministry of  Law and 
Justice is excepted, invariably, to append a delay statement. In the instant case there is a 
delay of over one year and Committee has not been a pprised of the reasons of delay. The 
Committee, therefore, recommend that appropriate st eps may be taken to prevent any such 
delay in future for laying of Notifications on the table of the  House by the Ministry of Law 
and Justice and in case of delay, a delay statement  should invariably be appended thereto. 
The Ministry may clarify the reasons for delay in laying and also why the delay statement has 
not been appended to the Notifications.  
 
(vii) Ministry of Personnel and Public Grievances a nd Pensions 
 (Department of Personnel and Training) 
  
Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensio ns (Department of Personnel and 
Training) have laid 14 Notifications (Sl. Nos. 154 to 167). Out of these 3 Notifications have been 
delayed by 7 to 9 months. There is no delay stateme nt appended to 2 Notifications (Sl. Nos. 155-
156). One Notification has a delay statement append ed (Sl. No. 157) to it. The reasons for delay 
given by the Ministry is as under:- 
 
“The Notification could not be laid on the Table of  the House within the specified time 
because of unintentional mistake and such a situati on will be avoided in future by being more 
vigilant, while dealing with such matters”. 
 
The Committee hopes that the Ministry would avoid s uch instances of delay in laying 
of subordinate legislation in future and would keep  off situations, intentional or 
unintentional, causing delay. The Committee have no ted the reply given by the Ministry and 
expects them to keep more vigil to avoid such unreasonable delays in future. 
 
(viii) Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas 
 
 Ministry of Petroleum and Natural have laid 2 Noti fications (Sl. Nos. 168 – 169) out of 
which one notification (Sl. No. 168) is delayed by 6 months and  no  delay statement  is attached  
thereto. 
 
The Committee reiterates its earlier recommendation , that in case of delay in laying, 
Notifications should be accompanied with delay stat ement. Attention to recommendation 
contained in 135 
th  Report of the Committee is drawn here. The Ministr y of Petroleum and 
Natural Gas should take care so that repetition of such delay is avoided in future.  
 
(ix) Ministry of Road Transport and Highways 
 
 The Ministry of Road Transport & Highways have lai d 196 Notifications
 on the Table of 
the House (Sl. Nos. 170 to 365). A total of 153 Not ifications have been delayed out of which 86 
Notifications are accompanied by delay statements a nd 67 Notifications have no delay statements 
appended with them. The delay period ranges from 4 months to 18 months. The reasons given by 

the Ministry is that it took some time to complete the procedural formalities and, therefore, papers 
could not be laid in time. 
 
 The Committee take note of the fact that Ministry of Road Transport and Highways 
have to lay  huge volume of Notifications on the table of the House.  The Committee, however, 
finds that percentage of delayed Notifications out of total Notifications laid is quite high i.e. as 
high as over 78%. This is simply unacceptable. Furt her, Ministry have not appended any 
delay statement with many delayed Notifications/Rul es. Ministry of Road Transport and 
Highways should see or look into the matter serious ly to eliminate recurrence of such delays 
in completing the procedural formalities. The Commi ttee desires that Ministry of Road 
Transport and Highways should adhere to the time sc hedule in laying of Notifications as 
prescribed in Committee’s 131 st  Report and append a delay statement in case there is  delay 
in laying. This has, sort of become a matter of rou tine with this Ministry, its seems. The 
Ministry may clarify the reasons for delay in layin g and also why the delay statement has not 
been appended to the Notifications. 
 
(x) Ministry of Rural Development 
 (Department of Land Resources) 
 
The Ministry of Rural Development (Department of La nd Resources) have laid only one 
Notification (Sl. No. 366) which was delayed by 6 m onths and moreover Ministry did not even 
bother to append a delay statement citing the reasons for such delay on their part. 
 
The Committee is not happy that the only Notificati on that Ministry of Rural 
Development (Department of Land Resources) have lai d, has been delayed by six months. 
Further, there is no reason given for this delay.  This is in contravention of Committee’s 
recommendation given in its 135 Report that Notific ation which are delayed should 
invariably be accompanied by a delay statement. The  Committee would like the Ministry of 
Rural Development (Department of Land Resources) to  take necessary steps to obviate such 
delays and, in case of delay in laying of Notificat ions, a delay statement should invariably be 
accompanied with them. 
 
 
 3.   Committee impresses upon all the Ministries/De partments to take immediate steps to ensure 
timely and proper laying of subordinate legislation. The Committee, accordingly, wishes to bring to 
the notice of all Ministries/Departments of the Gov ernment of India, particularly, the defaulting 
ones, the following recommendations, as contained i n its 131 
st 
, 135 
th 
, 152 
nd  ,   192 nd  and 201 st  
Reports: 
 
 “Orders required to be laid before the House shoul d be laid (i) if the House is not in 
Session, during the Session immediately following t he date of publication of the Order in the 
Official Gazette and (ii) if the House is in Sessio n, on the date of the publication of the Order, 
during its continuance and in case the time lag bet ween the date of publication and the date 
of the closing of the Session is less than 15 clear  days, before the expiry of the Session 
immediately following the said Session. All the Min istries/Departments of Government of 
India should henceforth comply with this schedule i n the matter of laying of the Orders 
issued under various Acts of Parliament on the Table of the Rajya Sabha. 
(131 st  Report) 
(Presented on 15 December 2000) 

 
 “The Committee has, time and again, emphasized tha t it is essential that in case there is a 
delay in the laying of Statutory Orders, the concer ned Ministry/Department should 
invariably append a delay statement along with the Notifications being laid so as to apprise 
Parliament of the causes of delay. The Committee de sires all Ministries/Departments to take 
a note of this, since the intention is that through  the process of formulation of a delay 
statement, the Ministry is able to introspect, iden tify bottlenecks and devise remedial 
measures”. 
(135 th  Report) 
(Presented on 27 July 2001) 
 
 “In the opinion of the Committee, every notificati on should be assigned a distinctive 
number in order to give it a separate identity and similarly, no notification should be 
published/laid which does not carry a notification number. The Committee expects all 
Ministries/Departments of Government of India to ex ercise caution in this regard. In case 
where there are more than one Notifications under a  single file, the Ministries/Departments 
should ensure that the file number on each notifica tion should be suitably distinguished from 
one another.” 
(152 
nd 
 Report) 
(Presented on 26 August 2004)  
 
 “In addition to the concern expressed by the Commi ttee over delay in laying of 
Notifications on the Table of the House, the Commit tee also express their deep concern over 
delay in framing of rules/regulations under differe nt Acts. The Committee in its 47 
th  report 
presented to the House on 14.9.1981 has recommended  that the rule-making process should 
be completed within a period of six months of the c oming into force on an Act. The 
Committee has further recommended that in case a Ministry is not able to adhere to this time 
limit, it should seek extension of time for complet ing the rule-making process. The 
recommendation of the committee reads as follows:- 
 
  “The Committee feels that the rule-making process c ould well have been 
completed within the time limit of six months which  the Committee has laid down for 
making of rules under an Act after coming into forc e of that Act. Where however, a 
Ministry does not find it possible to adhere to the  time limit, they should inform the 
Committee of the reasons why they cannot make rules  within the time limit and seek 
extension of time for completing the rule-making process.” 
 The Committee is constrained to take note of the f act that the Ministries/Departments 
of Government of India are not complying with the C ommittee’s recommendation to 
complete the process of framing of subordinate legi slation contemplated under various Acts 
of Parliament within a period of six months. At the  same time, the Committee also does not 
receive requests for extension of time for completi ng the rule-making process in terms of its 
recommendations as above from most of the Ministrie s/Departments. The Committee takes a 
serious note of the prevailing situation in which t he Ministries/Departments are neither able 
to complete the task of framing rules/regulations u nder different Acts within the given six 
months’ period nor do they suo-motu  approach the Committee for seeking extension of ti me. 
The Committee further notes that in order to ensure  timely framing of rules/regulations it 
has taken an initiative to monitor the progress of framing of subordinate legislation in respect 

of all legislations brought about by different Mini stries/Departments of Government of India 
from the year 2003 onwards with a view to ensure th at the framing of subordinate legislation 
is not delayed. The Committee, however, finds that the responses from the 
Ministries/Departments have not been prompt in this  monitoring exercise undertaken on 
behalf of the Committee. 
  
 In view of the above position, the Committee once again reiterates its recommendation 
that the Ministries/Departments should ensure putti ng in place subordinate legislation 
positively within a period of six months of coming into force of the Act. The Committee 
further recommends that in case the Ministry fails to meet with this deadline, they should 
invariably approach the Committee for seeking exten sion of time. The Committee further 
recommends that in cases where the time limit of si x months is not adhered to, they should, 
while laying rules/regulations before the Parliament invariably lay a statement explaining the 
reasons why the framing of rules/regulations was delayed beyond six months so as to keep the 
Parliament apprised of the compliance of the Parlia ment’s mandate  conferred upon the 
Executive.” 
(192 
nd 
 Report) 
(Presented on 26 August 2011)  
 
  Rules/Regulations/Orders/bye-laws are laid by dif ferent Ministries on the Table of the 
House under various provisions of parent Acts passe d by Parliament. These Rules/ 
Regulations/Orders/bye-laws are published in the of ficial Gazette before being laid on the 
Table of the House. Even after they are laid, it is  very difficult to get access to these 
Notifications. The Committee recommends that such R ules/Regulations/Orders, etc. laid on 
the Table of the House should be invariably uploade d on the websites of respective Ministries 
immediately on the same day when they have been lai d on the Table of the House, for 
information of Members of Parliament and people at large for their easy access. 
201 
st  Report 
(Presented on 14 th  December, 2012)  
 
 
The Committee observes that the whole process of en acting laws is defeated if rules 
are not framed and laid on the Table of the House i n time.  A reasonable delay could be 
understood but unjustifiably long delays should be avoided and the Ministries should work 
towards improving this position.   The Committee hopes that Ministry would strive to k eep 
the delay to the minimum and take care that Notific ations are laid on the Table of the House 
at the first available opportunity after publication of Notifications. 
  
 
The Committee would like to impress upon the Minist ry that it is their responsibility 
to ensure that copies of the Notifications are prin ted timely and for this purpose, they need to 
evolve a suitable mechanism to ensure that notifica tions are laid in time.   The Committee is 
happy that the Ministry has evolved an internal mechanism/ procedure for this purpose.  The 
Committee hopes that it would take action according ly in order to comply with the 
prescribed schedule in the matter of laying of statutory Notifications. 
 
 
 

The Ministry must take appropriate step to remove l acuna, if any, administrative or 
otherwise, causing such long delay by being little proactive and prompt.  Further, the 
Ministries should take it up with the Ministry of U rban Development for late receiving of 
printed copies of the Notification.
