Report 
On  
The Reverse Mortgage Scheme, 2008  
 
The Reverse Mortgage Scheme, 2008 ( Annexure I ) has been framed by the Central Board 
of Direct Taxes with an intent to monetize the hous e of a Senior Citizen  as an asset and the 
owners equity in the house. The Scheme involves the  senior citizen as borrower mortgaging the 
house property to a lender, who then makes periodic  payments to the borrower during the latter’s 
lifetime.  The Senior citizen borrower is not requi red to service the loan during his life time and, 
therefore, does not make monthly repayments of prin cipal and interest to the lender. On the 
borrower’s death or on the borrower leaving the hou se property permanently, the loan is repaid 
along with accumulated interest, through sale of the house property.  
2. The proportion of Senior Citizens as well as the ir dependency in the old age is increasing 
in the country. While on the one hand, there is sig nificant increase in longevity, on the other hand, 
cost of good health care facilities is also spirali ng and there is little social security. Senior citi zens, 
therefore, need regular cash flow for supplementing  their pension or other income scheme to 
address their financial needs.  
3. Keeping these issues in consideration and also t he fact that for most senior citizens, the 
house is the largest component of their wealth, the Committee took up for detailed examination the 
Reverse Mortgage Scheme, 2008. A questionnaire on t he Scheme was forwarded to the Ministry 
for their comments/ clarifications which have since  been received ( Annexure II ). The Committee 
also took up for discussion the said Scheme in its meetings held at Mumbai, Udhagamandalam and 
Bangalore on 24 
th  May,  2010; 28th  May, 2010; and, 30 th  May,  2010, respectively.  Study Notes on 
the said discussions are enclosed ( Annexure III, IV and V ). The Committee also had detailed 
discussion with the State Bank of Travancore at Kum aracom on 22 nd  June, 2011 and with IDBI 
Bank at Mumbai on 27 th  September, 2011.  Ministry of Finance (Department of Financial Studies) 
was also present on both the meetings.  Study Note on the said discussions are enclosed 
(Annexure VI and VII respectively).  The points raised by the Committee and the 
comments/clarifications of the Ministry are reproduced in the succeeding paragraphs. 
4. In response to the Committees query as to whethe r it was possible to amend the rules to 
specify the maximum charges that may be levied by a pproved lending institution for benefit of 
customers , it was informed that Primary lending institutions m ay levy One-time Upfront 
Processing charges which include origination, appra isal and inspection fees, property verification 
and title examination fees, legal charges, survey a nd property valuation charges and On going 
service charges. However, as per the operational gu idelines issued by National Housing Board 
(NHB) on the Reverse Mortgage Loan (RML), a detaile d schedule of all such costs should clearly 
be specified and provided to the prospective borrow ers.  The guidelines of the Bank on the new 
RML enabled Annuity have stipulated that the maximu m on-going service charges should not 
exceed 1.50 per cent per annum of the net loan outstanding. 
5. The Committee sought details as to how many Bank s were operating the scheme and what 
were the different steps taken by the Ministry and Banks to give wide publicity to this scheme. In 
response the Ministry informed that the reverse mor tgage scheme was being implemented by 23 
banks and two housing finance companies (HFCs). Til l March 31, 2010, an amount of Rs. 1413 
crore had been sanctioned to 7034 Senior Citizens, as per information furnished by the various 
Scheduled Commerical Banks and HFCs to NHB. Nationa l Housing Bank, the nodal organization 
for this scheme, has been continuing with its endea vour to promote the scheme. The Bank has 
launched programmes for counseling senior citizens in partnership with reputed non governmental 

organizations (NGOs) across the country. The main o bjective of such a programme is to generate 
greater awareness amongst senior citizen about the features, terms and conditions relating to 
reverse mortgage scheme and to enable the senior ci tizens to take informed decisions for availing 
the benefits under the scheme. So far seven reverse mortgage counseling centers have been opened 
by the Bank in partnership with NG0s. Further, NHB has also been involved in capacity building 
measures for strengthening the knowledge base about  the product and its features. NHB also 
organized a number of seminars and conferences in this regard. 
 6. On the issue of formulation of guidelines or mo del code by RBI/Ministry for 
implementation of the scheme for the Banks, the Min istry informed that pursuant to the 
announcement in the Union Budget for the year 2007- 08, National Housing Bank (NHB), being 
the nodal agency for the scheme, issued operational guidelines in May 2007 to facilitate Scheduled 
Commercial Banks (SCBs) and Housing Finance Compani es (HFCs) to extend Reverse Mortgage 
Loans (RML) to Senior Citizens in India in order to  enable them avail a periodic stream of cash 
flows against mortgage of his/her house. The guidel ines were notified by the Central Government 
vide its notification No. S.O. 2310 (E) dated 30th September, 2008 on Reverse Mortgage Scheme, 
2008.  
7. The announcement of the central Government in th e Union Budget 2008-09 enabled the 
addition of a new subsection (43) under Section 10 of the Income Tax Act to the effect that the 
stream of payments received by Senior Citizens unde r RML scheme made and notified by the 
Central Government would not be treated as "income.  Further, a new subsection (xvi) has been 
added to Section 47 of the Income Tax Act providing  that any transfer of a capital asset in a 
transaction of reverse mortgage shall not be regard ed as a transfer. A senior citizen borrower will 
be thus liable to tax on capital gains only at the point of alienation of the mortgaged property.  
8. The NHB conceptualized an extended RML scheme en suring assured life-time annuity 
payments to the senior citizens in December 2009. W ith a view to overcome limitations of the 
RML scheme launched in May 2007, the new scheme, termed as RML enabled Annuity scheme, is 
an extension over the initial RML scheme. The schem e envisages the bank / HFCs to source 
assured life time annuity for the senior citizens from a life insurance company. Further, the scheme 
provides an option for married couple-both husband and wife- to be joint borrowers for availing 
the periodic annuity payments throughout their life  time i.e. the payments shall continue to flow 
till the last surviving borrower is no more. NHB has also issued operational guidelines to the banks 
and HFCs for implementing the RML enabled Annuity scheme in December 2009.  
9. The Committee also sought details on the steps w hich have been taken to ensure that the 
borrower does not invest this money in speculative and other risk taking ventures thus putting his 
financial well being at stake as the loan amount ma y be disbursed in lump sum payment in one or 
more tranches. In response the Ministry informed th at as per the guidelines issued by NHB, the 
loan amount can be used for the purposes (i) Up gra dation, renovation, extension, improvement, 
maintenance and insurance of house; (ii) Medical pu rposes, meeting increased living expenses or 
any other consumption need; and (iii) The use of re verse mortgage loan payments for speculative, 
trading and business purposes shall not be permitted.  
10. As per the NHB guidelines issued in May 2007, t he maximum lump-sum payment shall be 
restricted to 50% of the total eligible amount of l oan subject to a cap of Rs.15 lakh or such other 
amount as may be notified by the Government of Indi a, to be used for medical treatment for self, 
spouse and dependants, if any. NHB further issued g uidelines in December 2009 (for the RML 
enabled Annuity scheme) wherein the maximum lump-su m payment has been reduced to 25% of 
eligible loan amount, in order to ensure greater pr oportion of monthly payments in the stream of 

fund inflows to senior citizens to meet increased l iving expenses and hence, their financial well 
being.  
11. In response to Committee’s query on the method devised to calculate the home loan 
eligibility of the applicants and revaluation of the property at periodic intervals to increase the loan 
eligibility of the applicants, the Ministry informe d that as per the operational guidelines of NHB, 
the amount of loan will depend on market value of r esidential property, as assessed by the primary 
lending institutions (PLIs), age of borrower(s), an d prevalent interest rate charged by the PLI. The 
PLIs will have the discretion to determine the elig ible quantum of loan. The methodology adopted 
for determining the quantum of loan including the d etailed tables of calculations, the rate of 
interest and assumptions (if any), shall be clearly  disclosed to the borrower. The Ministry further 
informed that the PLIs will need to re-value the pr operty mortgaged to them at intervals that may 
be fixed by the PLI depending upon the location of the property, its physical state etc. Such 
revaluation may be done at least once every five ye ars, the quantum of loan may undergo revision 
based on such re-valuation of property at the discretion of the lender.  
12. The PLIs shall ensure that all reverse mortgage  loan products carry a clear and transparent 
`no negative equity' or 'non-recourse' guarantee. That is, the Borrower(s) will never owe more than 
the net realizable value of their property, provide d the terms and conditions of the loan have been 
met. In the operational guidelines issued by NHB fo r RML enabled Annuity (December 2009), 
NHB has indicated stipulation of maximum Loan to Va lue (LTV) Ratio as hereunder, in addition 
to the above.  
J—Age of Borrower Maximum Loan to Value Ratio 
Between 60 and 70 60% 
Between 70 and 80 70% 
80 and above  75% 
 
13. The Committee also sought to be briefed on the major problems arising in giving effect to 
the Reverse Mortgage Scheme and the steps taken or proposed to be taken to remove these 
shortcomings. In response the Ministry informed tha t the senior citizens were mainly concerned 
about the Payment Tenure of 20 years only and Month ly payments not assured during entire 
lifetime of citizen. The Ministry to overcome these  shortcomings conceptualized an extended 
RML scheme ensuring assured life-time annuity payme nts to the senior citizens. This new scheme 
is an extension over the initial RML scheme of 2007 /2008. The new scheme will now facilitate the 
senior citizen borrowers to receive assured life-ti me payments i.e. even after completion of the 
fixed term of 20 years, in accordance with the anno uncement in Budget 2007-08. All payments 
under reverse mortgage loan are exempt from income tax under Section 10(43) of the Income tax 
Act, 1961. However, periodic annuity payments are s ubject to tax under provisions of Section 56 
of the Income Tax Act and taxable in the hands of t he annuity recipients. The Committee was 
informed that it was proposed that the RML, enabled  Annuity received by senior citizens may be 
exempted from taxation. The rationale for this prop osal is that the Annuity in this case emanates 
from the Reverse Mortgage Loan, essentially, the bo rrower finances such Annuity by way of the 
reverse mortgage loan.  
14. The Committee was further informed that the rev erse mortgage loan becomes due and 
payable to the primary lending institutions only on  death of the borrowers.  Therefore, while the 
primary lending institutions do not receive any int erest income till the loan becomes due ( which 
occurs only on the death of the borrowers), the sam e accrues in their books of accounts.  As such, 
primary lenders are taxed on the accrued income whi ch has actually not been received.   The 

Ministry proposed that the interest income on rever se mortgage loans to the primary lending 
institutions may be taxed only on actual receipt an d not on its accrual (but not received).  This will  
not only encourage the primary lending institutions  to implement the scheme widely, but also will 
facilitate in lowering the interest rates for the s cheme, thereby, resulting in better benefits to the  
senior citizens.   
15. The Committee sought the comments of the Minist ry on specific advantages that the 
reverse mortgage scheme intends to provide in compa rison with other social security schemes 
operational for elderly people. In response the Min istry informed that the reverse mortgages loan 
and reverse mortgage loan enabled annuity provide t he following advantages/benefits to senior 
citizens: 
a.  Release of the locked equity owned by senior ci tizens in their own houses, so that they can 
avail a stream of cash flows throughout their life time to meet their increased living 
expenses.  
b.  They continue to stay in their house and at the  same time can avail the cash inflows,  
c. They do not have to make any repayments to the P LIs throughout their life time as long as 
they continue to occupy the mortgaged house.  
d. In case the value of their house increases, they  may have option to increase their loan, based 
on the revaluation by the PLIs.  
e. It reduces the burden on the Government excheque r towards budgetary allocations for social 
security schemes (which the Government would have to provide otherwise).  
16. The Committee appreciates the effort of the Min istry to come up with the Reverse 
Mortgage Scheme as it provides a level of financial  support to the Senior Citizens. The 
Committee, however, observed that the Scheme did no t receive the response that was expected.  
Keeping in view the lackluster response of the Sche me, the Committee took note of the issues 
raised in its interactions with different organizat ions and the comments/ clarifications furnished by 
the Ministry. 
Observations and Recommendations  
17.  It was found out that some of the Banks had not sta rted implementing the Scheme. 
The Committee took an exception to this and was of the opinion that the Ministry should 
ensure that all the concerned financial institution s should implement the said Scheme as it is 
an important component for providing social securit y to the senior citizens of the country. 
The Committee would like to have the latest position in this regard. 
18. During the course of the discussions it was bro ught before the Committee that the 
cost of the registration charges as imposed by the State Governments tends to adversely 
affects the amount which the senior citizen receive s under the scheme. The Committee, 
keeping in view the social benefits associated with  the scheme, was of the opinion that the 
States could be urged to extend some concessions to  cases settled under this Scheme to make 
it more attractive and viable for old and needy per sons. Accordingly, the Committee 
recommends to Ministry to take this up with the Sta tes to persuade them to offer the 
required concessions to older people under the scheme . 
19.  Amongst the drawbacks associated with the Sche me was regarding the valuation of 
the property concerned. The Committee voiced its co ncern over the valuation procedure of 
the property and the scope of under-valuation leadi ng to loss to the owner of the asset. The 
Committee, therefore, recommends that the Ministry should ensure that valuation procedure 
is transparent and linked to the market rates of th e property concerned so that the owner 
gets a good price for his asset. This would help ge nerate confidence in the other potential 
clients of the Scheme. 

20.  The Committee also expresses its concern at th e indifferent attitude of the concerned 
officials in the implementation of schemes/policies  associated with elderly people. It felt that 
since this scheme was specially designed for senior  citizen, it would have been better if the 
officials with a proven track record of customer sa tisfaction were associated with its 
implementation. 
21. The Committee noticed that many of the senior c itizens or their relatives were not 
fully aware of this scheme. As a result, not many o f them were coming forward to take 
benefit of this socially useful scheme. Therefore, the Committee is of the opinion that more 
efforts were needed to give wider publicity to this  Scheme. It urges the Ministry ensure that 
the concerned institutions made suitable efforts to  generate awareness about this Scheme 
which may result in increased business for them. 
22. The Committee reiterates the Ministry’s proposa l that the Reverse Mortgage Loan 
enabled Annuity received by the senior citizen may be exempted from taxation as the 
Annuity in this case emanates from Reverse Mortgage  Loan and the borrower finances such 
Annuity by way of the reverse mortgage loan. The Co mmittee, therefore, recommends that 
necessary action may be taken in this regard on pri ority basis so as to reduce the taxation 
burden of senior citizen significantly. 
23. The Committee reiterates the Ministry’s proposa l that the interest income on reverse 
mortgage loans to the primary lending institutions may be taxed only on actual receipt and 
not on its accrual.  This will not only encourage t he primary lending institutions to 
implement the scheme widely, but also will facilita te in lowering the interest rates for the 
scheme, thereby, resulting in better benefits to th e senior citizens. Accordingly, Committee 
recommends to bring the required amendment in the r elevant law which would enable 
primary lending institutions to tax only on actual receipt thus making the scheme more 
popular by reducing the interest rate and producing greater benefits to senior citizen. 
24. The Committee is hopeful that the Ministry woul d carry out the recommendations of 
the Committee expeditiously under intimation to it.  The Committee is also of the opinion 
that proper monitoring and inspections are essentia l for the proper implementation of the 
Scheme and stresses upon the Ministry to ensure tha t the objectives of the Scheme are 
achieved.

2.  While scrutinizing these Orders, the Committee noted that there was a considerable time lag 
between issue  of Notifications and their laying in  some cases. The annexed statement also 
indicates the period of delay in cases where Notifi cations have not been laid as per the time 
schedule prescribed by the Committee. The Committee  observed that out of the total 216 delayed 
Notifications, there were 84 Notifications where no delay statement was appended to. However, the 
bulk of delayed Notifications were from the Ministr y of  Road Transport and Highways which 
comes to around 85.6% of the total delayed Notifications. 
 
The observations/recommendations of the Committee i n respect of the specific 
Ministries/Departments where delay in laying of Notifications has been noticed, are as follows: -  
 
(i) Ministry of Civil Aviation  
  

 Ministry of Civil Aviation has laid five Notificat ions (Sl. No. 9 to 13) during the Session. 
Out of these two Notifications (Sl. Nos. 9 – 10) ha ve been delayed by 16 and 14 months 
respectively and no delay statement is attached to both of these Notifications. 
 
 The Committee takes a strong view of such inordina te delay in laying of Notifications 
by the Ministry of Civil Aviation which in the inst ant case, has been  delayed by over more 
than one year. Further, there is no delay statement  attached to any of these Notifications. 
This is akin to defiance of Committee’s recommendat ion contained in its 135 
th  Report which 
requires concerned Ministries/Departments to invari ably append delay statement in case of 
delayed  Notifications being laid so as to apprise Parliament of the causes of delay. The 
Committee desires that the Ministry of Civil Aviati on should invariably append delay 
statement(s) in case of any delay actually taking p lace in laying of Notifications and avoid 
recurrence of such inordinate delay in future. 
 
  
 
(ii)  Ministry of Commerce and Industry 
 (Department of Commerce) 
 
 The Ministry of Commerce and Industry (Department of Commerce) have laid 3 
Notifications (Sl. Nos. 20 to 22) and out  of which  two (Sl. Nos. 20 and 21) were delayed by 12 
and 5 months respectively. One of the Notification had delay statement attached to it whereas the 
other did not have any delay statement with it. The  reasons for delay given by the Ministry are as 
under:-. 
  
 “Laying of Gazette Notification of amendment made in Agricultural and Processed Food 
Products Export Development Authority(APEDA) Act, 1985 vide S.O. 1038 (E), dated 04.04.1014 
regarding APEDA (Amendment) Rules published by the Ministry of Commerce and Industry was 
to be laid in both the Houses of Parliament. Howeve r, the notification could not be laid, within the 
stipulated time period, inadvertently. The Notifica tion S.O. No. 1038 (E), dated 04.04.2014 is 
being submitted before both the Houses of Parliament.” 
 
 The Committee directs that the Ministry must avoid  such instances of delay in laying 
of subordinate legislation in future and would keep  off situations, intentional or 

unintentional, causing delay. The Committee have no ted the reply given by the Ministry and 
expects them to keep more vigil to avoid such unreasonable delays in future.  
 
(iii) Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public  Distribution 
 (Department of Consumer Affairs) 
 
 Only one Notification that the Ministry of Consume r Affairs, Food and Public Distribution 
(Department of Consumer Affairs) (Sl. No. 32) have laid was delayed by 14 months and no delay 
statement has been appended therewith. 
 
 The Committee is not happy over the delay in layin g of the only  Notification by the 
Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distr ibution (Department of Consumer 
Affairs)   by  14 months. Further there is no delay statement  appended thereto giving reasons 
as to what caused such undue delay. The Committee, therefore, impresses upon the Ministry 
to take care that such instances of delay do not re cur in future and in case of any delay in 
laying, a delay statement should invariably be appended therewith. 
 
(iv) Ministry of Corporate Affairs 
 
 Ministry of Corporate Affairs have laid 17 Notific ations (Sl. Nos. 38 to 54), of which 3 
Notifications have been delayed.  Out of 3 delayed Notifications,  2  Notifications (Sl. Nos. 38 and 
40) have  been delayed each by 5 months and have no  delay statements attached to them. One 
Notification (Sl. No. 41) has been delayed  by 10 months although with a delay statement appended 
to it. The reason forwarded by the Ministry for delay is as under:- 
 
 “The notification relating to the G.S.R. No. 425(E)  dated 30.06.2014 on the Companies 
(Costs Records and Audit) Rules, 2014 is required to be laid before both the Houses of Parliament. 
 The notification relating to the G.S.R. No. 425(E)  dated 30.06.2014 on the Companies 
(Costs Records and Audit) Rules, 2014 was sent to G overnment Press for printing. Due to volume 
of pages, it took time (6 months) for printing in t he Government Press. The said notification could 
not be laid before both the Houses of Parliament du ring the Budget Session of Parliament, 2014 
due to delay in receiving the Gazette copy of said notification by this Ministry. The delay may be 
kindly be condoned.” 
 

 The Committee  expresses its deep concern about th e reply given by the Ministry of 
Corporate Affairs that the delay in laying of Notif ications was delayed due to volume of 
pages, which took time (6 months) for printing at t he Government Press.  The Ministry of 
Corporate Affairs  should, in future, ensure that a ll its papers are laid before the House as 
prescribed in the Committee’s 131 st  Report. The Ministry should frame a suitable mechanism 
to expedite the printing of papers so as to avoid undue delay. 
 
(v) Ministry of Finance 
 (Department of Economic Affairs) and (Department o f Financial Services) 
  
Ministry of Finance (Department of Economic Affairs ) have laid 14 Notifications (Sl. Nos. 
59 to 72) on the Table of the House during the Sess ion. Three of them  (Sl. Nos. 59 & 61-62) have 
been delayed by 6 to 7 months and no delay statemen t is appended to all of the delayed 
Notifications. 
Department of Financial Services have also laid 14 Notifications (Sl. Nos. 73 to 86). Out of 
these, one Notification (Sl. No. 73) has been delay ed by 5 months and there is no delay statement 
attached to it. 
 
The Committee, has time and again,  emphasised that  the Ministry should make all  
out effort for tabling of Notifications in time and  should avoid instances of delay in laying of 
Subordinate Legislation in future. The Committee al so impresses upon the Ministry to take 
note of the fact that in case, there is a delay in laying of any Statutory Notifications, the same 
should be accompanied by a delay statement while it  is being laid, as recommended in 
Committee’s 131 
st  and 135 th  reports respectively. The Ministry should clarify the reasons for 
delay in laying and also as to why the delay statem ent(s) has not been appended to the 
Notifications. 
 
  
  
(vi) Ministry of Health and Family Welfare 
 
 The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare  have la id 12 Notifications
 (Sl. Nos. 127 to 
138) out of which 7 Notifications have been delayed  (Sl. Nos. 127 and 130 to 135). Six 
Notifications  have been appended with delay statem ent and one Notification has no delay 

statement appended to it. The delay period ranges f rom 5 to 8 months. The Ministry has stated that  
the delay had been caused due to time taken in collection of required documents.  
  
 The Committee are unable to comprehend why the Min istry of Health and Family 
Welfare did not attach any delay statement to Notif ication at Sl. No. 127 while they have 
attached delay statement to other six delayed Notif ications. The Ministry have further, while 
explaining the reasons for delay, stated that delay  was caused due to time taken in collection 
of required documents. The Committee wonder whether  documents/papers to be laid were 
required to be procured from outside the Ministry. The Committee, therefore emphasises 
that the Ministry should strive henceforth to initi ate the process of laying and collection of 
documents as soon as Notifications are sent to Gove rnment of India press for laying and 
desist from  furnishing such excuses.  
 
  
(vii) Ministry of Human Resource Development 
 (Department of Higher Education and Department of School Education & Literacy) 
 
The Ministry of Human Resource Development (Departm ent of Higher Education) have 
laid 2 Notifications (Sl. Nos. 152 to 153). Both of  these  Notifications have been delayed. Delay 
period ranges from 19 months to 22 months and these  Notifications are accompanied with delay 
statement The reasons for delay given by the Minist ry is that due to paucity of time it could not be 
laid in the Parliament during the Winter Session. 
   
  Department of School Education and Literacy have la id 3 notifications (Sl. Nos. 154 – 
156). Out of these, 2 Notifications (Sl. Nos. 154 a nd 156) have been delayed by 5 months each and 
there is no delay statement appended thereto.  
  
 The Committee notes with serious concern that Mini stry of Human Resource 
Development (Department of Higher Education) have failed to lay the notifications in time on 
the Table of the House due to paucity of time. The laying of Notifications on the Table of the 
House is a statutory obligation which should be acc orded top priority. However, the Ministry 
has not shown intention of urgency to lay the paper  on the Table of Parliament causing 
inordinate delay. The Committee recommends that the  Ministry of Human Resource 
Development should strictly adhere to the schedule as recommended by the Committee in its 

131 st  Report for timely laying of Subordinate Legislatio n. The Committee hopes that the 
Ministry would avoid citing such unreasonable reasons for delay in future. 
  
(viii) Ministry of Power 
 
 Ministry of Power have laid 12 Notifications (Sl. Nos. 193 to 204). Two of these 
Notifications (Sl. Nos. 193 and 202) have been dela yed by 9 to 10 months with delay statements 
appended to them. The reason given for delay by the Ministry is as under:- 
 
 “The Notification No. JERC-1/2009, dated 15.05.201 4 issued by  the Joint Electricity 
Regulatory Commission for Goa and UTs is being laid  on the Table of Rajya Sabha as required 
under the provision of Section 182 of the Electrici ty Act, 2003 read with Section 2(64) of the 
Electricity Act, 2003. 
 Although the above Notification was published in t he Gazette of India Extraordinary dated 
17 
th  June, 2014, copies of the Notification could not b e laid on the Table of the Rajya Sabha before 
conclusion of the Monsoon Session and Winter Sessio n 2014 as printed copies of the same were 
received by Joint Electricity Regulatory Commission  for Goa & UTs from the Department of 
Publication only on 08 th  December, 2014. However, Joint Electricity Regulat ory Commission for 
Goa and UTs had forwarded the same to Ministry of P ower on 17 th  December, 2014. The 
Notification was on verge of conclusion. Hence the Notification are being laid on the first available 
opportunity.” 
 
 The Committee has taken note of the reasons causin g/delay in laying of papers on the 
Table of the House. In this respect the Committee a dvises that the Ministry of Power to take 
care so as to minimize such delays in future. 
 
(ix) Ministry of Railways 
 
Ministry of Railways  have laid 4 Notifications (Sl. Nos. 205 to 208). On e Notification (Sl. 
No. 205)  has been delayed by 5 months with a delay  statement appended thereto. The reasons of 
delay is given as under:- 
 
“Notification  G.S.R. 796(E) was got printed by Gov ernment of India Press, Mayapuri, 
Delhi – 64 on 13 
th  November, 2014 and as such the same could not have  been laid before the 

Parliament in the Winter Session of 2014-15. Howeve r, that could not be done so as printing error 
has crept in the said notification. When the matter  was taken up with the Press Office, it had 
advised for issuing of Corrigendum to this Notifica tion. Hence, the case continued to be under 
process for issuing of Corrigendum. By the time the  Corrigendum G.S.R. 13(E) dated 6 th  January, 
2015 was got printed and received in Railway Board’ s Office, last Winter Session of Parliament 
had already got over. Hence, some time got elapsed in between the last Parliament Winter Session 
and the current Session. The delay caused in puttin g up the case for laying the notifications in 
Parliament, therefore, is incidental, unavoidable and is regretted. 
Accordingly, G.S.R. 796(E) dated 13 th  November, 2014, alongwith its Corrigendum G.S.R. 
13(E) dated 6 th  January, 2015, is being laid on the Table of both the Houses of Parliament during 
the current Session.” 
 
The Committee has noted the reply given by the Mini stry of Railways regarding 
laying of Notification on the Table of the House an d, therefore,  cautions the Ministry of 
Railways  in future to ensure that all its papers a re laid before the House as prescribed in the 
Committee’s 131 
st  Report.  
 
 (x) Ministry of Road Transport and Highways 
 
The Ministry of Road Transport and Highways have la id highest number of Notifications 
during the Session which comes to a total of  436 N otifications (Sl. Nos. 209-642). Out of these, 
185 Notifications  have been delayed. The Ministry did not append any delay statement with 67 
delayed Notifications (Sl. Nos. 230 –232, 234, 236, 249, 257–258, 264, 267–268, 270 , 274, 276–
278, 280–302, 304–311, 314–339, 352, 361–364, 370–372, 374, 378, 381, 389, 392, 394–396, 398, 
404, 407–412, 414–415, 418–422, 424–427, 429–430, 4 34–438, 440–446, 448, 450–451, 453, 
455–459, 461–463, 465–471, 473–478, 480–483, 485–48 7, 489–495, 498, 500–503, 505–509, 
511,514, 519–520 & 523–530). However, 118 delayed Notifications were appended wi th delay 
statements. The delay period ranges from 4 months t o 20 months. The reason of delay given by the 
Ministry is that it took some time to collect the p apers and complete the procedural formalities 
therefore, papers could not be laid in time on the Table of  both Houses of Parliament.  
 
 The Committee takes note of the fact that Ministry  of Road Transport and Highways 
have laid a large number of Notifications on the table of the House in the said Session.  In this 
process, the procedural accuracy to the extent of h undred percent can’t be expected. The 

Committee, however, finds that percentage of delaye d Notifications is quite high i.e. as high 
as over 42.4%. This is simply unacceptable. Ministr y of Road Transport and Highways 
should look into the matter seriously to eliminate recurrence of such delays in future and 
strive to minimize such delays to the minimum exten t possible. The Committee desires that 
Ministry of Road Transport and Highways should adhe re to the time schedule in laying of 
Notifications as prescribed in Committee’s 131 st  Report and append a delay statement in case 
there is  a delay in laying.  
 
(xi) Ministry of Shipping 
  
 
The Ministry of Shipping have laid 8 Notifications (Sl. Nos. 643 to 650), out of which 4 
Notifications (Sl. Nos. 647 to 650) were delayed by  5 to 6 months. Not even a single Notification 
has been appended with a delay statement, whatsoever, explaining reasons therefore. 
 
The Committee, in the absence of delay statements, are not able to know the reasons 
behind the delay in laying of these Notifications. The Committee have clearly mentioned in its 
135 
th  Report that delay statements should invariably be appended where there is delay in 
laying of Notifications. The Committee, therefore, impress upon the Ministry to strictly 
adhere to the time schedule as prescribed in Commit tee’s Report that in case of any delay in 
laying, delay statement should invariably be append ed so that the valid reasons for such 
delay are brought to its notice. 
 
(xii) Ministry of Urban Development 
 
 Ministry of Urban Development have laid 2 Notifica tions
 (Sl. Nos. 655 to 656) out of 
which 1 Notification has been delayed (Sl. No. 655)  by 5 months and delay statement has been 
appended to it. The reason for delay given by the Ministry is as under:- 
 
 “The Notification regarding Addendum/Modification to Regulations for Regularization of 
Farm Houses in Delhi was published by the Delhi Development Authority (DDA) in the Gazette of 
India dated 26.11.2014. There is a delay of about 4  months in laying the Notification on the Table 
of both the Houses of the Parliament. The delay is due to the following reasons:- 
 

 DDA could not forward the notification to this Min istry in time due to oversight. 
 The notification was forwarded by Delhi Developmen t   Authority to Ministry of Urban 
Development (MoUD) on 23.03.2015 with delay statement. 
 DDA has provided the reasons for delay vide its le tter dated 07.04.2015. 
 The delay in placing the notification is regretted . 
 
 
  The Committee is pained to notice the fact that d elay was caused due to subordinate 
agency, Delhi Development Authority (DDA) which cou ld not send the Notification in time. 
The Committee advises that Ministry should impress upon their agencies to strictly adhere to 
the time schedule in laying of papers on the Table of the House. The Committee instructs the 
Ministry of Urban Development to note and  adhere t o the Committee’s recommendations 
contained in its 131 
st  Report so that such delays do not recur in future. 
 
 3.   Committee impresses upon all the Ministries/De partments to take immediate steps to ensure 
timely and proper laying of subordinate legislation. The Committee, accordingly, wishes to bring to 
the notice of all Ministries/Departments of the Gov ernment of India, particularly, the defaulting 
ones, the following recommendations, as contained i n its 131 
st 
, 135 
th 
, 152 
nd  ,   192 nd  and 201 st  
Reports: 
 
 “Orders required to be laid before the House shoul d be laid (i) if the House is not in 
Session, during the Session immediately following t he date of publication of the Order in the 
Official Gazette and (ii) if the House is in Sessio n, on the date of the publication of the Order, 
during its continuance and in case the time lag bet ween the date of publication and the date 
of the closing of the Session is less than 15 clear  days, before the expiry of the Session 
immediately following the said Session. All the Min istries/Departments of Government of 
India should henceforth comply with this schedule i n the matter of laying of the Orders 
issued under various Acts of Parliament on the Table of the Rajya Sabha. 
(131 st  Report) 
(Presented on 15 December 2000) 
 
 “The Committee has, time and again, emphasized tha t it is essential that in case there is a 
delay in the laying of Statutory Orders, the concer ned Ministry/Department should 

invariably append a delay statement along with the Notifications being laid so as to apprise 
Parliament of the causes of delay. The Committee de sires all Ministries/Departments to take 
a note of this, since the intention is that through  the process of formulation of a delay 
statement, the Ministry is able to introspect, iden tify bottlenecks and devise remedial 
measures”. 
(135 th  Report) 
(Presented on 27 July 2001) 
 
 “In the opinion of the Committee, every notificati on should be assigned a distinctive 
number in order to give it a separate identity and similarly, no notification should be 
published/laid which does not carry a notification number. The Committee expects all 
Ministries/Departments of Government of India to ex ercise caution in this regard. In case 
where there are more than one Notifications under a  single file, the Ministries/Departments 
should ensure that the file number on each notifica tion should be suitably distinguished from 
one another.” 
(152 
nd 
 Report) 
(Presented on 26 August 2004)  
 
 “In addition to the concern expressed by the Commi ttee over delay in laying of 
Notifications on the Table of the House, the Commit tee also express their deep concern over 
delay in framing of rules/regulations under differe nt Acts. The Committee in its 47 
th  report 
presented to the House on 14.9.1981 has recommended  that the rule-making process should 
be completed within a period of six months of the c oming into force on an Act. The 
Committee has further recommended that in case a Ministry is not able to adhere to this time 
limit, it should seek extension of time for complet ing the rule-making process. The 
recommendation of the committee reads as follows:- 
 
  “The Committee feels that the rule-making process c ould well have been 
completed within the time limit of six months which  the Committee has laid down for 
making of rules under an Act after coming into forc e of that Act. Where however, a 
Ministry does not find it possible to adhere to the  time limit, they should inform the 

Committee of the reasons why they cannot make rules  within the time limit and seek 
extension of time for completing the rule-making process.” 
  
 The Committee is constrained to take note of the f act that the Ministries/Departments 
of Government of India are not complying with the C ommittee’s recommendation to 
complete the process of framing of subordinate legi slation contemplated under various Acts 
of Parliament within a period of six months. At the  same time, the Committee also does not 
receive requests for extension of time for completi ng the rule-making process in terms of its 
recommendations as above from most of the Ministrie s/Departments. The Committee takes a 
serious note of the prevailing situation in which t he Ministries/Departments are neither able 
to complete the task of framing rules/regulations u nder different Acts within the given six 
months’ period nor do they suo-motu  approach the Committee for seeking extension of ti me. 
The Committee further notes that in order to ensure  timely framing of rules/regulations it 
has taken an initiative to monitor the progress of framing of subordinate legislation in respect 
of all legislations brought about by different Mini stries/Departments of Government of India 
from the year 2003 onwards with a view to ensure th at the framing of subordinate legislation 
is not delayed. The Committee, however, finds that the responses from the 
Ministries/Departments have not been prompt in this  monitoring exercise undertaken on 
behalf of the Committee. 
  
 In view of the above position, the Committee once again reiterates its recommendation 
that the Ministries/Departments should ensure putti ng in place subordinate legislation 
positively within a period of six months of coming into force of the Act. The Committee 
further recommends that in case the Ministry fails to meet with this deadline, they should 
invariably approach the Committee for seeking exten sion of time. The Committee further 
recommends that in cases where the time limit of si x months is not adhered to, they should, 
while laying rules/regulations before the Parliament invariably lay a statement explaining the 
reasons why the framing of rules/regulations was delayed beyond six months so as to keep the 
Parliament apprised of the compliance of the Parlia ment’s mandate  conferred upon the 
Executive.” 
(192 
nd 
 Report) 
(Presented on 26 August 2011)  
 

  Rules/Regulations/Orders/bye-laws are laid by dif ferent Ministries on the Table of the 
House under various provisions of parent Acts passe d by Parliament. These Rules/ 
Regulations/Orders/bye-laws are published in the of ficial Gazette before being laid on the 
Table of the House. Even after they are laid, it is  very difficult to get access to these 
Notifications. The Committee recommends that such R ules/Regulations/Orders, etc. laid on 
the Table of the House should be invariably uploade d on the websites of respective Ministries 
immediately on the same day when they have been lai d on the Table of the House, for 
information of Members of Parliament and people at large for their easy access. 
201 st  Report 
(Presented on 14 th  December, 2012)  
 
The Committee observes that the whole process of en acting laws is defeated if rules 
are not framed and laid on the Table of the House i n time.  A reasonable delay could be 
understood but unjustifiably long delays should be avoided and the Ministries should work 
towards improving this position.   The Committee hopes that Ministry would strive to k eep 
the delay to the minimum and take care that Notific ations are laid on the Table of the House 
at the first available opportunity after publication of Notifications. 
  
 
The Committee would like to impress upon the Minist ry that it is their responsibility 
to ensure that copies of the Notifications are prin ted timely and for this purpose, they need to 
evolve a suitable mechanism to ensure that notifica tions are laid in time.   The Committee is 
happy that the Ministry has evolved an internal mechanism/ procedure for this purpose.  The 
Committee hopes that it would take action according ly in order to comply with the 
prescribed schedule in the matter of laying of statutory Notifications. 
 
 
The Ministry must take appropriate step to remove l acuna, if any, administrative or 
otherwise, causing such long delay by being little proactive and prompt.  Further, the 
Ministries should take it up with the Ministry of U rban Development for late receiving of 
printed copies of the Notification. 
212 
th   Report 
(Presented on  3 rd  September, 2013)

comes to around 74.5% of the total delayed Notifications. 
 
The observations/recommendations of the Committee i n respect of the specific 
Ministries/Departments where delay in laying of Notifications has been noticed, are as follows: -  
 
(i) Ministry of Commerce and Industry 
 (Department of Commerce; & Department of Industrial Policy and  Promotion) 
  
The Ministry of Commerce and Industry (Department o f Commerce) have laid 9 
Notifications (Sl. Nos. 11-19) out of which 2 Notif ications have been delayed by 4 months each. 
These Notifications (Sl. Nos. 
14-15) have no delay statement attached.  
Department of Industrial Policy and Promotion have laid 3 Notifications (Sl. Nos. 20  –  
22). Out of these 2 Notifications (Sl. Nos. 21 – 22 ) have been delayed. The delay period ranges 
from 4 months to 8 months and there is  no delay st atement  appended to both of the delayed 
Notifications. 
 

 The Committee find that Ministry of Commerce and I ndustry (Department of 
Commerce & Department of Industrial Policy and Prom otion) have not only delayed the 
laying of Notifications but also failed to appended  delay statement to that. The Committee, in 
the absence of delay statements, are not able to kn ow the reasons behind this delay in laying 
of Notifications. The Committee have clearly mentio ned in its 131 st  Report that delay 
statements should invariably be appended where ther e is delay in laying of Notifications. The 
Committee, therefore, impress upon the Ministry of Commerce and Industry to strictly 
adhere to the time schedule as prescribed in Committee’s Report and in case of any delay in a 
laying, delay statement should invariably be appended thereto. 
 
(ii)  Ministry of Communications and Information Technology 
 (Department of Telecommunications) 
 
Only one  Notification that the Ministry of Communi cations and Information Technology 
(Department of Telecommunications) (Sl. No. 24) hav e laid is delayed by 5 months and there is no 
delay statement appended thereto. 
     
 The Committee are not happy over the delay of 5 mon ths on the part of the Ministry. 
Further there is no reason given as to what caused this delay. The Committee therefore, 
impress upon the Ministry to  take care so that suc h instances of delay do not recur in future 
and in case of any delay in laying,  a delay statement should invariably be appended. 
 
(iii) Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public  Distribution 
 (Department of Food and Public Distribution)  
 
 Ministry of Consumer Affairs  (Department of Food and Public Distribution) have laid 3 
Notifications (Sl. Nos. 28 to 30). Only 1 Notificat ion (Sl. No. 29) has been delayed by 4 Months 
and there is no delay statement appended to it.  
  
   The Committee notes that there has been delay in la ying of one Notification and no 
delay statement has been attached to it. The Commit tee reiterates its recommendation 
contained in its 135 
th  Report that in case of delay in laying of Notifica tions etc., invariably a 
delay statement should be attached. The Ministry should ensure such compliance in future.  
 

 
(iv) Ministry of Environment, Forests and Climate C hange 
 
Ministry of Environment, Forests and Climate Change  have laid 8 Notifications (Sl. Nos. 
44 to 51) on the Table of the House during the Sess ion. Three of  them  (Sl. Nos. 44, 47 - 48) have 
been delayed by 4 to 8 months. One Notification (Sl . No. 47) has delay statement appended to it 
whereas no delay statement  was appended with other  two notifications (Sl. Nos. 44 & 48). The 
reason forwarded by the Ministry for delay is as under:- 
 
“Laying of Gazette Notification No. S.O. 3111 (E) d ated 10 
th  December, 2014 bringing in 
an amendment to Rule 3 of the National Board for Wi ldlife Rules, regarding enabling continuity of 
the tenure of the members nominated in accordance to Rule 3(4) of the National Board for Wildlife 
Rules, 2003, till such time the nomination of the n ew members comes into effect, on the Table of 
both Houses of Parliament. 
The notifications could not be laid in the Budget S ession of Parliament 2015, as it was the 
first full Budget Session of the new Government and  several issues of the Ministry were being 
considered during the Session. Besides, the Ministr y was also actively involved in the process of 
withdrawal of the Wild Life (Protection) Bill, 2013  and matter regarding laying of this notification 
was inadvertently missed.” 
 
The Committee notes the reason given by the Ministr y of Environment, Forests and 
Climate Change that caused delay in laying of the N otifications. The Committee, however, 
emphasises that tabling of Gazette Notification is of utmost public importance and it is prime 
responsibility of the Ministry to discharge its duty to Parliament and to the public. 
 The Committee, therefore,  impresses upon the Mini stry to adhere to the time 
schedule and in case, there is a delay in the layin g of any Statutory Notification, the same 
should be accompanied by a delay statement while it  is being laid. The Ministry should 
clarify the reasons for delay in laying and also wh y the delay statement has not been 
appended to the Notifications. 
  
(v) Ministry of Finance 
(a)    (Department of Economic Affairs) 
 

Ministry of Finance (Department of Economic Affairs ) have laid 18 Notifications (Sl. Nos. 
53 to 70) out of which 7 Notifications (Sl. Nos. 53   – 55, 66 & 68  – 70)  have been delayed by 4 to 
11 months. Moreover, there is  no delay statement  appended to any of these notifications so 
delayed.  
 
The Committee takes a serious view not only of the delay in laying of seven 
Notifications (by the Department of Economic Affair s) on the Table of the House but also for 
its failure to append the required delay statement.  The Ministry/Department must know 
about the possible implications of failing to meet this requirement that tantamounts to 
diluting Executive’s accountability to Parliament. It must ensure to append a delay statement 
in all such cases in future. 
 
(b)    (Department of Financial Services) 
 
Ministry of Finance (Department of Financial Services) have laid 33 Notifications (Sl. Nos. 
71 to 103), of which 13 Notifications have been del ayed.  Out of these 13 delayed Notifications,  2  
Notifications (Sl. Nos. 98 to 99) have  been delaye d each by 4 months with delay statement 
appended thereto. Whereas in the 11 Notifications w hich have been delayed  by 4 to 7 months, 
there is  no delay statement attached. The reasons forwarded by the Ministry for delay is as under:- 
 
“At the time of publication of Notifications Nos. 2 69 (E) and G.S.R. 274 (E) of the 
insurance Regulatory and Development Authority (Sal ary and Allowance payable to and other 
Terms Conditions of Service of Chairperson and othe r Members) Rules, 2000, in the official 
Gazette of India, the Parliament was not in session. In the subsequent sessions of the Parliament the 
Notifications were inadvertently not laid on the Table of the Houses due to an oversight.” 
 
 The Committee cannot accept the reply given by the Ministry of Finance (Department 
of Financial Services)  that the Notifications could not be laid on time due to oversight. It only 
reflects the lack of seriousness on the part of the  Ministry in fulfilling its constitutional 
responsibility to Parliament. The Committee expects  the Ministry to be more careful about 
laying of its papers and see that persons responsible for this are held accountable. 
 
 (c)  (Department of Revenue) 
 

 Ministry of Finance (Department of Revenue) have la id 86 Notifications (Sl. Nos. 104 to 
189) on the Table of the House. Out of these 10 Not ifications have been delayed by 4 to 5 months 
respectively and no delay statement have been attached to any of these Notifications. 
 
 The Committee opines that had the Department of rev enue exercised a bit caution, 
they would have avoided such instances of delay as delay period is not exceptionally long. 
Further, delay statement is also not appended. The Committee, therefore,  impresses upon 
the Ministry to avoid such instances of delay and i n case there is a delay in the laying of any 
Statutory Notifications, the same should be accompa nied by a delay statement while it is  
being laid. The Departments’ attention is drawn tow ards recommendations in this regard as 
contained in 135 
th  Report of the Committee. 
 
(vi) Ministry of Health and Family Welfare; and  (D epartment of Health and Health & 
Family Welfare) 
 
 Ministry of Health & Family Welfare have laid 2 Not ifications (Sl. Nos. 190-191) out of 
which one Notification is delayed by 6 months and has delay statement appended to it. 
 Department of Health & Family Welfare have laid 3 Notifications (Sl. Nos. 192-194). All 
of these have been delayed from 5 to 11 months and there is no delay statement to any of these 
delayed Notifications.  The reason for delay given by the Ministry in respect of Notification at Sl. 
No. 191 is as under:- 
 
 “The Ministry of Health & Family Welfare has amend  Rule 18A (4) (ii) of the Pre-
conception and Pre-natal Diagnostic Techniques (Pro hibition of Sex Selection) Rules, 1996 vide 
the Notification G.S.R. 60 (E) dated 28 
th  January, 2015. As per the amended Rules, the Appropriate 
Authority shall ensure that no application for fres h registration or renewal of registration is 
accepted if any case is pending in any court agains t the applicant for violation of any provision of 
the Act and the rules made thereunder. 
2. As per Section 34 of the Pre-conception and Pre- natal Diagnostic Techniques Act, every 
rule made under this Act shall be laid, as soon as after it is made, before each House of the 
Parliament, while it is in session, for a total period of thirty days which may be comprised in one or 
two or more successive sessions. 
3. The aforesaid Notification, due to inadvertent r easons, could not be laid on the Table of 
both Houses of Parliament in the Budget Session of Parliament this year. The delay is regretted. 

4. Now, the Notification G.S.R. 60(E) dated 28.01.2 015 is proposed to be laid on the Table of 
both Houses of Parliament in the Monsoon Session of Parliament.” 
 
 The Committee can’t accept the reason that the Noti fication could not be laid on the 
Table of the House due to inadvertence. This is sheer negligence on the part of the Ministry in 
regard to Parliamentary matters. The Committee  cautious the Ministry to be more careful in 
future and not to have a casual approach while dealing with matters of public importance. 
 
(vii) Ministry of Home Affairs 
  
Ministry of Home Affairs have laid 24 Notifications  (Sl. Nos. 195 to 218). Out of  these,  4  
Notifications  have been delayed. Whereas 2 Notific ations (Sl. Nos. 201-202) have been delayed 
from a long period of 8 years and 1 month to 8 year s and 2 months and are accompanied with a 
delay statement. Other 2 Notifications (Sl. Nos. 20 8-209) have delayed by 4 months each and there 
is no delay statement appended to it. The reasons of delay given by the Ministry is as under:- 
 
“The Notification No.3/4/02/RO (1-2)/234 dated 13 
th  June, 2007 (English version) in 
respect of ‘Chandigarh Administration Protection of  Interest of Depositors (in Financial 
Establishments) Rules, 2007’ was published by UT Ad ministration of Chandigarh under Section 
18(1) of ‘The Bihar Protection of interests of Depo sitors (in Financial Establishments) Rules, 
2002’, as extended to UT of Chandigarh. The Hindi v ersion of the Notification was not however 
published inadvertently by Chandigarh Administratio n in their Gazette. Hence the notification 
could not be laid on the Table of the House. 
 
The Hindi version of Notification ]No.3/4/02/RO (1- 2)/417] has now been published on 3 
rd  
June, 2015 in the Gazette of Chandigarh Administrat ion. Hence, Notification is being laid on the 
Table of Lok Sabha/Rajya Sabha under Section 18(2) of ‘The Bihar Protection of Interests of 
Depositors (in Financial Establishments) Rules, 2002’, as extended to UT of Chandigarh.” 
 
 The Committee wonders that it has taken as long as  eight years in publishing of the 
Hindi version of a Notification. This is simply rid iculous and the Committee takes a serious 
note of this. The Ministry should find suitable mec hanism to eliminate such instances of 
delay. Just to have Hindi version publish should no t have taken file 8 years. This shows the 
lackadaisical attitude and approach of the Ministry. 

 
(viii) Ministry of Human Resource Development 
  (Department of Higher Education) 
 
 The Ministry of Human Resource Development (Depart ment of Higher Education) have 
laid 2 Notifications (Sl. Nos. 224 - 225). Out of t hese 1 Notification (Sl. No. 224) has been delayed 
by 4 months with delay statement appended to it. Th e reason for delay given by the Ministry is as 
under:- 
 
 “As per  the recommendations of the Committee on P apers Laid on the Table of Lok 
Sabha/Rajya Sabha, the Rules are required to be lai d on the Tables of the Lok Sabha/Rajya Sabha 
with a period of 15 days after their publication in  the Gazette, if the House is in session and if the  
House is not in Session the orders should be laid on the Table of the House as soon as possible (but 
in any case within 15 days) after the commencement of the following session. 
 However, due to lacunae leading to corrigendum, th e said rules could not be laid in the 
following sessions of Parliament. The said rules al ongwith the corrigendum notified vide G.S.R. 
244 (E) incorporating the omissions/infirmities poi nted out by the Committee on Subordinate 
Legislation will therefore be laid in the Monsoon Session, 2015 of the Parliament.” 
 
 The Committee find that delay was caused due to lac unal  in the Notification leading 
to corrigendum. The Committee observes that Ministr y have been following the practice of 
laying Notification on the first available opportun ity and laying corrigendum as and when 
published. However, in the instant case, the minist ry has waited for four months for 
publication of corrigendum and thereafter they have  laid both Notifications and 
Corrigendum simultaneously. The Committee recommend s that Ministry should lay the 
Notification at the first opportunity available and  thereafter lay the corrigendum as and 
when it has been published and not to wait for both of them to be laid together. 
 
(ix) Ministry of Information and Broadcasting 
 
 Ministry of Information and Broadcasting  have lai d 3 Notifications (Sl. Nos. 226 to 229). 
Only one of them (Sl. No. 228) has been delayed by 4 months and is accompanied with delay 
statement. The reason given by the Ministry for delay is as under:- 
 

 “In exercise of the power conferred by sub-section  (2) of section 22 of the Cable Television 
Networks (Regulation) Act, 1995 (7 of 1995), the Ce ntral Government had made Cable Television 
Networks (Amendment) Rules, 2015 to amend the Cable  Television Networks Rules, 1994 which 
were notified in the Gazette of India (Extraordinar y) on 23.03.2015. The Cable Television 
Networks (Amendment) Rules, 2015 could not be laid in the Budget Session 2015 immediately 
since the Session was already underway and the requ isite approvals for laying the papers could not 
be proposed.” 
 
  The Committee take serious note of the fact that delay was caused due to non-
completion of procedural formalities. The Committee  advises the Ministry of Information 
and Broadcasting to take care in future so that suc h delays do not recur and there are as 
lapses on its part vis-à-vis  procedural aspects. 
 
(x)  Ministry of Power  
 
Ministry Power have laid 7 Notifications (Sl. Nos. 252 to 258). Out of these, 2 Notifications 
(Sl. Nos. 256 – 257) have been delayed by 4 months each. Both of them have been appended with 
delay statement. The reasons given by the Ministry for the said delay is as under:- 
 
“The Notifications No. JERC-1/2009 and JERC-4/2009 issued by the Joint Electricity 
Regulatory Commission for Goa and UTs is being laid  on the Table of Rajya Sabha as required 
under the provisions of Section 182 of the Electric ity Act, 2003 read with section 2(64) of the 
Electricity Act, 2003. 
Although the said Notifications were published in t he Gazette of India Extraordinary dated 
9
th  March, 2015 copies of the Notifications could not be laid on the Table of the Rajya Sabha 
before conclusion of the Budget Session as printed copies of the same were received by Joint 
Electricity Regulatory Commission for Goa and UTs f rom the Department of Publication only on 
25 th  May, 2015. However, Joint Electricity Regulatory Commission of Goa and UTs had forwarded 
the same to Ministry of Power on 1 st  June, 2015. Hence the Notifications are being laid  on the first 
available opportunity.” 
 
The Committee does not accept the late receipt of p rinted copies of Notifications as a 
valid reason for  delayed laying of Notifications e tc. The Committee does not accept this as a 
convincing reason in respect of laying of statutory  papers before the Parliament. The 

Ministry of Power  should, therefore,  in future en sure that all its papers are laid before the 
House within the time frame as prescribed in the Co mmittee’s 131 st  Report wherein this 
aspect has been dealt with at great length. The Ministry should take it up with the Ministry of 
Urban Development for late receiving of printed copies of the Notifications. 
 
 
(xi) Ministry of Road Transport and Highways 
 
 The Ministry of Road Transport & Highways have lai d 249 Notifications
 on the Table of 
the House (Sl. Nos. 260 to 509). A total of 149 Not ifications have been delayed out of which 75 
Notifications (Sl. Nos. 260–271, 273 – 276, 279, 281–289, 305–306, 312, 320, 333, 345–352, 355–
368, 373, 376, 379–381, 384–386, 389–391, 393–394, 400–403 & 401–415)  are accompanied by 
delay statements and 74 Notifications (Sl. Nos. 277  –278, 280, 307–310, 313–319, 321–327, 329–
332, 334–344, 347, 353–354, 369–372, 374–375, 377–3 78, 382–383, 387–388, 392, 395–399, 
404–409, 416–423, 500–501 & 503)  have no delay statements appended with them. The de lay 
period ranges from 4 months to 18 months. The reaso ns given by the Ministry is that it took some 
time to complete the procedural formalities and, therefore, papers could not be laid in time. 
 
The Committee is not happy over such large number o f delayed Notifications. This is 
just not acceptable to the Committee that 74 out of  149 Notifications delayed did not have the 
delay statements, delay period being more than one year five months in the case of some 
Notifications. While there may be a reasons for the  delay, but there cannot be any reason for 
not furnishing reason for that. The Ministry must u nderstand the implications for not doing 
so regularly moreso, in such a large number of cases. 
 
The Committee does not accept the reasons of the delay given by the  Ministry of Road 
Transport and Highways that it took some time to co llect the papers and complete the 
procedural formalities. The Committee wonders how c an it take such a long time to receive 
Notifications and to complete procedural formalitie s. The Committee feels that Ministry did 
not take adequate precaution to avoid the delay. Th e Committee further makes a point that 
Ministry should append a delay statement in each su ch cases so as to apprise the Parliament 
of the reasons of delay in laying of Notifications on the Table of the House. 
 

 3.   Committee impresses upon all the Ministries/De partments to take immediate steps to ensure 
timely and proper laying of subordinate legislation. The Committee, accordingly, wishes to bring to 
the notice of all Ministries/Departments of the Gov ernment of India, particularly, the defaulting 
ones, the following recommendations, as contained i n its 131 
st 
, 135 
th 
, 152 
nd  ,   192 nd  , 201 st  and 
212 th  Reports: 
 
 “Orders required to be laid before the House shoul d be laid (i) if the House is not in 
Session, during the Session immediately following t he date of publication of the Order in the 
Official Gazette and (ii) if the House is in Sessio n, on the date of the publication of the Order, 
during its continuance and in case the time lag bet ween the date of publication and the date 
of the closing of the Session is less than 15 clear  days, before the expiry of the Session 
immediately following the said Session. All the Min istries/Departments of Government of 
India should henceforth comply with this schedule i n the matter of laying of the Orders 
issued under various Acts of Parliament on the Table of the Rajya Sabha. 
(131 st  Report) 
(Presented on 15 December 2000) 
 
 “The Committee has, time and again, emphasized tha t it is essential that in case there is a 
delay in the laying of Statutory Orders, the concer ned Ministry/Department should 
invariably append a delay statement along with the Notifications being laid so as to apprise 
Parliament of the causes of delay. The Committee de sires all Ministries/Departments to take 
a note of this, since the intention is that through  the process of formulation of a delay 
statement, the Ministry is able to introspect, iden tify bottlenecks and devise remedial 
measures”. 
(135 th  Report) 
(Presented on 27 July 2001) 
 
 “In the opinion of the Committee, every notificati on should be assigned a distinctive 
number in order to give it a separate identity and similarly, no notification should be 
published/laid which does not carry a notification number. The Committee expects all 
Ministries/Departments of Government of India to ex ercise caution in this regard. In case 
where there are more than one Notifications under a  single file, the Ministries/Departments 

should ensure that the file number on each notifica tion should be suitably distinguished from 
one another.” 
(152 
nd 
 Report) 
(Presented on 26 August 2004)  
 
 “In addition to the concern expressed by the Commi ttee over delay in laying of 
Notifications on the Table of the House, the Commit tee also express their deep concern over 
delay in framing of rules/regulations under differe nt Acts. The Committee in its 47
th  report 
presented to the House on 14.9.1981 has recommended  that the rule-making process should 
be completed within a period of six months of the c oming into force on an Act. The 
Committee has further recommended that in case a Ministry is not able to adhere to this time 
limit, it should seek extension of time for complet ing the rule-making process. The 
recommendation of the committee reads as follows:- 
 
  “The Committee feels that the rule-making process c ould well have been 
completed within the time limit of six months which  the Committee has laid down for 
making of rules under an Act after coming into forc e of that Act. Where however, a 
Ministry does not find it possible to adhere to the  time limit, they should inform the 
Committee of the reasons why they cannot make rules  within the time limit and seek 
extension of time for completing the rule-making process.” 
 The Committee is constrained to take note of the f act that the Ministries/Departments 
of Government of India are not complying with the C ommittee’s recommendation to 
complete the process of framing of subordinate legi slation contemplated under various Acts 
of Parliament within a period of six months. At the  same time, the Committee also does not 
receive requests for extension of time for completi ng the rule-making process in terms of its 
recommendations as above from most of the Ministrie s/Departments. The Committee takes a 
serious note of the prevailing situation in which t he Ministries/Departments are neither able 
to complete the task of framing rules/regulations u nder different Acts within the given six 
months’ period nor do they suo-motu  approach the Committee for seeking extension of ti me. 
The Committee further notes that in order to ensure  timely framing of rules/regulations it 
has taken an initiative to monitor the progress of framing of subordinate legislation in respect 
of all legislations brought about by different Mini stries/Departments of Government of India 

from the year 2003 onwards with a view to ensure th at the framing of subordinate legislation 
is not delayed. The Committee, however, finds that the responses from the 
Ministries/Departments have not been prompt in this  monitoring exercise undertaken on 
behalf of the Committee. 
  
 In view of the above position, the Committee once again reiterates its recommendation 
that the Ministries/Departments should ensure putti ng in place subordinate legislation 
positively within a period of six months of coming into force of the Act. The Committee 
further recommends that in case the Ministry fails to meet with this deadline, they should 
invariably approach the Committee for seeking exten sion of time. The Committee further 
recommends that in cases where the time limit of si x months is not adhered to, they should, 
while laying rules/regulations before the Parliament invariably lay a statement explaining the 
reasons why the framing of rules/regulations was delayed beyond six months so as to keep the 
Parliament apprised of the compliance of the Parlia ment’s mandate  conferred upon the 
Executive.” 
(192 
nd 
 Report) 
(Presented on 26 August 2011)  
 
  Rules/Regulations/Orders/bye-laws are laid by dif ferent Ministries on the Table of the 
House under various provisions of parent Acts passe d by Parliament. These Rules/ 
Regulations/Orders/bye-laws are published in the of ficial Gazette before being laid on the 
Table of the House. Even after they are laid, it is  very difficult to get access to these 
Notifications. The Committee recommends that such R ules/Regulations/Orders, etc. laid on 
the Table of the House should be invariably uploade d on the websites of respective Ministries 
immediately on the same day when they have been lai d on the Table of the House, for 
information of Members of Parliament and people at large for their easy access. 
201 
st  Report 
(Presented on 14 th  December, 2012)  
 
The Committee observes that the whole process of en acting laws is defeated if rules 
are not framed and laid on the Table of the House i n time.  A reasonable delay could be 
understood but unjustifiably long delays should be avoided and the Ministries should work 
towards improving this position.   The Committee hopes that Ministry would strive to k eep 

the delay to the minimum and take care that Notific ations are laid on the Table of the House 
at the first available opportunity after publication of Notifications. 
  
The Committee would like to impress upon the Minist ry that it is their responsibility 
to ensure that copies of the Notifications are prin ted timely and for this purpose, they need to 
evolve a suitable mechanism to ensure that notifica tions are laid in time.   The Committee is 
happy that the Ministry has evolved an internal mechanism/ procedure for this purpose.  The 
Committee hopes that it would take action according ly in order to comply with the 
prescribed schedule in the matter of laying of statutory Notifications. 
 
The Ministry must take appropriate step to remove l acuna, if any, administrative or 
otherwise, causing such long delay by being little proactive and prompt.  Further, the 
Ministries should take it up with the Ministry of U rban Development for late receiving of 
printed copies of the Notification.
