2.  While scrutinizing these Orders, the Committee note d 
that there was a considerable time lag between issu e  of 

Notifications and their laying in some cases. The a nnexed 
statement also indicates the period of delay in cas es where 
Notifications have not been laid as per the time sc hedule 
prescribed by the Committee. The Committee observed  that 
out of the total of 135 delayed Notifications, ther e were 96 
Notifications where no delay statement was appended  to. 
However, the bulk of delayed Notifications were fro m the 
Ministry of  Road Transport and Highways which come s to 
around 40.7% of the total delayed Notifications. 
 
The observations/recommendations of the Committee 
in respect of the specific Ministries/Departments w here delay 
in laying of Notifications has been noticed, are as follows: -  
 
(i) Ministry of AYUSH  
 
 The  Ministry of AYUSH have laid only one 
Notification (Sl. No. 19) which has been delayed by 5 months 
and is accompanied with delay statement. The reason  given 
by the Ministry for delay is as under: 
 “Laying of the Regulation made under the provision s 
of Homoeopathy Central Council Act, 1973 namely 
“Homoeopathy (Degree Course) Amendment Regulations,  
2015” vide  gazette Notification no. 12-13/2006-CCH(Pt.V) 
published in Part-III, Section 4, of Gazette of Ind ia dated the 
14 
th  July, 2015 published by Central Council of 
Homoeopathy, a statutory body under the Ministry of  
AYUSH (erstwhile Department of AYUSH under Ministry  of 
Health and Family Welfare). The reasons for delay i n laying 
the notified Regulation in both the Houses of Parli ament are 
given below:- 
 
(i)  The Regulation notified by CCH on 14 
th  July, 
2015. 

(ii)  CCH furnished the notified copies of the 
regulation to the Department on 17.08.2015. 
(iii)  The copies could not be laid by 13.08.2015 
(the last date of the session) as delay occurred 
in completing the formalities for laying. 
 
 The Committee takes serious note of such a long 
delay of 5 months and find the reasons of delay giv en by 
the Ministry unconvincing and evasive. In view of t he fact 
that it is a statutory obligation to lay the 
notifications/orders/rules on the Table of the Hous e in 
time, the situation should have been assessed well in 
advance and adequate arrangements should have been 
made in respect thereof. The Committee advises the 
Ministry of AYUSH to take precaution in future so t hat 
such delay does not recur and time schedule prescri bed in 
Committee’s  131 
st  Report be strictly adhered to. 
 
(ii) Ministry of Chemical and Fertilizers 
 (Department of Chemicals and Petrochemicals)  
 
Ministry of Chemical and Fertilizers (Department of  
Chemicals and Petrochemicals) has laid  one Notification (Sl. 
No. 20) and has no delay statement appended thereto . The 
delay period is of astounding 21 months. 
 
The Committee is constrained to note that not only 
has there been inordinate delay in  laying of the o nly one 
Notification by the Ministry of Chemical and Fertil izers 
(Department of Chemicals and Petrochemicals) on the  
Table of the House but also gross failure of that t o have 
appended the delay statement with it. The 
Ministry/Department must ensure that Notifications 
should be laid in time on the Table of the House. I t also 

must ensure to append a delay statement in all such  cases 
in future. 
 
 
(iii) Ministry of Civil Aviation  
 
 Ministry of Civil Aviation have laid only one 
Notification (Sl. No. 22) which has been delayed by  8 
months. The Ministry have appended delay statement with 
the Notification and the reasons given by the Minis try are as 
under:- 
 “The Gazette Notification to make amendment in rul e 
2 and to insert a new rule 9A in the Aircraft (Carr iage of 
Dangerous Goods) Rules, 2003 vide  G.S.R. No. 296 (E), 
dated the 16 
th  April, 2015 published by the Ministry of Civil 
Aviation was to be laid in both the Houses of Parli ament. The 
authenticated copies of Gazette Notification along with 
bilingual explanatory notes were sent to Lok Sabha/ Rajya 
Sabha Secretariat for laying them on the Table of t he Houses 
of Parliament during the Monsoon Session of Parliam ent 
2015. However, due to the fact that no question day  was left 
for Ministry of Civil Aviation, the papers could no t be laid on 
the Table of the Houses of Parliament. Therefore, n ow 
Gazette Notification is being submitted along with the 
explanatory notes before both the Houses of Parliament.” 
 
The Committee, time and again, have emphasized 
that laying of rules/regulations/orders is a statut ory 
obligation of the Ministries and should be complete d on 
priority within specified time-frame. The Ministry of Civil 
Aviation should understand the implications of such  
failures. However, the Ministry of Civil Aviation h ave 
failed to comply with the recommendations of the 
Committee in this regard by delaying it for 8 month s and 

then sending on the day when the laying could not b e 
undertaken as session was nearing its end. This is in 
violation of the recommendation of the Committee in  this 
regard. The Committee emphasizes that Ministry shou ld 
adhere to the time schedule in laying of Notificati ons as 
prescribed in Committee’s 131 st  Report. 
 
(iv) Ministry of Commerce and Industry 
 (Department of Commerce) 
  
The Ministry of Commerce and Industry (Department 
of Commerce) have laid 6 Notifications (Sl. Nos. 26 -31) out 
of which one Notification (Sl. No. 26) has been del ayed by 4 
months and there is no delay statement appended thereto.  
 
 The Committee notes that there has been delay in 
laying of one Notification and no delay statement has been 
attached to it. The Committee reiterates its 
recommendation contained in its 135 
th  Report that in case 
of delay in laying of Notifications etc., invariabl y, a delay 
statement should be attached. The Ministry of Comme rce 
and Industry (Department of Commerce) should ensure  
such compliance in future. 
 
(v) Ministry of  Consumer Affairs, Food and Public 
Distribution 
 (Department of Food and Public Distribution) 
 
 Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public 
Distribution  (Department of Food and Public Distri bution) 
have laid 10 Notifications (Sl. Nos. 44 to 53) on t he Table of 
the House during the Session. One of them (Sl. No. 47) has 
been delayed by 6 Months and has no delay statement  
appended thereto.  

  
 The Committee notes with concern  that Ministry 
of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution 
(Department of Food and Public Distribution) did no t act 
promptly to lay the Notification (Sl. No. 47) on th e Table 
of the House. Had they taken prompt action, the del ay 
would not have occurred. The Committee, therefore, 
recommends that the Ministry of Consumer Affairs, F ood 
and Public Distribution (Department of Food and Pub lic 
Distribution) should act promptly to avoid such del ay and 
in case of such delays in laying of Notifications, delay 
statements should invariably be accompanied with them. 
  
 
 
(vi)  Ministry of Corporate Affairs 
 
Ministry of Corporate Affairs have laid 23 
Notifications (Sl. Nos. 54 to 76). Out of  these,  8  
Notifications  have been delayed. 3 Notifications (Sl. Nos. 54, 
58 - 59) have been delayed for  a period of 5 month  in each 
case and there is no delay statement appended to th ose 
Notifications. Whereas other 5 Notifications (Sl. N os. 62 - 
66) have been delayed for a period of  6 to 10  mon ths  and 
are accompanied with a delay statement. The reasons of delay 
given by the Ministry is that the Notifications cou ld not be 
laid on the Table of the House due to volume of pag es and  
late receipt of printed copies of the Notifications. 
 
 The Committee  expresses its deep concern about 
the reply given by the Ministry of Corporate Affair s that 
the delay in laying of Notifications was delayed du e to 
volume of pages, which took time (6 to 10 months) f or 
printing at the Government Press.  The Ministry of 

Corporate Affairs  should, in future, ensure that a ll its 
papers are laid before the House as prescribed in t he 
Committee’s 131 st  Report. The Ministry should frame a 
suitable mechanism to expedite the printing of pape rs so 
as to avoid undue delay.  
 
(vii)  Ministry of Defence 
  
The Ministry of Defence have laid only one 
Notification (Sl. No. 77) which has been delayed by  6 
months. The Ministry have appended delay statement with 
the Notification and the reasons given by the Minis try is as 
under:- 
“The Pune Cantonment Board (Local Body Tax) Bye-
laws, 2015 were sent to the Government of India Pre ss for 
publication in the Official Gazette of India on 04. 06.2015. It 
took some time to get the published copies of the N otification 
from the Government of India Press. The Sitting of the Eighth 
(5 
th ) Session of Sixteenth Lok Sabha and Two Hundred an d 
Thirty Six (236 th ) Session of Rajya Sabha concluded on 13 th  
August, 2015. 
2. As per the procedure for laying of Papers on the  Table 
of Lok Sabha/Rajya Sabha issued from time to time b y Lok 
Saha/Rajya Sabha Secretariat, the papers to be laid  before the 
Houses are required to be forwarded to them at leas t three 
days in advance before the date on which these were  
proposed to be laid on the Table. It is requested t hat the 
marginal delay on the part of Ministry of Defence m ay kindly 
be condoned.” 
 
 The Committee finds that laying of Notifications 
was delayed due to late receipt of published copies  of 
Notification in the Ministry. The Committee does no t 
accept this as a convincing reason at all for such delays in 

laying of statutory papers. The Committee observes that it 
is the Ministry’s prime responsibility to ensure th at 
Subordinate Legislation is laid before the Parliame nt 
within the prescribed schedule and accordingly, it is for 
the Ministry only to ensure that they receive the p rinted 
copies  timely.  
 The Committee is not inclined to accept the late 
availability of printed copies of Notifications fro m the 
Government of India Press as the reason for delay i n 
laying of the Notifications. The Committee directs all the 
Ministries that, in case, there is delay in procuring printed 
copies in time, they may obtain G.S.R. and S.O. num bers 
from the Government of India Press and prepare 
requisite number of copies in cyclostyled form for laying 
in the Parliament as suggested by Secretary, Minist ry of  
Urban Development, the controlling Ministry of 
Government of India Press, in its meeting held on 3 0  
July, 2013. The Committee also recommends that this  
process may be adopted by Ministries suo moto  on 
immediate basis so as to avoid such delays henceforth. 
 
 
(viii) Ministry of Finance 
(a)    (Department of Economic Affairs) 
 
 Ministry of Finance  (Department of Economic 
Affairs) have laid 15 Notifications (Sl. Nos. 80 to  94). Only 1 
Notification (Sl. No. 92) has been delayed by 14 Mo nths and 
there is no delay statement appended to it.  
  
   The Committee notes that there has been delay in 
laying of one Notification and no delay statement has been 
attached to it. The Committee reiterates its 
recommendation contained in its 135 
th  Report that in case 

of delay in laying of Notifications etc., invariabl y a delay 
statement should be attached. The Ministry should e nsure 
such compliance in future.  
 
(b)    (Department of Financial Services) 
 
Ministry of Finance (Department of Financial 
Services) have laid 25 Notifications (Sl. Nos. 95 - 119) during 
the Session. Out of the total Notifications laid, 6 Notifications 
have been delayed.  Out of these 6 delayed Notifica tions,  5  
Notifications (Sl. Nos. 106 – 107 & 113 - 115) have   been 
delayed between 8 months to 4 years and 5 months th ough 
with delay statement appended thereto and one Notif ication 
(Sl. No. 103) was delayed  by 5 months and there is  no delay 
statement appended to it. The reasons forwarded by the 
Ministry for delay are as under:- 
  
(1) “The Notification dated 06.07.2011 regarding 
amendment in State Bank of Travancore (Employees) 
Pension Regulations, 1995, published in the Gazette  of India, 
vide No. 144 on 22.07.2011. 
 As the Bank furnished the requisite copies of Gaze tte 
Notification after the stipulated period, clarifica tion was 
sought from State Bank of Travancore (SBT). 
 The Bank has reported that the amendment to 
Regulation was notified in the Gazette on 22.07.201 1 and has 
stated that delay in submission was due to unawaren ess and 
this was the first opportunity for SBT to frame and  lay the 
notifications, earlier it was being done by State B ank of India 
(SBI). It has further requested to condone the dela y with 
assurance to be meticulous in future. 
 In view of the above, the said Notification could not 
be laid on the Table of both the Houses on earlier occasions. 

Delay in this regard is deeply regretted and may pl ease be 
condoned.” 
 
(2) “The Notification dated 08.10.2014 regarding 
amendment in State Bank of Bikaner & Jaipur (Employ ees’) 
Pension Regulations, 1995 vide  Notification No. 290, dated 
10.10.2014. 
 As the Bank furnished the requisite copies of Gaze tte 
Notification after the stipulated period, clarifica tion was 
sought from State Bank of Bikaner and Jaipur (SBBJ). 
 The Bank has reported that the amendment to 
Regulation was notified in the Gazette on 10.10.201 4 and has 
stated that this was the first opportunity for SBBJ  to take up 
such matter with the Ministry and all such matters were 
earlier being dealt by SBI. Moreover, some delay al so 
occurred due to the delayed receipt of print out of  the 
notification from the Government of India Press. It  has 
further assured that they have already put in place  a 
mechanism to ensure meticulous compliance of such m atters 
and requested to condone the delay. 
 In view of the above, the said Notification could not 
be laid on the Table of the both the Houses on earl ier 
occasions. Delay in this regard is deeply regretted  and may 
please be condoned.” 
 
 The Committee are surprised at the length of time 
taken by the Ministry of Finance  (Department of 
Financial Services) in laying of their Notification s 
extending from fourteenth months to almost five yea rs!  
The Committee is unable to accept the reasons given  by 
the Ministry of Finance  (Department of Financial 
Services) for the delay in laying, such as, late re ceiving of 
printed copies of Notifications from the Government  
Press, administrative reasons, time taken to comple te 

procedural formalities, etc. It only reflects the l ack of 
seriousness in the Ministry in fulfilling its const itutional 
responsibility towards  Parliament. The Committee 
expects the Ministry to be careful about laying of its 
papers and see to it that persons responsible for t his 
important obligation remain vigilant about it. It o nly 
reflects the lack of seriousness on the part of  th e Ministry 
in fulfilling its constitutional responsibility to Parliament. 
 
 
 (c)  (Department of Revenue) 
 
 Ministry of Finance (Department of Revenue) have 
laid 76 Notifications (Sl. Nos. 120 to 195) on the Table of the 
House. Out of these 18 Notifications (Sl. Nos. 120 – 122, 136 
– 142, 148 – 150, 170 & 186-189) have been delayed by 4 to 
6 months respectively and no delay statement have b een 
attached to any of these Notifications. 
  
The Committee takes a serious view not only of the 
delay in laying of eighteen Notifications (by the 
Department of Revenue) on the Table of the House bu t 
also for its failure to append the required delay s tatement 
thereto. The Ministry/Department must realise the 
possible implications of failing to meet this requi rement 
that tantamounts to diluting Executive’s accountabi lity to 
Parliament. It must ensure to append a delay statem ent in 
all such cases in future.

  Department of Health and Family Welfare have laid 2

(Sl. Nos. 202 to 222), out of these four Notificati ons (Sl. Nos.

  (Department of Higher Education)

(xii) Ministry of Labour and Employment 
 
 Ministry of Labour and Employment have laid 7 
Notifications (Sl. Nos. 231 to 237).  Out of these,  4 
Notifications (Sl. Nos. 231–233 & 235) have been de layed by  
7 months each and there is  no delay statement appe nded  to

above Notifications could not be laid on the Table of Rajya 
Sabha during the Monsoon Session as CERC had forwar ded 
the same to Ministry of Power on 1 
st  September, 2015 only. 
These Notifications are being laid on the first ava ilable 
opportunity.” 
 

The Committee hopes that the Ministry of Power 
would avoid such instances of delay in laying of 
subordinate legislation in future and would remove 
lacuna, if any, causing delay. The Committee also 
impresses upon the Ministry to take note of the fac t that 
in case there is a delay in the laying of any Statu tory 
Notifications, the same should be accompanied by a delay 
statement while it is being laid. The Committee als o 
advises the Ministry to avoid recurrence of such de lays in 
future. 
 
 
(xv) Ministry of Road Transport and Highways 
 
 The Ministry of Road Transport & Highways have 
laid 79 Notifications
 on the Table of the House (Sl. Nos. 272 
to 350). A total of 55 Notifications have been dela yed out of 
which 11 Notifications (Sl. Nos. 305, 307 & 311–319 ) are 
accompanied by delay statements and 44 Notification s (Sl. 
Nos. 272 –273, 278–304, 306, 308–310, 320–329, & 33 1) 
have no delay statements appended with them. The de lay 
period ranges from 4 months to 20 months. The reasons given 
by the Ministry is that it took some time to comple te the 
procedural formalities and, therefore, papers could  not be laid 
in time. 
 
The Committee does not accept the reasons of the 
delay given by the Ministry of Road Transport and 
Highways that it took some time to collect the pape rs and 
complete the procedural formalities, as convincing.  The 
Committee wonders as to how can it take one year and ten 
months to receive Notifications and to complete 
procedural formalities. The Committee feels that Ministry 
did not take adequate precaution to avoid the delay . The 

Committee further takes a serious view of the fact that 
even after delay of one year and ten months in cert ain 
case, Ministry did not feel it necessary to append a delay 
statement so as to apprise the Parliament  explaini ng  the 
reasons of delay in laying of Notifications on the Table of 
the House. The Committee recommends that the Minist ry 
should initiate urgent measures so as to avoid dela y in 
completing the procedural formalities so that such delay 
can be eliminated. 
 
 
(xvi)  Ministry of Shipping 
 
 Ministry of Shipping have laid 18 Notifications (S l. 
Nos. 352 to 369) out of which 13 Notification have delayed. 9 
Notifications (Sl. Nos. 358-366) have been delayed by 4 to 6 
month and have no delay statement appended with the m. 
Another 4 Notifications (Sl. Nos. 352, 355-357)  ha ve been 
delayed by 8 to 20 months and have delay statements  
appended with them. The reasons for delay given by the 
Ministry is that due to oversight Notifications cou ld not be 
laid on the Table of the House. 
 
 The Committee cannot appreciate the reasons 
given by the Ministry of Shipping that Notification s could 
not be laid on the Table of the House due to oversi ght. 
This is sheer lackadaical approach on the part of t he 
Ministry to have neglected the constitutional 
responsibility. This approach calls for 
relook/introspection so as to bring improvement in the 
current situation. 
 
(xvii) Ministry of Urban Development 
 

 Ministry of Urban Development have laid 9 
Notifications (Sl. Nos. 372-380) on the Table of th e House. 
Out of 7 Notifications which have been delayed, 2 
Notifications (Sl. Nos. 377-378) have been delayed by 5 to 6 
months and have no delay statement attached to both  of the 
delayed Notifications. Other 5 Notifications (Sl. N os. 372-
376) have been delayed from 6 to 10 months and 
accompanied with a delay statement. The reason of d elay 
given by the Ministry is that it took some time to collect the 
papers and complete the procedural formalities ther efore, 
papers could not be laid in time on the Table of  the House. 
 
 The Committee are not convinced by the reason 
given for delay by the Ministry that the printed co pies of 
Gazette Notifications could not be made available i n time. 
Ministry should have mentioned the date as to when the 
printed copies were to be given to it by the Govern ment of 
India Press as also should have made sincere effort s to get 
the printing expedited. The delay could have been 
avoided, had adequate precaution been taken by the 
Ministry to expedite decision in the matter. The 
Committee feels  that the Ministry of Urban Develop ment 
did not take it with required seriousness. Such del ays in 
future, particularly on account of delay in receivi ng 
printed copies of notifications will not be accepta ble to the 
Committee. Ministry would have to adhere to the tim e 
schedule for notifying as well as laying of papers as 
prescribed in Committee’s 131 
st  Report. 
 
3.   Committee impresses upon all the 
Ministries/Departments to take immediate steps to e nsure 
timely and proper laying of subordinate legislation . The 
Committee, accordingly, wishes to bring to the noti ce of all 
Ministries/Departments of the Government of India, 

particularly, the defaulting ones, the following 
recommendations, as contained in its 131 
st 
, 135 
th 
, 152 
nd  ,   
192 nd  , 201 st  and 212 th  Reports: 
 
 “Orders required to be laid before the House shoul d 
be laid (i) if the House is not in Session, during the Session 
immediately following the date of publication of the Order 
in the Official Gazette and (ii) if the House is in  Session, 
on the date of the publication of the Order, during  its 
continuance and in case the time lag between the da te of 
publication and the date of the closing of the Sess ion is 
less than 15 clear days, before the expiry of the S ession 
immediately following the said Session. All the 
Ministries/Departments of Government of India shoul d 
henceforth comply with this schedule in the matter of 
laying of the Orders issued under various Acts of 
Parliament on the Table of the Rajya Sabha. 
(131 st  Report) 
(Presented on 15 December 2000) 
 
 “The Committee has, time and again, emphasized 
that it is essential that in case there is a delay in the laying 
of Statutory Orders, the concerned Ministry/Departm ent 
should invariably append a delay statement along with the 
Notifications being laid so as to apprise Parliamen t of the 
causes of delay. The Committee desires all 
Ministries/Departments to take a note of this, sinc e the 
intention is that through the process of formulatio n of a 
delay statement, the Ministry is able to introspect, identify 
bottlenecks and devise remedial measures”. 
(135 th  Report) 
(Presented on 27 July 2001) 
 

 “In the opinion of the Committee, every notificati on 
should be assigned a distinctive number in order to  give it 
a separate identity and similarly, no notification should be 
published/laid which does not carry a notification 
number. The Committee expects all 
Ministries/Departments of Government of India to 
exercise caution in this regard. In case where ther e are 
more than one Notifications under a single file, th e 
Ministries/Departments should ensure that the file 
number on each notification should be suitably 
distinguished from one another.” 
(152 
nd 
 Report) 
(Presented on 26 August 2004)  
 
 “In addition to the concern expressed by the 
Committee over delay in laying of Notifications on the 
Table of the House, the Committee also express thei r deep 
concern over delay in framing of rules/regulations under 
different Acts. The Committee in its 47 
th  report presented 
to the House on 14.9.1981 has recommended that the rule-
making process should be completed within a period of six 
months of the coming into force on an Act. The 
Committee has further recommended that in case a 
Ministry is not able to adhere to this time limit, it should 
seek extension of time for completing the rule-maki ng 
process. The recommendation of the committee reads as 
follows:- 
 
  “The Committee feels that the rule-
making process could well have been completed 
within the time limit of six months which the 
Committee has laid down for making of rules 
under an Act after coming into force of that Act. 

Where however, a Ministry does not find it possible 
to adhere to the time limit, they should inform the  
Committee of the reasons why they cannot make 
rules within the time limit and seek extension of 
time for completing the rule-making process.” 
 The Committee is constrained to take note of the 
fact that the Ministries/Departments of Government of 
India are not complying with the Committee’s 
recommendation to complete the process of framing o f 
subordinate legislation contemplated under various Acts 
of Parliament within a period of six months. At the  same 
time, the Committee also does not receive requests for 
extension of time for completing the rule-making pr ocess 
in terms of its recommendations as above from most of 
the Ministries/Departments. The Committee takes a 
serious note of the prevailing situation in which t he 
Ministries/Departments are neither able to complete  the 
task of framing rules/regulations under different A cts 
within the given six months’ period nor do they suo-motu  
approach the Committee for seeking extension of tim e. 
The Committee further notes that in order to ensure  
timely framing of rules/regulations it has taken an  
initiative to monitor the progress of framing of 
subordinate legislation in respect of all legislati ons 
brought about by different Ministries/Departments o f 
Government of India from the year 2003 onwards with  a 
view to ensure that the framing of subordinate legi slation 
is not delayed. The Committee, however, finds that the 
responses from the Ministries/Departments have not been 
prompt in this monitoring exercise undertaken on be half 
of the Committee. 
  

 In view of the above position, the Committee once 
again reiterates its recommendation that the 
Ministries/Departments should ensure putting in pla ce 
subordinate legislation positively within a period of six 
months of coming into force of the Act. The Committ ee 
further recommends that in case the Ministry fails to meet 
with this deadline, they should invariably approach  the 
Committee for seeking extension of time. The Commit tee 
further recommends that in cases where the time lim it of 
six months is not adhered to, they should, while la ying 
rules/regulations before the Parliament invariably lay a 
statement explaining the reasons why the framing of  
rules/regulations was delayed beyond six months so as to 
keep the Parliament apprised of the compliance of t he 
Parliament’s mandate  conferred upon the Executive.” 
(192 
nd 
 Report) 
(Presented on 26 August 2011)  
 
 
  Rules/Regulations/Orders/bye-laws are laid by 
different Ministries on the Table of the House unde r 
various provisions of parent Acts passed by Parliam ent. 
These Rules/ Regulations/Orders/bye-laws are publis hed 
in the official Gazette before being laid on the Table of the 
House. Even after they are laid, it is very difficu lt to get 
access to these Notifications. The Committee recomm ends 
that such Rules/Regulations/Orders, etc. laid on th e Table 
of the House should be invariably uploaded on the 
websites of respective Ministries immediately on th e same 
day when they have been laid on the Table of the Ho use, 
for information of Members of Parliament and people  at 
large for their easy access. 
201 
st  Report 

(Presented on 14 th  December, 2012)  
 
The Committee observes that the whole process of 
enacting laws is defeated if rules are not framed a nd laid 
on the Table of the House in time.  A reasonable de lay 
could be understood but unjustifiably long delays s hould 
be avoided and the Ministries should work towards 
improving this position.   The Committee hopes that 
Ministry would strive to keep the delay to the mini mum 
and take care that Notifications are laid on the Ta ble of 
the House at the first available opportunity after 
publication of Notifications. 
  
The Committee would like to impress upon the 
Ministry that it is their responsibility to ensure that copies 
of the Notifications are printed timely and for thi s 
purpose, they need to evolve a suitable mechanism t o 
ensure that notifications are laid in time.   The C ommittee 
is happy that the Ministry has evolved an internal 
mechanism/ procedure for this purpose.  The Committ ee 
hopes that it would take action accordingly in orde r to 
comply with the prescribed schedule in the matter o f 
laying of statutory Notifications. 
 
The Ministry must take appropriate step to 
remove lacuna, if any, administrative or otherwise,  
causing such long delay by being little proactive a nd 
prompt.  Further, the Ministries should take it up with the 
Ministry of Urban Development for late receiving of  
printed copies of the Notification. 
 
212 
th   Report 
(Presented on  3 rd  September, 2013)

.

(ii) 

Report 
 
        Laying of Statutory Orders on the Table of Rajya Sabha 
   
 During the 238
th    Session of the Rajya Sabha,     (23 rd    February  – 16 th   March, 2016), a 
total of 404 (Four Hundred Four) Statutory Orders/N otifications relating to 
Rules/Regulations/Schemes/Bye-laws etc. framed unde r the Constitution/ Acts of Parliament were 
laid on the Table of the House by various Ministrie s/Departments of the Government of India. The 
details of the Gazette Notifications in which these  were published and  the date of their laying on 
the Table of the Rajya Sabha have been indicated Mi nistry-wise, in a  Statement placed at 
Annexure . Of the total 404 Notifications that were laid, th ere has been a delay in laying of 116 
(29%) of these. Notifications of various Ministries /Departments that have been laid, are as per the 
details given below:-

2.  While scrutinizing these Orders, the Committee noted that there was a considerable time lag 
between issue  of Notifications and their laying in  some cases. The annexed statement also 
indicates the period of delay in cases where Notifi cations have not been laid as per the time 
schedule prescribed by the Committee. The Committee  observed that out of the total 116 delayed 
Notifications, there were 33 Notifications where no delay statement was appended to. However, the 
bulk of delayed Notifications were from the Ministr y of  Road Transport and Highways which 
comes to around 66.37% of the total delayed Notifications. 
 
The observations/recommendations of the Committee i n respect of the specific 
Ministries/Departments where delay in laying of Notifications has been noticed, are as follows: -  
 
(i)  Ministry of Civil Aviation  
  
 Ministry of Civil Aviation  have laid 4 Notificati ons (Sl. Nos. 5 to 8). Two of them (Sl. No. 
5 and 8) have been delayed by 5 months each and are  accompanied with delay statement. The 
reason given by the Ministry for delay is as under:- 
  
 “The Ministry of Civil Aviation (Height Restrictio ns of Safeguarding of Aircraft 
Operations) Rules, 2015 were sent on 30.9.2015 to t he Government of India Press, Mayapuri with 
a request to provide 150 copies of the printed noti fication for record/laying on the Table of the 
House. Although the Rules were published in the Gaz ette on 1.10.2015, printed copies of the same 
were awaited from the Government of India Press and  hence the Rules could not be laid on the 
Table of the House in the last Winter Session. Subsequently, it came to notice that due to change in 
the guidelines, the physical printing of Gazette No tification of Government of India has been 
dispensed and exclusive e-publishing of the same has been started.” 
 
 The reasons cited by Ministry of Civil Aviation  i .e. Notifications could not be laid 
down because the printed copies of Notifications could not be provided by the Government of 
India Press in time, is an oft-repeated excuse. Man y Ministries have been citing this as a 
reason for delay, quite often. It reflects the lack adaisical approach on the part of the 
Ministry. On account of delay in getting printed co pies of Notifications from Printing Press 
so as to adhere to the time schedule as prescribed in Committee’s 131
st    Report, they may 
obtain the G.S.R./S.O. number from the Government o f India Press in advance and print the 

same in a cyclostyle form so as to lay the Notification in time. This had also been suggested by 
the Ministry of Urban Development, the controlling Ministry for Government of India Press.  
 
(ii) Ministry of Coal 
   
 The Ministry of Coal have laid 2 Notifications (Sl . Nos. 9 and 10) out of which one (Sl. No. 
9) has been delayed by 5 months. There is no delay statement appended with the Notifications. 
   
 The Committee finds that Ministry of Coal have not  only delayed the laying of 
Notifications but have also failed to append delay statement thereto. The Committee, in the 
absence of delay statements, are not able to know t he actual reasons behind the delay in 
laying of Notifications. The Committee have clearly  mentioned in its 135
th  Report that delay 
statements should invariably be appended to wheneve r there is a delay in laying of 
Notifications. The Committee, therefore, impresses upon the Ministry of Coal to strictly 
adhere to the time schedule as prescribed in Commit tee’s Report, and, in case of any delay in 
a laying, a delay statement should invariably be appended thereto. 
 
(iii)  Ministry of Communications and Information Technology 
 (Department of Telecommunications) 
 
The Ministry of Communications and Information Tech nology (Department of 
Telecommunications) have laid 4 Notifications (Sl. Nos. 13 to 16) out of which 3 Notifications (Sl. 
Nos. 13 to 15)  have been delayed by 6 to 11 months . Moreover, there is  no delay statement  
appended to any of the notifications so delayed.  
     
 The Committee is of the considered opinion that had  the Ministry of Communications 
and Information Technology (Department of Telecommu nications) exercised a bit caution, 
they would have avoided such instances of delay as delay period is not exceptionally long. 
Further, a delay statement is also not appended wit h any of these. The Committee, therefore,  
reiterates its recommendation as contained in its 1 35 
th  Report i.e. to attach a delay statement, 
wherever required, and simultaneously devise methods to introspect and ensure bottlenecks. 
 
 
 

 
(iv) Ministry of Corporate Affairs  
 
 Ministry of Corporate Affairs  have laid 7 Notific ations (Sl. Nos. 18 to 24). Only 1 
Notification (Sl. No. 19) has been delayed by 5 months and there is no delay statement appended to 
it.  
  
   The Committee notes that though there has been dela y in laying of one Notification, 
no delay statement has been attached to it. The Com mittee expects the Ministry to be careful 
and responsible in these matters henceforth.  The M inistry should ensure such compliance in 
future with due caution so that such recurrence does’nt take place. 
 
(v) Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Cha nge 
 
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change have laid 3 Notifications (Sl.Nos.25 - 
27), out of these only one Notification (Sl.No.26) has been delayed and that too by 1 year. There is 
no delay statement appended thereto. 
 
The Committee expresses its deep concern over the i nordinate delay that has taken 
place in the laying of one Notification. The Commit tee  also takes serious note of the fact that 
the Ministry has not appended any delay statement w ith the delayed Notification. The 
Committee is wondering as to how in absence of any delay statement can it be ascertained 
what caused this inordinate delay. The Committee, t herefore,  recommends that the Ministry 
of Environment, Forest and Climate Change should ta ke all necessary precautions in future 
to avoid recurrence of such situations and append delay statements invariably. 
 
(vi) Ministry of Finance 
 (Department of Revenue) 
 
 Ministry of Finance (Department of Revenue) have la id 140 Notifications (Sl. Nos. 104 to 
243) on the Table of the House. Out of these 20 Notifications (Sl. Nos. 141-160) have been delayed 
by 4 to 8 months respectively and no delay statemen t have been attached to any of these delayed 
Notifications. 
 

This is just not acceptable to the Committee that 14% (20 out of 140) Notifications laid 
by the Ministry did not have delay statements. Whil e there may be a reason for the delay, 
there cannot be any reason for not furnishing reason therefor. The Ministry must understand 
the implications for not doing so regularly and tha t too in such a large number of cases. The 
Committee makes a point that Ministry should append  a delay statement so as to apprise the 
Parliament of the reasons of delay in laying of Notifications on the Table of the House. 
 
 
(vii) Ministry of Health and Family Welfare 
 (Department of Health and Family Welfare) 
 
Ministry of Health and  Family Welfare (Department Health and Family Welfare) have laid 
3 Notifications (Sl. Nos. 244 to 246) during the Se ssion. Out of these, only one Notification (Sl. 
No. 244) has been delayed by 4 months and has no delay statement appended to it. 
 
Although there is a delay in one of the Notificatio n and that too of 4 months, yet the 
Committee take a serious view about the delay in laying of one of its Notifications and  also its 
failure to append the delay statement along with it . The Ministry/Department must ensure to 
append a delay statement henceforth should such a situation arise . 
 
(viii) Ministry of Home Affairs 
  
Ministry of Home Affairs have laid 15 Notifications  (Sl. Nos. 247 to 261). Out of  these,  5  
Notifications  have been delayed. Whereas 4 Notific ations (Sl. Nos. 248 – 249 & 252 – 253) have 
been delayed from a long period of 5 months to 2 ye ars and 8 months and are accompanied with a 
delay statement. Whereas another one Notification (Sl. No. 250) has been delayed by 8 months and 
there is no delay statement appended to it. The reasons of delay given by the Ministry is as under:- 
 
“The Notification No. 30 dated 20.08.2014 (English version) in respect of the Daman and 
Diu Panchayat (Election Procedure) Rules, 2014 was published by UT Administration of Daman 
and Diu under Section 121 (1) of ‘The Daman and Diu  Panchayat Regulation, 2012 (04 of 2012). 
The notification could not be laid on the Table of the House due to the delay in the publication of 
the Hindi translation of the notification by the UT Administration. 

The Hindi version of Notification [No.30] has now b een published on 09.10.2015 in the 
Gazette of Daman and Diu vide Notification No. 61. Hence, Notifications (both in Hindi & English 
version) is being laid on the Table of Lok Sabha/Ra jya Sabha under Section 123 of ‘The Daman 
and Diu Panchayat Regulation, 2012 (04 of 2012).” 
 
“The Notification No. 20 dated 20 
th  June, 2013 (English/Hindi version) in respect of ‘ The 
Daman and Diu Election of Upa-Sarpanch of a Gram Pa nchayat and President and Vice-President 
of District Panchayat, Rules, 2013’ was published b y UT Administration of Daman and Diu under 
Section 121(1) of ‘The Daman and Diu Panchayat Regu lation, 2012’ (04 of 2012). The 
Notification could not be laid on the Table of the Houses, due to non availability of required 
number of copies (both in Hindi/English version) from UT Administration. 
The  required number of copies of the Notification both in English/Hindi version has now 
been provided by UT Administration of Daman and Diu . Hence, it is being laid on the Table of 
Lok Sabha/Rajya Sabha under Section 123 of  ‘The Da man and Diu Panchayat Regulation, 2012’ 
(04 of 2012).” 
 
 The Committee wonders as to how it has taken as lo ng as one year and six months and 
two years and eight months, respectively,  in the p ublication of the Hindi translation of the 
Notification and non- availability of required numb er of copies (both Hindi/English version) 
from UT Administration. This is simply ridiculous a nd the Committee takes a serious note of 
this. The Ministry should find some suitable mechan ism to eliminate such instances of delay. 
This shows the lackadaisical attitude and approach of the Ministry. The Committee advises 
that Ministry should impress upon their agencies to  strictly adhere to the time schedule in 
laying of papers on the Table of the House. 
  
(ix) Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas 
 
 Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas  have laid 5  Notifications (Sl. Nos. 286 to 290) 
during the Session. Out of these 2 Notifications (S l. Nos. 286 & 290) have been delayed by 7 
months to 1 year and 6 months and no delay statement is attached to both of delayed Notifications.  
   
 The Committee are pained to notice that out of 5 N otifications which Ministry of 
Petroleum and Natural Gas have laid, two Notificati ons have been delayed from 7 months to 
18 months. Further, there is no reason given for th is inordinate delay.  This is in 

contravention of Committee’s recommendation given i n its 135 Report that Notification 
which are delayed should invariably be accompanied by delay statement. The Committee 
would like the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Ga s to take necessary steps to obviate such 
delays and in case of delay in laying of Notificati ons, a delay statement should invariably be 
appended with them. 
 
(x) Ministry of Road Transport and Highways 
 
 The Ministry of Road Transport and  Highways have laid 88 Notifications
 on the Table of 
the House (Sl. Nos. 293 to 380) out of which 77 Not ifications (87.5%) (Sl. Nos. 293 to 320 and 
322 to 370) have been delayed. All the delayed Noti fications are though accompanied by delay 
statements The delay period ranges from 5 months to  13 months. The reasons given by the 
Ministry is that it took some time to complete the procedural formalities and therefore, papers 
could not be laid in time. 
 
The Committee observes that the Ministry of Road Tr ansport and Highways lays a 
large number of Notifications every Session. This i s a voluminous task being handled by the 
Ministry of Road Transport and Highways. However, t he Committee finds that 87.5% of 
total Notifications laid by the Ministry of Road Tr ansport and Highways have been delayed 
and only 12.5% of the total Notifications have been  laid in time. The Committee notes the 
reasons for delay given by the Ministry  that it to ok ‘some time’ to collect the papers and 
complete the procedural formalities,  but cannot accept such inordinate delay as of 13 months 
under the definition of ‘some time’ for laying of p apers. The Committee feels that if the 
Ministry can lay some papers  in time, it can also lay other papers likewise. Only due 
precaution is required therefor. The Committee hope s that the Ministry should, therefore,  
look into the matter seriously to eliminate recurrence of such delays in future. 
 
 (xi) Ministry of Shipping 
 
 Ministry of Shipping have laid 18 Notifications (S l. Nos. 382 to 399). Out of these 3 
Notifications  (Sl. Nos. 382 to 384) have been dela yed. The delay period is of about 4 months in 
each case and moreover no delay statement has been attached to any of these delayed Notifications. 
 

 The Committee, in the absence of delay statements,  are not able to decipher the 
reasons behind this delay in laying of Notification s. The Committee have time and again 
mentioned in its earlier Reports that delay stateme nts should invariably be appended where 
there is delay in laying of Notifications. The Comm ittee, therefore, impresses upon the 
Ministry to strictly adhere to the time schedule. The Ministry cannot just take the Committee 
for granted  
 
3.   The Committee impresses upon all the Ministrie s/Departments to take immediate steps to 
ensure timely and proper laying of subordinate legi slation. The Committee, accordingly, wishes to 
bring to the notice of all Ministries/Departments o f the Government of India, particularly, the 
defaulting ones, the following recommendations, as contained in its 7
th , 131 
st 
, 135 
th 
, 152 
nd  ,   192 nd  
, 201 st  , 212 th  and 213 th  Reports: 
 
 “The Committee desires that for the convenience of  the public and Members, 
Ministries should henceforth send copies of 'order'  duly authenticated by the Ministers 
concerned, incorporating therein all the corrections and amendments issued till date of laying 
such 'orders' instead of laying the uncorrected cop y along with corrigenda. The Committee 
feels that to obviate any legal or technical difficulty, Ministries should examine whether there 
is any necessity of assigning a separate G.S.R. No.  to a corrigendum at the time of its 
publication in the Gazette and whether such a corri gendum should not be published without 
assigning any G.S.R. No. The Committee would, therefore, like to impress upon all Ministries 
of the Government of India that the present practice of laying the rules without incorporating 
corrigenda in the body of the rules is not a health y one. The Committee hopes that the 
Ministries will ensure supply of only corrected cop ies of the rules for laying on the Table so 
that they depict a true and correct picture and serve the desired purpose."  
7
th   Report) 
(Presented on 21 st   December 1974) 
 
 
 “Orders required to be laid before the House shoul d be laid (i) if the House is not in 
Session, during the Session immediately following t he date of publication of the Order in the 
Official Gazette and (ii) if the House is in Sessio n, on the date of the publication of the Order, 
during its continuance and in case the time lag bet ween the date of publication and the date 

of the closing of the Session is less than 15 clear  days, before the expiry of the Session 
immediately following the said Session. All the Min istries/Departments of Government of 
India should henceforth comply with this schedule i n the matter of laying of the Orders 
issued under various Acts of Parliament on the Table of the Rajya Sabha. 
(131 st  Report) 
(Presented on 15 th   December 2000) 
 
 “The Committee has, time and again, emphasized tha t it is essential that in case there is a 
delay in the laying of Statutory Orders, the concer ned Ministry/Department should 
invariably append a delay statement along with the Notifications being laid so as to apprise 
Parliament of the causes of delay. The Committee de sires all Ministries/Departments to take 
a note of this, since the intention is that through  the process of formulation of a delay 
statement, the Ministry is able to introspect, iden tify bottlenecks and devise remedial 
measures”. 
(135 th  Report) 
(Presented on 27 th   July 2001) 
 
 “In the opinion of the Committee, every notificati on should be assigned a distinctive 
number in order to give it a separate identity and similarly, no notification should be 
published/laid which does not carry a notification number. The Committee expects all 
Ministries/Departments of Government of India to ex ercise caution in this regard. In case 
where there are more than one Notifications under a  single file, the Ministries/Departments 
should ensure that the file number on each notifica tion should be suitably distinguished from 
one another.” 
(152 
nd 
 Report) 
(Presented on 26 th   August 2004)  
 
 “In addition to the concern expressed by the Commi ttee over delay in laying of 
Notifications on the Table of the House, the Commit tee also express their deep concern over 
delay in framing of rules/regulations under differe nt Acts. The Committee in its 47 
th  report 
presented to the House on 14.9.1981 has recommended  that the rule-making process should 
be completed within a period of six months of the c oming into force of an Act. The 

Committee has further recommended that in case a Ministry is not able to adhere to this time 
limit, it should seek extension of time for complet ing the rule-making process. The 
recommendation of the committee reads as follows:- 
 
  “The Committee feels that the rule-making process c ould well have been 
completed within the time limit of six months which  the Committee has laid down for 
making of rules under an Act after coming into forc e of that Act. Where however, a 
Ministry does not find it possible to adhere to the  time limit, they should inform the 
Committee of the reasons why they cannot make rules  within the time limit and seek 
extension of time for completing the rule-making process.” 
 The Committee is constrained to take note of the f act that the Ministries/Departments 
of Government of India are not complying with the C ommittee’s recommendation to 
complete the process of framing of subordinate legi slation contemplated under various Acts 
of Parliament within a period of six months. At the  same time, the Committee also does not 
receive requests for extension of time for completi ng the rule-making process in terms of its 
recommendations as above from most of the Ministrie s/Departments. The Committee takes a 
serious note of the prevailing situation in which t he Ministries/Departments are neither able 
to complete the task of framing rules/regulations u nder different Acts within the given six 
months’ period nor do they suo-motu  approach the Committee for seeking extension of ti me. 
The Committee further notes that in order to ensure  timely framing of rules/regulations it 
has taken an initiative to monitor the progress of framing of subordinate legislation in respect 
of all legislations brought about by different Mini stries/Departments of Government of India 
from the year 2003 onwards with a view to ensure th at the framing of subordinate legislation 
is not delayed. The Committee, however, finds that the responses from the 
Ministries/Departments have not been prompt in this  monitoring exercise undertaken on 
behalf of the Committee. 
  
 In view of the above position, the Committee once again reiterates its recommendation 
that the Ministries/Departments should ensure putti ng in place subordinate legislation 
positively within a period of six months of coming into force of the Act. The Committee 
further recommends that in case the Ministry fails to meet with this deadline, they should 
invariably approach the Committee for seeking exten sion of time. The Committee further 
recommends that in cases where the time limit of si x months is not adhered to, they should, 

while laying rules/regulations before the Parliament invariably lay a statement explaining the 
reasons why the framing of rules/regulations was delayed beyond six months so as to keep the 
Parliament apprised of the compliance of the Parlia ment’s mandate  conferred upon the 
Executive.” 
(192 
nd 
 Report) 
(Presented on 26 th   August 2011)  
 
  Rules/Regulations/Orders/bye-laws are laid by dif ferent Ministries on the Table of the 
House under various provisions of parent Acts passe d by Parliament. These Rules/ 
Regulations/Orders/bye-laws are published in the of ficial Gazette before being laid on the 
Table of the House. Even after they are laid, it is  very difficult to get access to these 
Notifications. The Committee recommends that such R ules/Regulations/Orders, etc. laid on 
the Table of the House should be invariably uploade d on the websites of respective Ministries 
immediately on the same day when they have been lai d on the Table of the House, for 
information of Members of Parliament and people at large for their easy access. 
201 
st  Report 
(Presented on 14 th  December, 2012)  
 
 
The Committee observes that the whole process of en acting laws is defeated if rules 
are not framed and laid on the Table of the House i n time.  A reasonable delay could be 
understood but unjustifiably long delays should be avoided and the Ministries should work 
towards improving this position.   The Committee hopes that Ministry would strive to k eep 
the delay to the minimum and take care that Notific ations are laid on the Table of the House 
at the first available opportunity after publication of Notifications. 
  
 
The Committee would like to impress upon the Minist ry that it is their responsibility 
to ensure that copies of the Notifications are prin ted timely and for this purpose, they need to 
evolve a suitable mechanism to ensure that notifica tions are laid in time.   The Committee is 
happy that the Ministry has evolved an internal mechanism/ procedure for this purpose.  The 
Committee hopes that it would take action according ly in order to comply with the 
prescribed schedule in the matter of laying of statutory Notifications. 

 
 
The Ministry must take appropriate step to remove l acuna, if any, administrative or 
otherwise, causing such long delay by being little proactive and prompt.  Further, the 
Ministries should take it up with the Ministry of U rban Development for late receiving of 
printed copies of the Notification. 
 
212 
th   Report 
(Presented on  3 rd  September, 2013) 
 
 “The Committee is not inclined to accept the late availability of printed copies of 
Notifications from the Government of India Press as  the reason for delay in laying of the 
Notifications. The Committee directs all the Minist ries that in case there is a delay in 
procuring printed copies in time, they may obtain G .S.R. and S.O. numbers from the 
Government of India Press and prepare requisite num ber of copies in cyclostyled form for 
laying in the Parliament. The Committee also recomm ends that this process may be adopted 
by Ministries suo moto  on immediate basis so as to avoid such delays henceforth”.

INTRODUCTION 
1. I, the Chairman of the Committee on Subordinate Legislation, having been 
authorized by the Committee, do hereby present on its behalf, this Two Hundred and Twenty 
Eighth Report of the Committee.  
2.  The Committee on Subordinate Legislation, Rajya  Sabha has been constituted under 
Rule 204 of the Rules of Procedure and Conduct of B usiness in the Council of States.  The 
mandate of the Committee is to scrutinize and repor t to the Council whether the powers to 
make rules, regulations, bye-laws, schemes or other  statutory instruments conferred by the 
Constitution or delegated by Parliament have been p roperly exercised within such 
conferment or delegation as the case may be.   
3. The Committee's concern is centered mainly aroun d the serious implications of 
delayed framing of rules/regulations/orders, etc de spite the Committee’s several 
recommendations on the issue and repeated observati ons in its reports that rules/regulations 
should be framed within six months of the coming in to force of the Act.  The Committee has 
been calling the defaulting Ministries/ Departments  to know the reason for the delay, the 
problems faced by them in framing the rules/regulat ions, etc and to find solutions to the 
problems.

administered by various Ministries/Departments of t he Government of India  and the issue of 
legality of Master Circulars issued by the Reserve Bank of India under the Banking 
Regulation Act, 1949 have been covered.  The Report  contains general as well as specific 
observations/recommendations of the Committee on the subject. 
 
5. The   Committee considered and adopted the draft  Report in its meeting held on the 
9
th  August 2016.

REPORT 
ON 
THE DELAY IN FRAMING OF SUBORDINATE LEGISLATION UNDER ACTS OF 
PARLIAMENT ADMINISTERED BY THE VARIOUS MINISTRIES/DEPARTMENTS 
       
Meaning of the term “subordinate legislation” 
 
 The term “subordinate legislation” refers to notif ications, orders, schemes, rules and bye-
laws referred to in Sections 20 and 21 of the Gener al Clauses Act. In the Indian context, the term 
subordinate legislation refers to rules, regulation s, orders, schemes, bye-laws, statutes, 
ordinances, notifications or any instrument framed under an Act of Parliament or the 
Constitution.  Such subordinate legislations have t o be published in the Gazette of India and laid 
on the Table of both Houses of Parliament. As per 7 5 th  Report of the Committee on Subordinate 
Legislation, Rajya Sabha presented to the House on the 29 th  March, 1988, all “Orders” have to be 
laid on the Table of the House as it affords an opp ortunity to Members of Parliament, if they so 
desire, to move an amendment or modification to suc h “Order”, including a Motion for their 
annulment. 
 
Need for subordinate legislation 
 
 
2. The primary function of the Parliament is to pas s legislation which becomes an Act of 
Parliament. In modern times, it is not always possi ble to make laws providing every detail. In 
view of newer areas emerging, the process of law-ma king today has become not only time 
consuming but also an increasingly complicated and a technical affair. Therefore, Parliament 
lays down the broad policy framework and basic purp ose of the legislation in the form of an Act 
and leaves it to the executive, experts and technoc rats to provide for working details within the 
framework of the enactment by way of rules, regulat ions, bye-laws, schemes, Orders or other 
statutory instruments.  Powers have also been veste d/conferred under various provisions of the 
Constitution of India on the different functionaries to frame rules, regulations or schemes dealing 
with various aspects. That is why, delegated legisl ation in present days is increasingly assuming 
an important role in the process of law-making, com prising an important component of 
legislation. 

 
 
Committee on Subordinate Legislation and its Role 
 
 
3. As subordinate legislation has become an importa nt constituent element of legislation, the 
role of legislature is equally important to monitor  and examine that the subordinate legislation is 
in accordance with the spirit of the Act or Constit ution and also to keep a proper check on the 
executive exceeding its powers provided under the A cts of Parliament or the Constitution. 
Legislation is an inherent and inseparable right of  Parliament and it has to ensure that this power 
is not usurped nor transgressed under the guise of subordinate legislation. The Committee on 
Subordinate Legislation, Rajya Sabha is one such in strument and it is constituted to scrutinize 
and report to the Council of States/ Rajya Sabha wh ether the powers to make rules, regulations, 
bye-laws, schemes or other statutory instruments co nferred by the Constitution or delegated by 
Parliament have been properly exercised within such  conferment or delegation as the case may 
be. 
 
4. It is important that legislature must retain in its own hands the essential legislative 
functions which consist in declaring the legislativ e policy and laying down the standard which is 
to be enacted into rule of law, and what can be del egated is the task of subordinate legislation 
which by its own nature ancillary to the Statute which delegates the power to make it.  
 
Important Recommendations of the Committee with reg ard to framing of subordinate 
legislation  
 
5. The Statute can be fully enforced only when all the subordinate legislation stipulated 
under the Act is framed in time. The Committee, whi le carrying out its work, has found that the 
Ministries have taken considerable time in framing of the rules/regulations and therefore the Acts 
remain unimplemented or partially implemented. The Committee has, therefore, made very 
important recommendations/observations regarding th e delay in framing of rules/regulations by 
the Ministries. In 1971 the Committee in its 9 
th  Report prescribed six months time limit for 
framing the subordinate legislation contemplated un der the Act. However, in the same year the 
Committee in its 10 th  Report suggested that if Rules are not framed with in the time limit of 6 

 
months, the Secretary or Head of Department should be informed and in turn Secretary with a 
comprehensive note inform the Minister concerned an d obtain his orders.  The Committee was 
persuaded to make this suggestion for the reason th at for any non-compliance or excessive delay 
in compliance with the provision of a statute the Minister is also answerable to the House. 
 
6. The Committee in due course, however, found that  most of the Ministries do not adhere 
to the time limit of six months prescribed by it fo r framing of rules/regulations and also do not 
give appropriate reasons for such delay. The Commit tee, therefore, recommended in its 31 
st  and 
47 th  Reports as:- 
"In regard to the request of the Ministries for ext ension of time for making rules and 
regulations under various enactments, the Committee  observes that of late such requests 
have almost become a routine' and the Ministries ha ve not been adhering to the time-
limit of six months for making the rules as earlier  recommended by the Committee. In 
some cases the Committee has noticed that while req uesting for extension of time, the 
Ministries do not disclose full facts and advance i nadequate reasons for seeking such an 
extension. 
“The Committee in its Ninth Report recommended that  rules and regulations required to 
be made under a statute should be made as soon as p ossible but in no case later than six 
months from the date on which the statute comes into force." 
                          (Extract from 31 st   Report)  
(presented on 13.3.1979)  
“The Committee feels that the rule-making process c ould well have been completed 
within the time limit of six months which the Committee has laid down for making of rules 
under an Act after coming into force of that Act.  Where however, a Ministry does not 
find it possible to adhere to the time limit, they should inform the Committee of the 
reasons why they cannot make rules within the time limit and seek extension of time for 
completing the rule-making process.” 
(Para 29 of the 47 th  Report)  
      (presented on 14.9.1981)  
 

 
7. Since most of the Ministries still do not adhere  to the time limit of six months despite 
several recommendation in its consecutive reports, the  Committee reiterated its 
recommendations in its 192 nd  Report as under:- 
 
"In addition to the concern expressed by the Commit tee over delay in laying of 
Notifications on the Table of the House, the Commit tee also express its deep concern 
over delay in framing of rules/regulations under di fferent Acts. The Committee in its 47th 
report presented to the House on 14.9.1981 had reco mmended that the rule-making 
process should be completed within a period of six months of the coming into force of an 
Act. The Committee has further recommended that in case a Ministry is not able to 
adhere to this time-limit, it should seek extension  of time for completing the rule-making 
process. The recommendation of the Committee reads as follows:— 
"The Committee feels that the rule-making process c ould well have been completed 
within the time-limit of six months which the Commi ttee has laid down for making of 
rules under an Act after coming into force of that Act. Where however, a Ministry does 
not find it possible to adhere to the time-limit, t hey should inform the Committee of the 
reasons why they cannot make rules within the time- limit and seek extension of time for 
completing the rule-making process." 
 
The Committee is constrained to take note of the fa ct that the Ministries/Departments of 
Government of India are not complying with the Comm ittee's recommendation to 
complete the process of framing of subordinate legi slation contemplated under various 
Acts of Parliament within a period of six months. A t the same time, the Committee also 
does not receive requests for extension of time for  completing the rule-making process in 
terms of its recommendations as above from most of the Ministries/Departments. The 
Committee takes a serious note of the prevailing si tuation in which the 
Ministries/Departments are neither able to complete the task of framing rules/regulations 
under different Acts within the given six months' p eriod nor do they suo-motu approach 
the Committee for seeking extension of time. The Co mmittee further notes that in order to 
ensure timely framing of rules/regulations it has t aken an initiative to monitor the 
progress of framing of subordinate legislation in r espect of all legislations brought about 

 
by different Ministries/Departments of Government o f India from the year 2003 onwards 
with a view to ensure that the framing of subordina te legislation is not delayed. The 
Committee, however, finds that the responses from t he Ministries/Departments have not 
been prompt in this monitoring exercise undertaken on behalf of the Committee. 
In view of the above position, the Committee once a gain reiterates its recommendation 
that the Ministries/Departments should ensure putti ng in place subordinate legislation 
positively within a period of six months of the Act  coming into force of the Act. The 
Committee further recommends that in case the Minis try fails to meet with this deadline, 
they should invariably approach the Committee for s eeking extension of time. The 
Committee further recommends that in cases where th e time-limit of six months is not 
adhered to, they should, while laying rules/regulat ions before the Parliament invariably 
lay a statement explaining the reasons why the fram ing of rules/regulations was delayed 
beyond six months so as to keep the Parliament appr ised of the compliance of the 
Parliament's mandate conferred upon the Executive." 
[Para 2(xiv) of 192nd Report] 
(Presented on 24.8.2011) 
 
8. The Committee had, in its 212 
th  Report also reiterated the need for framing of subordinate 
legislation within the stipulated timeframe by poin ting out specific instances where the framing 
of rules/regulations have been delayed, in some cases, for more than 10 years. 
 
Committee’s Recommendation on uploading of rules/regulations on Ministry’s website 
 
 
9. Keeping in view the importance of subordinate legis lation and the need for the public to 
easily access them, the Committee had also, in its 135 
th  Report, recommended that all 
subordinate legislation should be uploaded on the website of the respective Ministries as under: 
“The Committee would like to take this opportunity to recommend that Ministries, as part 
of their e-governance initiative, put all subordina te legislation on their websites, 
preferably bilingually. The Committee further recom mends that the Ministry of 
Information Technology immediately develop a standa rd application software with an 
Internet interface for use in all Ministries, which  will provide a searchable database of 

 
subordinate legislation linked to the principal Act s administered by the respective 
Ministry.” 
(Para 10 of135th   Report)  
(presented on 27.7.2001)   
 
10. The Committee again in its 201 
st  Report stressed the very need of uploading all the  
rules/regulations, etc on the respective website of  the 
Ministries/Departments/organizations/institutions for the benefit of Members of Parliament and 
the people for easy access which is as under: 
“Rules/Regulations/Orders/bye-laws are laid by diff erent Ministries on the Table of the 
House under various provisions of parent Acts passe d by Parliament. These 
Rules/Regulations/Orders/bye-laws are published in the Official Gazette before being 
laid on the Table of the House. Even after they are  laid, it is very difficult to get access to 
these notifications. The Committee recommends that such Rules/Regulations/Orders, etc. 
laid on the Table of the House should be invariably  uploaded on the websites of 
respective Ministries immediately on the same day when they have been laid on the Table 
of the House, for information of Members of Parliam ent and people at large for their 
easy access.” 
201 st  Report 
(Presented on 14 th  December, 2012)   
 
11. Despite these recommendations, the Committee feels that Ministries/Departments do not 
pay the due attention that subordinate legislation deserves.  While delay in framing subordinate 
legislation hinders implementation, delay in laying  of the rules and regulations before the House 
impinges upon right of Members of Parliament to mov e motion for either amending or annulling 
them altogether. If such a motion is adopted by bot h Houses, the said notification shall remain 
amended or annulled accordingly.  In this backdrop,  the Committee had decided to sit with the 
Ministries and Departments of the Government of Ind ia to understand the problems faced by 
them in fulfilling the requirements concerning subo rdinate legislations and to sensitize them 
about the significance of timely framing of subordi nate legislation and its laying in Parliament. 
Accordingly, the Committee has been calling various  Ministries/Departments in this regard. The 
details of meetings held by the Committee with various Ministries/Departments, the points/issues 

 
that arise out of these meetings and the observatio ns/recommendations of the Committee have 
been enumerated in the succeeding paragraphs. The d etails of pending cases of framing of 
rules/regulations under various Acts passed by Parl iament as on 21 st  July, 2016 has been placed 
as Annexure-I. 
 
I 
DISCUSSION WITH THE MINISTRIES/DEPARTMENTS 
 
12. The Committee held discussion with the Department of Revenue, Department of 
Economic Affairs and Department of Financial Servic es of the Ministry of Finance on the 27 th  
October, 2014. Secretary, Department of Revenue, br iefed the Committee about the Acts under 
their administrative control and the rules/regulati ons that were to be framed under them. He 
informed the Committee that with respect to Finance  Act, 2013 framing of the requisite 
rules/regulations had been delayed as they related to the General Anti Avoidance Rules (GAAR) 
implementation of which had been deferred upto 1 st  April, 2015 as certain issues connected to it 
were under examination. He also informed the Commit tee about the issues on which 
rules/regulations under the Finance Act, 2014 were in the process of being framed. He also 
informed that all the Acts and subordinate legislat ion were being uploaded on the website of the 
Ministry. He further informed the Committee that ru les framed under the Income Tax Act, 
Excise & Customs Act or Prevention of Money Laundering Act are put into immediate operation 
and they will be valid, subject to Parliament amend ing or nullifying them. In response to the 
issue of framing of subordinate legislation under t he Benami Transaction Act, 1988,  he 
informed that the said Act was to be repealed by a new Act which the Ministry would shortly 
introduce in the Parliament.  
 
13. Secretary, Department of Financial Services bri efed the Committee about the Acts being 
administered by them and the status of framing of s ubordinate legislation under them. Regarding 
framing of rules/regulations under the SBI (Subsidi ary Laws) Amendment Act, 2011, LIC 
(Amendment) Act, 2011 and Actuaries Act, 2007, he i nformed that in the case of the State Bank 
of India Amendment Rules, the Ministry had sought e xtension of time upto 30 
th  June, 2015. In 

 
the case of all others, the Ministry had sought tim e upto 1 st  January, 2015 to frame all the 
rules/regulations.   
 
14. The Committee is happy to note that subsequently th e Department of Financial 
Services have completed the framing of rules/regula tions under the  SBI (Subsidiary Laws) 
Amendment Act, 2011 and have laid them on the Table  of both the Houses of Parliament. 
The Committee, however, regrets to note that the De partment of Revenue and Department 
of Financial Services has not yet completed the fra ming of subordinate legislation under 
the Finance Act, 2013; LIC (Amendment) Act, 2011 and Actuaries Act, 2007 despite a lapse 
of so many years since the passage of these Acts. T he Committee, accordingly, urges the 
Departments to expedite the process and complete th e framing of subordinate legislation 
under these Acts without any further delay.   
 
15. The Committee heard the representatives of the Ministry of Power, Ministry of Law & 
Justice (Legislative Department), Ministry of Envir onment, Forest & Climate Change and the 
Ministry of Civil Aviation on the 12 
th  February, 2015 on the reasons for delay in the fra ming of 
the rules/regulations under Acts administered by th em.  Secretary, Ministry of Power stated that 
the Electricity Act, 2003 amalgamated all the earli er Acts that existed in the power sector and 
certain amendments were made in the Act in the same  year and all the rules and regulations that 
were required to be framed under the Act by the var ious authorities, i.e. the Ministry, the Central 
Electricity Authority (CEA) or the Central Electric ity Regulatory Commission (CERC), all stand 
notified as well as laid on the Table of the House.   Under the Damodar Valley Corporation 
(DVC) Act, 1948 also, all the contemplated subordin ate legislations have been framed.  With 
respect to Energy Conservation Act, 2001 and the Energy Conservation (Amendment) Act, 2011, 
a total of 21 rules were required to be framed out of which 16 rules have been notified, 2 rules 
have not been considered necessary and 3 are under process and will be notified shortly. Total 13 
regulations were required to be framed under the En ergy Conservation Act out of which 8 
regulations have been framed and 2 are under proces s of framing and would be notified shortly. 
The Ministry is of the view that the remaining 3 re gulations are not necessary. The Committee 
again heard the Secretary, Ministry of Power, CERC,  Bureau of Energy Efficiency (BEE) and 
CEA on 28 September 2015 for further clarifications in the matter of framing of rules/regulations 

 
under the Energy Conservation Act, 2001 and subsequ ent amendments. During this meeting, 
Secretary, Ministry of Power informed the Committee  that as advised by the Committee, the 
Ministry made a reference to the Ministry of Law & Justice with regard to the necessity for 
framing of rules under Section 56 (2)(e) and (v) of the Act and once their comments are received, 
further necessary action would be taken.  He furthe r updated the Committee on the status of 
framing of 3 rules which are still pending by stati ng that rules under Section 56(2)(d) and (l) will 
be finalized by December, 2015, however, rule under  Section 56(2)(n) will take some more time 
as it involves consultation with the State Governments. DG, BEE informed that as advised by the 
Committee, they have referred the matter to the Min istry of Law & Justice on the 3 regulations 
on which they feel that no regulations need to be f ramed.  Based on the advice of the Ministry of 
Law & Justice, the matter will be placed before the  Committee and Parliament. He also updated 
the Committee on the status of framing of 2 regulat ions which are still pending by stating that 
regulation on powers and duties of Director General  (DG), BEE will be notified by 31 st   
December, 2015 and regulations on the manner and in terval of time for conduct of energy audit 
of buildings will be completed by the end of next y ear.  The regulations dealing with the energy 
audit under the powers given to the States has been  referred to the Ministry of Law & Justice as

 17. The Committee further observed that statutory organizations like Central Electricity 
Regulatory Commission and Central Electricity Autho rity do not get the subordinate legislation 
framed by them vetted from the Ministry of Law & Ju stice.  The Committee sought clarification 
on this matter from the representatives of the Legi slative Department, Ministry of Law & Justice 
who were present in the Committee’s meeting on 12 
th  February, 2015.  The Legislative 
Department expressed the following views: 
 
 Firstly, it is for the administrative Ministry to decide the necessity of making 
rules, though there is a power delegated under the provisions of the parent Act or Statute.  
But its necessity and to what extent they want to f rame the rules on a particular subject 
matter, is the domain of the administrative Ministry.   
 Secondly, nowadays, there are Acts which provide t hat the enforcement date of 
certain provisions will be different.  There is a different date for different provisions also.  
So, if the substantive provision of the Act has not  come into force, then certainly, there 
are no rules and regulations for that very provisio n which requires rules and regulations 
to be made.   
 Thirdly, it is a discretionary power that the auth ority may make rules and 
regulations or the Commission may makes rules and r egulations.  So, it does not have a 

 
binding effect.  And, as far as the word ‘may’ or ‘shall’ is to be used, generally, this word 
‘may’ has been interpreted as ‘shall’ also by way o f construction.  It is the executive 
power, delegated power.  So, flexibility has been g iven by using the word ‘may’ to the 
Executive.   
 Generally, the phraseology “the authority of the C entral Government to make 
rules and regulations” is working well.  In some ca ses, there might have been a lapse, 
otherwise, all the rules and regulations made under all the Acts are being implemented.   
 
18. The Committee, however, has some reservations in th e matter.  The Committee 
failed to understand how the framing or non-framing  of rules/regulations becomes a 
discretionary power of the Executive when there is express provision in the Act that the 
rules/regulations shall be framed.  In the Committe e’s view, unless the rules are framed, 
the provision of the Act cannot be implemented.  So , whenever a law is to be framed, the 
Ministry of Law & Justice, while vetting the Bills to be introduced in the House, must 
examine whether there is a necessity of making the rules or not.  Because once the 
provision is made, it has to be implemented through a process and the process is prescribed 
in the rules only. 
 
19. The Committee reasoned further that it is not a  question of playing up on the words ‘may’ 
or ‘shall’.  It is a legislative practice of Parlia ment that in all Statutes they used the word only 
‘may’.  But, what is important is that there will b e situations when the Ministry have to make the 
rules; and, there may be situations when only certa in circumstances manifest and Ministry will 
have a duty to make the rules.  Therefore, it is ei ther discretion or a mandate.  But the discretion 
becomes a mandate when certain circumstances precip itate.  This is the law prepared by the 
Supreme Court. Therefore, the Ministry would normally have to make the rules and cannot say it 
is its discretion.  But, if certain situations manifest, then this ‘may’ will get converted into ‘shall’.  
Then, Ministry will be bound by duty to make the rules.

available under Section 14D and 14E (Chapter IVA) o f the Act and in the Weapons of 
Mass Destruction and their Delivery Systems (Prohib ition of Unlawful Activities) Act,

for the purposes of another Act and how the Ministr y can claim that there is no need for 
framing of rules when the Act delegates power to th e Ministries/Departments to frame the 
rules. The Committee, therefore, recommends that th e Ministry of External Affairs, in 
consultation with other concerned Departments should expedite action in the matter.
